# Overview


This page gives a beginner-friendly map of the **terra-ligand-perturbation** repository: what scientific question it answers, how the seven pipeline steps fit together, what controls make the results trustworthy, and where to read next in this documentation. No prior knowledge of spatial transcriptomics or foundation models is assumed — each concept is introduced in plain terms before being used.

## What this repository does
This repository answers a specific biological question with a computational experiment: **if we remove the ligand *CSF1* from cancer-associated fibroblasts sitting near tumour macrophages, does the model's internal representation of those macrophages change — and is the change specific to CSF1?** It does this *in silico* (inside the computer, no wet-lab experiment) using the pretrained spatial transcriptomics foundation model **TERRA-112M**, applied to the public triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) Xenium cohort of Yan *et al.* The pipeline is version 0.1, packaged from the original analysis scripts, with TERRA used for zero-shot inference — meaning the model is applied as-is, without any additional training. It was developed with `terra-st` 0.1.13 at Hugging Face revision `00d1c977`, and TERRA's interface may change in later versions.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L3-L14), [CITATION.cff](/CITATION.cff#L3-L6)

For beginners, three terms recur throughout this documentation. A **foundation model** is a large neural network pretrained on massive data, here encoding a cell *together with its spatial neighbours* rather than in isolation. A **token** here is one gene inside the model's input: TERRA-112M represents each cell as 11 blocks of 256 gene tokens — the cell's own genes, then the genes of its 10 nearest neighbours, each listed in order of normalised expression. **In silico perturbation** means editing those tokens directly (removing the *CSF1* token) and observing how the model's output embedding changes, instead of running a real experiment.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L20-L28), [README.md](/README.md#L67-L71)

## The two guiding principles of the design
Two verifiable facts about TERRA motivated the pipeline's most important design decision. First, setting a gene's counts to zero and **re-tokenising** changes tokens of cells far beyond the intended target, because re-tokenisation re-normalises the edited cell. Second, TERRA's built-in `perturb_dataset` in `terra-st 0.1.13` edits neighbour blocks belonging to unlisted cells. The pipeline therefore **tokenises every patient exactly once** (step 04) and builds every perturbation by editing the saved baseline token sequences directly — only in the neighbour blocks that belong to a CSF1+ fibroblast. This is why the pipeline splits tokenisation (04) from editing (06) instead of re-running the model's own perturbation utility.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L65-L83)

> [!TIP]
> Every downstream condition is derived from the *same saved token sequences* produced by step 04. If you re-run tokenisation with different settings, cached knockout results from step 06 become invalid — this coupling is the single most important thing to understand before modifying the pipeline.

## Pipeline at a glance
The pipeline is a strict seven-step sequence, numbered by script prefix. It begins in **R** (exporting the data authors' per-patient objects into a language-neutral format) and continues in **Python** (assembly, quality filtering, tokenisation, perturbation, and statistics). Every step writes an `.xlsx` summary to `RESULTS_DIR/<step>/`, and large intermediates go to `WORK_DIR`. Steps 01, 02, 04 and 06 skip patients whose outputs already exist, and step 07 reuses cached per-donor predictions — so interrupted runs resume rather than restart. Steps 03 and 05 are quick and always recompute.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    X["Input: per-patient Xenium objects<br/>(distributed by the data authors)"] --> S01["01_export.R — R export<br/>shared gene panel, tissue pieces,<br/>checksummed binary counts"]
    S01 --> S02["02_build_h5ad.py<br/>one .h5ad per patient for TERRA"]
    S02 --> S03["03_sample_table.py<br/>pre-specified inclusion rules<br/>44 → 38 patients"]
    S03 --> S04["04_tokenise.py<br/>tokenise each patient ONCE<br/>cell + 10 neighbours × 256 tokens"]
    S04 --> S05["05_null_genes.py<br/>choose 20 rank-matched null genes"]
    S05 --> S06["06_ko_embed.py — GPU<br/>token-level knockouts<br/>+ TERRA-112M embeddings"]
    S06 --> S07["07_ko_pool.py<br/>leave-one-donor-out classifier<br/>+ cohort statistics"]
    CFG["config/analysis.cfg<br/>SOURCE_STATES · TARGET_STATES"] -.-> S03
    CFG -.-> S04
    CFG -.-> S07
    S07 --> O["Outputs: .xlsx summaries per step<br/>S07_summary.xlsx + S07_details.xlsx"]
```

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L160-L183), [README.md](/README.md#L187-L198)

The repository layout is deliberately flat: one numbered script per step, plus a shared R/`sh` launcher pair, and two example configuration files that you copy and edit before the first run. The `config/analysis.cfg` file (validated by `scripts/analysis_config.py`, which steps 03, 04 and 07 all import) defines which fibroblast states are the ligand **source** and which macrophage states are the **targets** — the pipeline is general in structure but parameterised by these cell-state labels.

| Step | Script | Language | Purpose | Main output |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 01 | `01_export.R` / `.sh` | R | Export per-patient matrices on the shared gene panel, defining tissue pieces | `<WORK_DIR>/export/` binary counts + manifest |
| 02 | `02_build_h5ad.py` | Python | Assemble one AnnData `.h5ad` per patient in TERRA's expected layout | `<WORK_DIR>/export/<P>/adata.h5ad` |
| 03 | `03_sample_table.py` | Python | Per-patient summary table and pre-specified inclusion rules | `03_sample_table.xlsx` |
| 04 | `04_tokenise.py` | Python | Harmonise and tokenise each included patient **once** | tokenised datasets + per-patient summary |
| 05 | `05_null_genes.py` | Python | Choose the 20 rank-matched null genes for the cohort | null-gene list + cohort table |
| 06 | `06_ko_embed.py` | Python (GPU) | Build token-level knockouts and embed target macrophages with TERRA-112M | `emb_ko.npz` per patient |
| 07 | `07_ko_pool.py` | Python | Pool embeddings, fit the classifier readout, compute cohort statistics | `S07_summary.xlsx` + `S07_details.xlsx` |

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L160-L183), [analysis_config.py](/scripts/analysis_config.py#L1-L35), [02_build_h5ad.py](/scripts/02_build_h5ad.py#L19-L26), [06_ko_embed.py](/scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L1-L9)

> [!TIP]
> The R→Python boundary in steps 01→02 is a checksummed binary handoff: step 01 writes raw sparse-matrix slots (`x`, `i`, `p` as int32) plus a manifest, and step 02 verifies shapes and checksums against that manifest before assembling the `.h5ad`. Corrupted or partially-written exports are therefore caught at step 02, not silently propagated.

Sources: [01_export.R](/scripts/01_export.R#L26-L43)

## The experimental conditions — how specificity is established
Every perturbation edit happens **only in the neighbour blocks belonging to CSF1+ fibroblasts** — the receiving macrophage's own block is never touched. The test condition `CSF1_remove` is never interpreted alone: it is compared against 20 **null genes** selected once for the cohort, whose presence and median rank in fibroblast token blocks match CSF1's within fixed bands (presence within 0.15, median rank within 40 positions), excluding CSF1 itself and ligands with known direct effects on macrophages. Three further controls — a positive control, an encoding check, and a negative control — close the loop. This layered design exists because *any* input change alters a model's output; the question is whether the CSF1 effect exceeds what comparable, non-specific edits produce.

| Condition | Edit in each CSF1+ fibroblast neighbour block | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `CSF1_remove` (test) | *CSF1* token and value removed; remaining tokens move up | The perturbation of interest |
| `NULL_<gene>` × 20 | Same removal, for a rank-matched null gene | Reference distribution for an edit of comparable size at the same positions |
| `POS_block` | Whole block emptied | Positive control — proves the pipeline can detect a neighbourhood change |
| `CSF1_zero` | *CSF1* value set to 0, token kept | Checks sensitivity to how a loss is encoded |
| `cell_emb` readout | (all conditions) | Negative control — a neighbour edit cannot change the cell's own embedding |

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L85-L97), [README.md](/README.md#L112-L128), [06_ko_embed.py](/scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L10-L25)

The **primary readout** is statistical rather than raw: a logistic regression trained on baseline embeddings of all macrophage states scores each cell's probability of being in a target state, fitted leave-one-donor-out so the model scoring a donor never saw that donor's cells; per cell, `dP = P(perturbed) − P(baseline)`. Two **descriptive magnitude readouts** accompany it — per-cell cosine shift and TERRA's own Wasserstein-2 distance per donor. A full walkthrough of the statistics belongs to the dedicated readout pages; here it suffices to know that step 07 produces both.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L99-L110), [07_ko_pool.py](/scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L20-L35)

## What you get out
Every step writes an unformatted `.xlsx` workbook; the analysis's endpoint is step 07, which produces `S07_summary.xlsx` (one table plus a sheet explaining every column) and `S07_details.xlsx` with per-sheet breakdowns: the cross-donor Wilcoxon test (overall and per depth batch), per-condition gene rankings, per-donor summaries, stratified results by number of edited neighbours and by target state, W2-distance comparisons against the null genes, per-donor held-out classifier AUC, and per-patient input quality checks. Every workbook carries the run's settings signature, so results are traceable to their exact configuration.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L140-L158)

## Running environment at a glance
This is a cluster-oriented pipeline, not a laptop notebook. It expects a Linux cluster with Sun Grid Engine (`qsub` job chaining via `-hold_jid`), Singularity or Apptainer containers, an NVIDIA GPU with at least 40 GB memory for the embedding step 06, and R (developed with 4.4.1) with `Matrix`, `igraph` and `openxlsx` for step 01. Before any job runs, you copy the two example configs (`paths.cfg` — five paths including input data, work and results directories; `analysis.cfg` — the source and target cell states), install the environment once via `env/install.sh` on an internet-connected node, and validate everything with `env/check_config.sh`. The full walkthrough is reserved for the Getting Started pages that follow.

| Requirement | Detail |
|---|---|
| Cluster scheduler | Sun Grid Engine, jobs chained with `-hold_jid` |
| Container runtime | Singularity or Apptainer |
| GPU | NVIDIA, ≥ 40 GB memory (step 06 only) |
| R | 4.4.1 with `Matrix`, `igraph`, `openxlsx` (step 01) |
| Configuration | `config/paths.cfg` (5 paths) + `config/analysis.cfg` (cell states) |
| Validation | `bash env/check_config.sh`, also inside a GPU session |

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L185-L222), [paths.cfg.example](/config/paths.cfg.example#L1-L24), [analysis.cfg.example](/config/analysis.cfg.example#L1-L12)

A few caveats frame every interpretation: a ligand is only visible to the model if it falls within a cell's 256 most-expressed genes; TERRA was not trained to predict perturbation responses, so a representation shift is not a predicted biological response; and the classifier readout depends on the data authors' cell-state annotations. These are expanded in the dedicated limitations page.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L130-L138)

# Quick Start



This page takes you from a fresh clone of `terra-ligand-perturbation` to a completed cohort analysis. It covers the four phases you must execute in order: **configure**, **install and verify**, **launch the seven-step job chain**, and **collect outputs**. Each phase is deliberately minimal — the reasoning behind the study design, the tokenisation strategy, and the statistics are treated in their dedicated Deep Dive pages. By the end of this page you will have submitted all seven pipeline stages and located the final result workbooks.

The pipeline performs an in silico knockout of the ligand *CSF1* in the spatial neighbourhood of tumour macrophages, using the pretrained TERRA foundation model on the public TNBC Xenium cohort, with rank-matched null-gene and positive controls to contextualise any observed effect.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L1-L9)

## Prerequisites

Before starting, confirm your environment satisfies every requirement below. The pipeline was developed for a specific cluster profile, and a missing item here is the most common cause of a failed first run.

| Requirement | Detail | Needed by |
|---|---|---|
| Scheduler | Linux cluster with Sun Grid Engine (job scripts submit via `qsub`) | All steps |
| Container runtime | Singularity or Apptainer | Steps 02–07 |
| GPU | NVIDIA card with **≥ 40 GB** memory | Step 06 only |
| Internet-connected node | For the one-off installation | Setup phase |
| R ≥ 4.4.1 | With packages `Matrix`, `igraph`, `openxlsx` | Step 01 only |

Note two asymmetries that trip up newcomers: the GPU is needed **only** for step 06 (embedding the perturbations), and R runs **only** in step 01 and must be visible to that job on the host — the rest of the pipeline executes Python inside the Singularity/Apptainer container. If your cluster uses different resource names than `tmem`, `h_vmem`, and `gpu`, adapt the `#$` directives at the top of each job script.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L187-L190), [README.md](/README.md#L220-L222), [01_export.sh](/scripts/01_export.sh#L2-L7)

## Phase 1 — Clone and Configure

Configuration is the only editing you do before running. Copy both example files into their live counterparts, then edit the copies — the `.example` files remain as documentation, and the live files are ignored by git.

```bash
git clone <this repository> && cd terra-ligand-perturbation
cp config/paths.cfg.example config/paths.cfg       # edit the five paths
cp config/analysis.cfg.example config/analysis.cfg # set the cell states
mkdir -p logs
```

`paths.cfg` has exactly five keys, all of which must be **absolute paths** on your system:

| Key | What it points to | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `INPUT_DIR` | Per-patient Xenium folders as distributed by the dataset authors | Each patient folder contains `mat_counts.rds`, `df_meta.rds`, `spatial_xy.rds` |
| `WORK_DIR` | Large intermediates: exported matrices, `.h5ad` files, tokenised datasets, embeddings, caches | Expect **several hundred GB** for the full cohort |
| `RESULTS_DIR` | The `.xlsx` summary workbooks written by each step | Small files only |
| `SOFTWARE_DIR` | Container image, Python packages, model weights, caches | Populated by `env/install.sh` |
| `BIND_PATHS` | Host paths mounted inside the container, comma-separated | Must cover this repository **and** every path above |

`analysis.cfg` defines which cell states the study reads out, replacing the placeholders with `cell_state` labels exactly as they appear in the dataset — comma-separated, no quotes, comments on their own lines:

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `SOURCE_STATES` | Fibroblast states whose *CSF1+* cells are the ligand source |
| `TARGET_STATES` | Macrophage states whose model representation is measured |

> [!TIP]
> The `BIND_PATHS` entry is the least obvious requirement: because all Python steps run inside a container, anything the container must see — including the cloned repository itself — must appear in this comma-separated list. `env/check_config.sh` verifies this for you, so run it before submitting anything.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L192-L199), [paths.cfg.example](/config/paths.cfg.example#L8-L25), [analysis.cfg.example](/config/analysis.cfg.example#L7-L12)

## Phase 2 — Install and Verify

Two scripts do all environment work. Run the install **once**, on a node with internet access, because it downloads the container image, Python packages, and the TERRA-112M weights from Hugging Face. Then run the checker — importantly, run it **also inside a GPU session**, since part of the verification is GPU-specific.

```bash
bash env/install.sh      # once, on a node with internet
bash env/check_config.sh # also inside a GPU session
```

The checker validates your configuration, software, input data, and model in one pass. If it reports a problem, fix the offending `paths.cfg` or `analysis.cfg` entry and re-run — do not submit jobs against an unverified configuration. Behind the scenes, every job script sources `env/terra_env.sh`, which defines the container execution commands (`tx` for CPU jobs, `txg` for GPU jobs) used throughout the pipeline.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L196-L197), [04_tokenise.sh](/scripts/04_tokenise.sh#L17-L20), [06_ko_embed.sh](/scripts/06_ko_embed.sh#L23-L26)

## Phase 3 — Launch the Pipeline

All jobs are submitted from the repository root, and steps are chained with `-hold_jid` so that each starts only when its predecessor's job name completes. The first five steps form a single CPU chain:

```bash
qsub -o logs/ scripts/01_export.sh
qsub -o logs/ -hold_jid tlp_01_export      scripts/02_build_h5ad.sh
qsub -o logs/ -hold_jid tlp_02_build_h5ad  scripts/03_sample_table.sh
qsub -o logs/ -hold_jid tlp_03_sample_table scripts/04_tokenise.sh   # array, 38 tasks
qsub -o logs/ -hold_jid tlp_04_tokenise    scripts/05_null_genes.sh
```

Step 06 is the GPU-heavy stage and follows a **smoke-test-first** pattern: run exactly one patient, read its log, and only then submit the full array. Because completed patients are skipped, the array simply resumes past the patient you already did:

```bash
qsub -o logs/ -t 1-1 -v PATIENT=P12 scripts/06_ko_embed.sh   # one patient first
qsub -o logs/ scripts/06_ko_embed.sh                         # GPU array, rest of cohort
qsub -o logs/ -hold_jid tlp_06_ko_embed scripts/07_ko_pool.sh
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Phase 1+2<br/>configs, install.sh, check_config.sh"] --> B["01_export<br/>CPU · single · 64 GB · 6 h"]
    B --> C["02_build_h5ad<br/>CPU · single"]
    C --> D["03_sample_table<br/>CPU · quick · inclusion rules"]
    D --> E["04_tokenise<br/>CPU · array × 38 · one patient per task"]
    E --> F["05_null_genes<br/>CPU · quick · selects 20 null genes"]
    F --> G{"06 smoke test<br/>one patient on GPU"}
    G -- "log clean" --> H["06_ko_embed<br/>GPU · array × 38 · ≥ 40 GB card · max 8 concurrent"]
    G -- "log shows OOM" --> G2["Check card: 24 GB fails<br/>batch 256 needs ~21 GB + CUDA overhead"]
    G2 --> G
    H --> I["07_ko_pool<br/>CPU · single · 24 h"]
    I --> J["RESULTS_DIR/07/<br/>S07_summary.xlsx · S07_details.xlsx"]
```

The per-step resource profile is fixed in each job script's `#$` header; know it before you submit so your scheduler quotas are not surprised:

| Step | Execution model | Memory / time request | Special |
|---|---|---|---|
| 01_export | CPU, single job | 64 GB, 6 h | Runs R on the host |
| 04_tokenise | CPU, array of 38 tasks | 64 GB, 6 h each | One included patient per task |
| 06_ko_embed | GPU, array of 38 tasks | 32 GB RAM / 200 GB h_vmem, 3 h | `gpu=true`; throttled to 8 concurrent tasks |
| 07_ko_pool | CPU, single job | 32 GB, 24 h | Pools all patients, fits classifiers |

> [!TIP]
> The one-patient GPU test before the full array is not optional ceremony: step 06's embedding batch size is deliberately fixed at 256 (so every patient is embedded identically), which needs roughly 21 GB plus CUDA overhead and **fails on 24 GB cards**. Catching this on one patient costs minutes; discovering it in a 38-task array wastes quota and time.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L201-L218), [06_ko_embed.sh](/scripts/06_ko_embed.sh#L11-L17), [01_export.sh](/scripts/01_export.sh#L5-L7), [04_tokenise.sh](/scripts/04_tokenise.sh#L5-L8), [07_ko_pool.sh](/scripts/07_ko_pool.sh#L5-L8)

## Phase 4 — Monitor and Resume

The pipeline is designed so that **resubmission is safe**. Steps 01, 02, 04 and 06 skip any patient whose outputs already exist, and step 07 reuses cached per-donor predictions (`FORCE_REBUILD = False` at the top of each script). Only steps 03 and 05 are quick enough that they always recompute from scratch. Practically, this means a killed or timed-out job is repaired by resubmitting the same script — the completed patients are never redone.

| Step | On resubmission |
|---|---|
| 01, 02, 04, 06 | Skips patients whose outputs already exist |
| 03, 05 | Always recomputes (inherently quick) |
| 07 | Reuses cached per-donor predictions unless rebuilt |

Every step writes an unformatted `.xlsx` summary to `RESULTS_DIR/<step>/`, while large intermediates accumulate in `WORK_DIR`. The final step produces two workbooks: **S07_summary.xlsx**, a single table plus a sheet explaining every column, and **S07_details.xlsx**, with sheets for the Wilcoxon donor test, gene ranks, per-donor and per-condition summaries, W2 distances, classifier AUCs, and input QC. Interpreting those sheets is the subject of [Outputs and Result Interpretation](20-outputs-and-result-interpretation).

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L179-L183), [README.md](/README.md#L140-L160)

## Where to Go Next

This page gave you the operational path; the following pages fill in what you just executed. A natural progression:

- [Data and Model Requirements](3-data-and-model-requirements) — what must be inside `INPUT_DIR`, and which TERRA version the pipeline pins.
- [Configuration Setup](4-configuration-setup) — a deeper treatment of `paths.cfg` and `analysis.cfg` than the summary tables above.
- [Pipeline Architecture](5-pipeline-architecture) — what each of the seven steps actually computes, stage by stage.
- [Cluster Execution and Job Chaining](18-cluster-execution-and-job-chaining) — the `-hold_jid` mechanics, array jobs, and resource tuning behind Phase 3.
- [Outputs and Result Interpretation](20-outputs-and-result-interpretation) — how to read `S07_summary.xlsx` and `S07_details.xlsx` once Phase 4 completes.

# Data and Model Requirements



This page defines everything that must exist **before** you run the first pipeline step: the input dataset and its exact on-disk format, the cell-state labels you must configure, the pinned TERRA model bundle, and the hardware/software environment. Each requirement is traced to the script that checks it, so you can verify your setup with evidence rather than guesswork. If a requirement listed here is not met, the pipeline stops early with an explicit error — it never silently continues.

## Requirements at a Glance

The pipeline has four categories of requirements, and each is enforced automatically at a specific stage:

| Category | What you must provide | Where it is verified |
|---|---|---|
| Input dataset | Yan *et al.* TNBC Xenium per-patient folders with three `.rds` files each | Step 01 export, Step 02 assembly |
| Configuration | `config/paths.cfg` (5 absolute paths) and `config/analysis.cfg` (2 cell-state lists) | `analysis_config.py`, every step |
| Model | TERRA-112M bundle (`terra-st` 0.1.13, HF revision `00d1c977`) | Step 04 config checks |
| Hardware | SGE cluster, Apptainer/Singularity container, GPU ≥ 40 GB for step 06, R 4.4.1 for step 01 | Job scripts, runtime checks |

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L187-L190), [analysis_config.py](scripts/analysis_config.py#L1-L35), [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L170-L185), [06_ko_embed.sh](scripts/06_ko_embed.sh#L6-L14)

## Input Dataset Requirements

The expected input is the publicly released triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) Xenium cohort of Yan *et al.* (2026) — spatial transcriptomics data where each cell has a position and a gene-count profile. The per-patient Xenium objects are distributed by the dataset authors (code repository: `navinlabcode/tnbc-chemo`), and cell types and states are the authors' annotations, which the pipeline relies on and does not recompute.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L32-L37), [README.md](README.md#L50-L54)

The data must be laid out as **one folder per patient**, where `<PATIENT>` is the patient identifier (e.g. `P12`), each containing three R data files (`.rds` is R's serialised object format):

```
INPUT_DIR/
├── P01/
│   ├── mat_counts.rds    # genes × cells raw count matrix
│   ├── df_meta.rds       # one metadata row per cell
│   └── spatial_xy.rds    # x/y coordinates per cell
├── P02/
│   └── ...
└── P44/
    └── ...
```

Sources: [paths.cfg.example](config/paths.cfg.example#L8-L12), [01_export.R](scripts/01_export.R#L11-L22)

Each file has a precise contract, checked with hard assertions before anything is written:

| File | Required content | Validation performed |
|---|---|---|
| `mat_counts.rds` | Genes × cells matrix (sparse `dgCMatrix`), rownames = gene symbols, **raw integer counts** | Aborts if counts are non-integer; colnames must equal `df_meta` rownames |
| `df_meta.rds` | One row per cell, rownames = cell IDs; columns `cell_type`, `cell_state`, `Niche`, `paper_patient_id`, `nCount_Xenium`, `nFeature_Xenium` | Row count must match matrix columns |
| `spatial_xy.rds` | Columns `x`, `y` (finite, in micrometres), rownames = cell IDs | Must be identical to `df_meta` rownames, same row count |

Sources: [01_export.R](scripts/01_export.R#L120-L166), [02_build_h5ad.py](scripts/02_build_h5ad.py#L6-L17)

> [!TIP]
> The most common failure at this stage is **row-order misalignment**: the three `.rds` files must list cells in exactly the same order (`rownames(spatial_xy) == rownames(df_meta)` and `ncol(mat_counts) == nrow(df_meta)`). The pipeline deliberately aborts instead of guessing an alignment, because a silent misalignment would attach wrong coordinates and metadata to cells downstream.

## Quality Filters Applied Before the Model

You do not need to pre-filter your data — step 01 applies three fixed selection rules that mirror the original study and TERRA's own preprocessing:

| Filter | Rule | Parameter |
|---|---|---|
| Genes | Only the **intersection of all patients' gene panels** is kept, so every section shares one panel; *CSF1* must be present (checked again in step 03) | — |
| Tissue pieces | Cells are grouped into connected regions of 100 µm bins (≥ 5 cells/bin, rook connectivity); regions smaller than 10 bins are treated as debris and dropped, so spatial neighbourhoods never bridge separate pieces | `BIN_UM=100`, `MIN_CELLS_BIN=5`, `MIN_REGION_BINS=10` |
| Cells | Cells with ≥ 10 detected genes on the shared panel are kept — including **unannotated cells**, because they are real spatial neighbours; this threshold matches TERRA's pretraining QC | `MIN_GENES_CELL=10` |

Sources: [01_export.R](scripts/01_export.R#L11-L22), [01_export.R](scripts/01_export.R#L53-L66), [03_sample_table.py](scripts/03_sample_table.py#L77-L78)

Step 02 then re-assembles these exports into one `.h5ad` file (the HDF5 container format of the Python `AnnData` library that TERRA reads) per patient, validating every transfer against a checksum manifest: shapes, non-zero counts, gene indices, total counts, and per-cell gene counts must all agree between the R export and the Python read.

Sources: [02_build_h5ad.py](scripts/02_build_h5ad.py#L58-L75)

## Cohort Inclusion Requirements

From the 44 patients with Xenium data, step 03 applies three pre-specified inclusion rules. All must hold for a patient to enter the analysis, leaving **38 patients**:

| Rule | Threshold | Why it exists |
|---|---|---|
| Median sequencing depth (annotated cells) | ≥ 100 counts | Too-shallow sections cannot represent the ligand |
| CSF1+ fibroblasts (source cells) | ≥ 50 | Enough source cells to edit neighbour blocks |
| Target macrophages (receiving cells) | ≥ 50 | Enough receiving cells for a stable readout |

A "CSF1+ fibroblast" is a cell with `cell_type == "Fibro"`, a `cell_state` in your configured source states, and a raw *CSF1* count > 0; a "target macrophage" is a cell with `cell_type == "Mye"` and a `cell_state` in your configured target states. Patients are additionally tagged as a **depth batch** ("deep" vs "shallow") from their median depth, which later steps use for stratified statistics.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L50-L60), [03_sample_table.py](scripts/03_sample_table.py#L13-L23), [03_sample_table.py](scripts/03_sample_table.py#L46-L49)

Steps 04 and 06 additionally hard-fail unless **exactly 38 patients** pass (the six excluded patients — P10, P23, P71, P87, P89, P93 — are listed in the scripts with their exclusion reasons). This is a cohort-specific guard for reproducing the published analysis, not a general requirement of the method.

Sources: [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L54-L58), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L62-L64)

## Cell-Type and Gene Labels the Pipeline Expects

Two things are configurable, and three are currently hard-coded — knowing the difference is essential before substituting your own data:

| Setting | Value | Configurable? |
|---|---|---|
| Ligand | `CSF1` | No (hard-coded in steps 03–06) |
| Source cell type | `Fibro` | No (hard-coded) |
| Target cell type | `Mye` | No (hard-coded) |
| Source cell **states** | `SOURCE_STATES` in `config/analysis.cfg` | Yes |
| Target cell **states** | `TARGET_STATES` in `config/analysis.cfg` | Yes |

The two state lists must use the exact `cell_state` labels of the dataset authors' annotations, written as comma-separated values without quotes. `analysis_config.py` validates your file and refuses to run if the config is missing, either key is empty, or placeholder text like `<fibroblast_state_1>` is still present.

Sources: [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L13-L17), [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L61-L66), [analysis.cfg.example](config/analysis.cfg.example#L7-L11), [analysis_config.py](scripts/analysis_config.py#L18-L33)

> [!TIP]
> Only the state *labels* are configurable in version 0.1 — the ligand and the coarse cell types (`Fibro`, `Mye`) are hard-coded, so swapping in a different dataset or ligand requires editing the scripts. Generalising these is the explicitly planned roadmap item, so check the roadmap before investing effort in adapting the pipeline yourself.

## TERRA Model Requirements

The pipeline uses the pretrained spatial-transcriptomics foundation model **TERRA-112M** in zero-shot mode (no fine-tuning). Version pinning is strict because TERRA is under active development and its interface may change:

| Requirement | Value |
|---|---|
| Python package | `terra-st` 0.1.13 |
| Model | TERRA-112M |
| Hugging Face revision | `00d1c977` |
| Weights licence | CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial — check the model card) |

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L12-L14), [README.md](README.md#L38-L44), [README.md](README.md#L252-L254)

The weights are downloaded from Hugging Face by the installation script and are **not redistributed** with this repository. Once downloaded, the model folder (`MODEL_DIR`, set via `config/paths.cfg`) must contain a specific bundle, and step 04 verifies its structure against TERRA's expected input layout before doing any work:

| Bundle file | What it provides | What is checked |
|---|---|---|
| `model_config.yaml` | Data configuration | `tokenizer_type == "cell_graph"`, `model_input_size == 2816`, `n_neighs == 10`, `seq_len_cell == 256`, `seq_len_neighborhood == 2560` |
| `token_dictionary.pkl` | Maps gene symbols to token IDs | Loaded and used for all knockout edits |

The checked numbers encode TERRA's input format: each cell is represented as **11 blocks of 256 gene tokens** (2,816 values wide) — the cell's own genes, then its 10 nearest neighbours, nearest first, each listing genes in order of normalised expression. If your model bundle does not match this `11 × 256` layout, step 04 exits with *"Model config does not match the 11 x 256 cell_graph layout"*.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L62-L66), [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L170-L185)

Step 06 uses the same bundle for inference via `terra.inference.embed.embed_dataset`, requesting three embedding types per cell: `spatial_cell_emb` (primary readout), `neighborhood_emb` (secondary), and `cell_emb` (kept as a negative control).

Sources: [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L57-L69), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L195-L200)

> **Repository note:** the README lists `env/terra_env.sh`, `env/install.sh` and `env/check_config.sh` as the components that set paths, install dependencies and validate the setup — however, no `env/` directory is present in the current repository snapshot. If you clone the repository and these files are missing, treat them as a required prerequisite described in [Configuration Setup](4-configuration-setup) and [Quick Start](2-quick-start).

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L163-L168)

## Environment and Hardware Requirements

| Requirement | Details | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| Cluster scheduler | Sun Grid Engine (`qsub`); job arrays chain steps via `-hold_jid` | All steps |
| Container runtime | Singularity or Apptainer (Python steps run inside the TERRA container; `SOFTWARE_DIR` holds image + weights + caches) | Steps 02–07 |
| GPU | NVIDIA card with **≥ 40 GB memory**, step 06 only | Step 06 |
| CPU support | AVX instructions required (`require_avx` check) | Containerised steps |
| R | 4.4.1, running on the **host** (not container), with packages `Matrix`, `igraph`, `openxlsx` | Step 01 |
| Memory / time (step 01) | 64 GB, 6 h | Step 01 |
| Memory / time (step 06) | 32 GB requested, 200 GB `h_vmem`, 3 h | Step 06 |
| Disk | Several hundred GB for `WORK_DIR` (exports, h5ad files, tokenised datasets, embeddings, caches) | All steps |
| Network | One node with internet access for the installation | Setup only |

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L187-L190), [README.md](README.md#L220-L222), [01_export.sh](scripts/01_export.sh#L6-L10), [06_ko_embed.sh](scripts/06_ko_embed.sh#L6-L14), [paths.cfg.example](config/paths.cfg.example#L12-L24)

> [!TIP]
> The GPU threshold of 40 GB is not arbitrary: step 06 embeds all conditions with a **fixed batch size of 256**, which needs about 21 GB plus CUDA overhead and fails on 24 GB cards. The batch size is deliberately not configurable — identical batching across baseline and all perturbation conditions is what makes the embedding shifts comparable.

## How the Pipeline Verifies Your Setup

Each requirement is checked exactly once, at the earliest possible step, so failures surface with a specific message rather than as corrupted results downstream:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    RDS["Raw .rds files<br/>(3 per patient)"] -->|"01: alignment,<br/>integer counts,<br/>shared panel"| H5AD["adata.h5ad<br/>(1 per patient)"]
    H5AD -->|"02: manifest &<br/>shape checks"| INC["03: CSF1 on panel,<br/>inclusion thresholds<br/>(must leave 38 patients)"]
    INC --> TOK["04: model_config.yaml ==<br/>cell_graph 11 x 256,<br/>token_dictionary.pkl"]
    TOK -->|"tokens + meta.npz"| GPU["06: layout checks,<br/>GPU embedding<br/>(≥ 40 GB card)"]
    CFG2["config/analysis.cfg"] -.->|"validated by<br/>analysis_config.py"| INC
    CFG1["config/paths.cfg"] -.->|"5 absolute paths,<br/>exported as env vars"| RDS
    MODEL["MODEL_DIR bundle"] -.-> TOK
```

Two design properties are worth noticing as a beginner: every step is **idempotent** (it skips patients whose outputs already exist unless `FORCE_REBUILD` is set), and every check result is recorded into the per-step `.xlsx` summary, so you can audit what was verified after the fact.

Sources: [01_export.R](scripts/01_export.R#L58-L66), [02_build_h5ad.py](scripts/02_build_h5ad.py#L30-L75), [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L170-L185), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L195-L200), [README.md](README.md#L179-L183)

## Where to Go Next

Once you have confirmed your data, model, and hardware match the requirements above, the logical reading order is:

1. **[Configuration Setup](4-configuration-setup)** — fill in the five paths in `config/paths.cfg` and the two state lists in `config/analysis.cfg` (the exact files introduced in the sections above).
2. **[Quick Start](2-quick-start)** — submit the job chain and run your first patient end-to-end.
3. **[Pipeline Architecture](5-pipeline-architecture)** — understand how the seven steps connect and what each writes.
4. For deeper background on the requirements introduced here, see **[Patient Inclusion Rules](8-patient-inclusion-rules)** for the statistical reasoning behind the 38-patient cohort, and **[Harmonisation and Model Bundles](10-harmonisation-and-model-bundles)** for what happens to your data inside the TERRA container.


# Configuration Setup



Every value that makes this pipeline *yours* lives in exactly two files. This page walks you through creating, editing, and validating them before any pipeline step is submitted: `config/paths.cfg` tells the pipeline where your data, scratch space, results, and software live, and `config/analysis.cfg` tells it which cell states to analyse. Both are created by copying a tracked `.example` template — the real files are machine-specific and git-ignored, so your edits never touch the repository. The workflow is: copy → edit → validate.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L192-L199), [analysis.cfg.example](config/analysis.cfg.example#L1-L6)

## What You Are Configuring

The repository ships only templates; nothing under `config/` is ever read directly by the pipeline until you create the non-example versions. The two files are deliberately separated by *concern*: one answers "where is everything on my system", the other answers "which biological populations does this study compare". Keeping them apart means you can switch datasets or study designs without touching filesystem layout, and vice versa.

| | `config/paths.cfg` | `config/analysis.cfg` |
|---|---|---|
| Template | `paths.cfg.example` | `analysis.cfg.example` |
| Controls | Five absolute filesystem paths | Two cell-state selections |
| Format | `KEY=value`, one per line | `KEY=state1,state2`, comma-separated |
| Read by | `env/terra_env.sh`, which exports them as environment variables | `scripts/analysis_config.py`, imported by steps 03, 04, 07 |
| Validation | `bash env/check_config.sh` | Built-in guards in `load_states()` |

Sources: [paths.cfg.example](config/paths.cfg.example#L1-L6), [analysis.cfg.example](config/analysis.cfg.example#L1-L12), [analysis_config.py](scripts/analysis_config.py#L13-L34), [README.md](README.md#L163-L177)

The relevant slice of the repository, annotated for this page:

```
config/
├── analysis.cfg.example   # template → copy to config/analysis.cfg
└── paths.cfg.example      # template → copy to config/paths.cfg
scripts/
├── 01_export.R|.sh        # step 01: reads $REPO_DIR from the env layer
├── 02_build_h5ad.py|.sh   # step 02: reads WORK_DIR from environment
├── 03_sample_table.py|.sh # step 03: reads paths AND analysis.cfg
├── 04_tokenise.py|.sh     # step 04: reads paths AND analysis.cfg
├── 05_null_genes.py|.sh   # step 05: paths only
├── 06_ko_embed.py|.sh     # step 06: paths only
├── 07_ko_pool.py|.sh      # step 07: reads paths AND analysis.cfg
└── analysis_config.py     # loader + validator for config/analysis.cfg
```

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L163-L177), [analysis.cfg.example](config/analysis.cfg.example#L1)

## The Configuration Flow

Understanding *how* values travel prevents the most common beginner mistake: editing a config file and wondering why nothing changed. Job scripts do not read `config/paths.cfg` themselves — every `.sh` file begins by sourcing `env/terra_env.sh` (for example, `01_export.sh` does so immediately after enabling strict error mode), which turns the configured paths into environment variables that the Python and R programs then read via `os.environ`. The cell states take a different route: steps 03, 04, and 07 import `load_states()` from `scripts/analysis_config.py`, which parses `config/analysis.cfg` directly.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph T["Tracked templates"]
        PCE["config/paths.cfg.example"]
        ACE["config/analysis.cfg.example"]
    end
    subgraph Y["Your files, git-ignored"]
        PC["config/paths.cfg"]
        AC["config/analysis.cfg"]
    end
    PCE -- "cp + edit" --> PC
    ACE -- "cp + edit" --> AC
    PC -- "sourced and exported" --> ENV["env/terra_env.sh"]
    ENV -- "environment variables" --> JOBS["scripts/*.sh - qsub jobs"]
    JOBS -- "os.environ reads" --> PY["steps 01-07"]
    AC -- "parsed at import" --> LOADER["scripts/analysis_config.py load_states"]
    LOADER -- "SOURCE_STATES, TARGET_STATES" --> PY3["step 03"]
    LOADER --> PY4["step 04"]
    LOADER --> PY7["step 07"]
```

Sources: [01_export.sh](scripts/01_export.sh#L15-L18), [03_sample_table.py](scripts/03_sample_table.py#L44-L48), [analysis_config.py](scripts/analysis_config.py#L13-L13)

> [!TIP]
> The five keys in `paths.cfg` are never read directly by a pipeline step. They reach the code as environment variables exported by `env/terra_env.sh` — every job script sources it first — and Python steps read them with `os.environ` (`WORK_DIR`, `RESULTS_DIR`, and additionally `MODEL_DIR`, which `04_tokenise.py` notes is "set by terra_env.sh"). This is why the pipeline must always be launched through the `.sh` job scripts from the repository root, not by running the `.py` files alone.

Sources: [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L56-L59), [06_ko_embed.sh](scripts/06_ko_embed.sh#L21-L26)

## Step 1 — Create `config/paths.cfg`

Start from the repository root with the copy command from the README:

```bash
cp config/paths.cfg.example config/paths.cfg       # edit the five paths
```

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L192-L195)

Then replace every placeholder with an **absolute path on your system** — the template states this requirement explicitly, and the checker described below enforces it. Each key has a precise role in the pipeline's data flow:

| Key | Points to | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| `INPUT_DIR` | Per-patient Xenium folders as distributed by the dataset authors (`<PATIENT>/{mat_counts.rds, df_meta.rds, spatial_xy.rds}`) | The only read-only source of raw data; step 01 exports from here |
| `WORK_DIR` | Large intermediates: exported matrices, `.h5ad` files, tokenised datasets, embeddings, caches | Expect **several hundred GB** for the full cohort — plan quota accordingly |
| `RESULTS_DIR` | Summary workbooks (`.xlsx`) written by each step | Small; each step appends a subdirectory here |
| `SOFTWARE_DIR` | Container image, installed Python packages, model weights, caches | Populated by the one-off `env/install.sh` |
| `BIND_PATHS` | Host paths mounted inside the container, comma-separated | Must together contain this repository *and* every path above |

Sources: [paths.cfg.example](config/paths.cfg.example#L8-L25)

Two details deserve attention. First, `BIND_PATHS` is a container concern: since jobs run inside a Singularity/Apptainer image, the host directories must be mounted in, and the template notes that `check_config.sh` verifies the repository and all configured paths are covered by the bind mounts. Second, `INPUT_DIR` layout is not arbitrary — step 01 expects the exact per-patient folder structure produced by the dataset authors, with the three `.rds` files shown above.

Sources: [paths.cfg.example](config/paths.cfg.example#L22-L25), [README.md](README.md#L187-L190)

## Step 2 — Create `config/analysis.cfg`

This file defines the biological contrast of the study: which fibroblast states supply the CSF1 ligand, and which macrophage states receive it. The README's design section confirms that source and target states are the dataset's own cell-state labels and are set here.

```bash
cp config/analysis.cfg.example config/analysis.cfg # set the cell states
```

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L192-L195), [README.md](README.md#L59-L60)

| Key | Meaning | Constraint |
|---|---|---|
| `SOURCE_STATES` | Fibroblast states whose CSF1+ cells are the ligand source | One or more labels, comma-separated |
| `TARGET_STATES` | Macrophage states whose model representation is read out | One or more labels, comma-separated, **no duplicates** |

Sources: [analysis.cfg.example](config/analysis.cfg.example#L7-L12), [analysis_config.py](scripts/analysis_config.py#L27-L33)

The template documents the formatting rules inline: labels are comma-separated, **no quotes**, and comments must sit on their own lines (any line starting with `#` is skipped by the parser). Copy, then edit:

| Before (template placeholder) | After (illustrative syntax — use your dataset's state labels) |
|---|---|
| `SOURCE_STATES=<fibroblast_state_1>,<fibroblast_state_2>` | `SOURCE_STATES=state_A,state_B` |
| `TARGET_STATES=<macrophage_state_1>,<macrophage_state_2>` | `TARGET_STATES=state_X,state_Y` |

Sources: [analysis.cfg.example](config/analysis.cfg.example#L8-L11)

The illustrative labels above are syntax only: the valid values are the cell-state annotations of the Yan *et al.* TNBC Xenium cohort, documented on the [Data and Model Requirements](3-data-and-model-requirements) page. The angle brackets are not decorative — the loader treats any surviving value that starts with `<` as an unedited placeholder and refuses to run, so removing them is itself part of the validation.

Sources: [analysis_config.py](scripts/analysis_config.py#L30-L31), [README.md](README.md#L36-L37)

## Step 3 — Validate Before Running

Validation happens on two independent fronts, and both fail loudly rather than silently. For `paths.cfg`, run the checker the template points to — the README describes it as checking "configuration, software, input, model", which makes it the single command that certifies your setup end-to-end (run it once normally, and again inside a GPU session):

```bash
bash env/install.sh        # once, on a node with internet access
bash env/check_config.sh   # also inside a GPU session
```

Sources: [paths.cfg.example](config/paths.cfg.example#L4-L6), [README.md](README.md#L166-L168), [README.md](README.md#L196-L197)

For `analysis.cfg`, validation is built into the loader itself. `load_states()` in `scripts/analysis_config.py` raises a `SystemExit` with a targeted message the moment anything is wrong, which means a mis-configured step 03/04/07 aborts at startup instead of producing empty results. The four guards and their fixes:

| Error message (from `load_states()`) | Trigger | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `... not found; copy config/analysis.cfg.example to config/analysis.cfg ...` | The real config file does not exist | Run the `cp` command from Step 2 |
| `SOURCE_STATES is not set in ...` / `TARGET_STATES is not set in ...` | Key missing, or value empty | Fill in both keys — one is not optional without the other |
| `... still holds placeholders` | Any value still starts with `<` | Replace every `<...>` label with a real dataset state |
| `TARGET_STATES lists a state more than once` | Duplicate label in the target list | Remove the duplicate |

Sources: [analysis_config.py](scripts/analysis_config.py#L18-L33)

> [!TIP]
> One prerequisite check the checker cannot do for you: the job scripts and config templates depend on an `env/` directory (`terra_env.sh`, `install.sh`, `check_config.sh`, `versions/`) that the README lists in its repository layout, but which is **not present in the packaged repository tree** shown here (only `config/` and `scripts/` exist). Since every job script starts with `set -euo pipefail` and then `source env/terra_env.sh`, a missing `env/` will abort the job on its first line — confirm you have this directory before submitting anything.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L163-L177), [01_export.sh](scripts/01_export.sh#L15-L16)

## Where Each Setting Is Used

With both files validated, it helps to see the consumption map at a glance — it tells you which config to revisit if a particular step misbehaves, and it explains why steps 03/04/07 will refuse to start on a bad `analysis.cfg` while steps 02, 05, 06 will happily run without it:

| Step | Paths via `env/terra_env.sh` | Cell states via `analysis_config.py` |
|---|---|---|
| 01 export (R) | `REPO_DIR` used to locate the R script | — |
| 02 build_h5ad | `WORK_DIR` → export directory | — |
| 03 sample_table | `WORK_DIR`, `RESULTS_DIR` | `load_states()` imported at startup |
| 04 tokenise | `WORK_DIR`, `RESULTS_DIR`, `MODEL_DIR` | source/target states for cell classification |
| 05 null_genes | paths only | — |
| 06 ko_embed | paths only (GPU embedding) | — |
| 07 ko_pool | paths only | target states define the classifier readout |

Sources: [01_export.sh](scripts/01_export.sh#L18-L18), [02_build_h5ad.py](scripts/02_build_h5ad.py#L37-L38), [03_sample_table.py](scripts/03_sample_table.py#L44-L48), [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L14-L17), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L26-L28), [analysis.cfg.example](config/analysis.cfg.example#L1)

## From Clone to Ready — Full Checklist

The complete setup sequence, exactly as the README prescribes it, fits in one flowchart. Every arrow is a command you run; the loop back through `check_config.sh` is deliberate — configuration errors are cheap to fix now and expensive to discover mid-pipeline:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[git clone the repository] --> B[cp paths.cfg.example to paths.cfg]
    A --> C[cp analysis.cfg.example to analysis.cfg]
    B --> D[Fill five absolute paths and BIND_PATHS]
    C --> E[Replace angle-bracket placeholders with real state labels]
    D --> F[bash env/install.sh - once, on a node with internet]
    E --> F
    F --> G[bash env/check_config.sh - also in a GPU session]
    G --> H{All checks pass}
    H -- No --> I[Correct paths.cfg or analysis.cfg]
    I --> G
    H -- Yes --> J[mkdir -p logs - ready to submit jobs]
```

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L192-L199)

Three habits make this setup durable. Re-run `check_config.sh` inside every new GPU session type, since bind-mount visibility can differ between nodes; treat `analysis.cfg` as your study definition — changing `TARGET_STATES` changes the classifier readout of step 07, and the pipeline's caching behaviour around reruns is covered in [Reproducibility and Caching](19-reproducibility-and-caching); and never commit your `.cfg` files, which the git-ignore design makes the default anyway.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L196-L197), [README.md](README.md#L179-L183), [analysis.cfg.example](config/analysis.cfg.example#L3-L4)

## Where to Go Next

Configuration is the last stop before execution. If you have not yet confirmed your input data and TERRA model versions, read [Data and Model Requirements](3-data-and-model-requirements) alongside this page — the `INPUT_DIR` layout and `SOFTWARE_DIR` contents it describes are exactly what `paths.cfg` must point at. To understand why the pipeline is structured as seven chained steps, continue to [Pipeline Architecture](5-pipeline-architecture); for how the configured steps are actually submitted and chained on a Sun Grid Engine cluster — including the `qsub -hold_jid` sequence that assumes this page's setup is complete — see [Cluster Execution and Job Chaining](18-cluster-execution-and-job-chaining).


# Pipeline Architecture



This page explains how the terra-ligand-perturbation repository is organised as an executable system: what the seven numbered stages are, the data contracts between them, how compute is orchestrated on a cluster, and which conventions hold across every stage. It is deliberately architectural — the biological rationale of each design decision is documented in the linked Deep Dive pages at the end.

## The Seven-Stage DAG

The repository implements a single linear directed acyclic graph of seven stages. Each stage pairs a compute script (`.R` or `.py`) with a Sun Grid Engine wrapper (`.sh`), and each stage writes large intermediates to `WORK_DIR` and a human-readable `.xlsx` summary to `RESULTS_DIR/<step>/`. The stage numbers are not cosmetic — they encode execution order, and downstream stages assert that upstream artifacts exist before proceeding.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L160-L183), [01_export.R](scripts/01_export.R#L1-L44)

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Stage 01 · 01_export.R<br/>raw Xenium RDS to CSC binaries + manifest"]
    B["Stage 02 · 02_build_h5ad.py<br/>one AnnData per patient"]
    C["Stage 03 · 03_sample_table.py<br/>inclusion gate: 44 to 38 patients"]
    D["Stage 04 · 04_tokenise.py<br/>tokenise once: tokens + meta.npz + cf_blocks.npz"]
    E["Stage 05 · 05_null_genes.py<br/>20 rank-matched null genes to TSV"]
    F["Stage 06 · 06_ko_embed.py<br/>23 token-level conditions to emb_ko.npz"]
    G["Stage 07 · 07_ko_pool.py<br/>classifier + statistics to two xlsx workbooks"]
    A --> B --> C --> D
    D --> E
    D --> F
    E --> F
    F --> G
```

The full stage inventory, with compute tier and execution mode:

| Stage | Script pair | Role | Compute tier | Execution mode |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 01 | `01_export.R` + `.sh` | Export raw Xenium matrices | R on host, CPU | single job |
| 02 | `02_build_h5ad.py` + `.sh` | Assemble one `.h5ad` per patient | TERRA container, CPU | single job |
| 03 | `03_sample_table.py` + `.sh` | Patient table + pre-specified inclusion | TERRA container, CPU | single job |
| 04 | `04_tokenise.py` + `.sh` | Harmonise + tokenise each patient once | TERRA container, CPU | array job, 38 tasks |
| 05 | `05_null_genes.py` + `.sh` | Select the 20 rank-matched null genes | TERRA container, CPU | single job |
| 06 | `06_ko_embed.py` + `.sh` | Build perturbations, embed with TERRA-112M | TERRA container, GPU ≥ 40 GB | array job, 38 tasks, throttled |
| 07 | `07_ko_pool.py` + `.sh` | Cohort pooling, classifier, statistics | TERRA container, CPU | single job |

Sources: [04_tokenise.sh](scripts/04_tokenise.sh#L1-L21), [06_ko_embed.sh](scripts/06_ko_embed.sh#L1-L27), [03_sample_table.py](scripts/03_sample_table.py#L34), [05_null_genes.py](scripts/05_null_genes.py#L36), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L79)

## Stage Contracts: Reads/Writes at Every Boundary

Every script opens with a docstring that declares its exact `Reads` and `Writes` paths, and every stage boundary is protected by validation rather than convention. The `01 → 02` handoff uses a binary-plus-manifest scheme with checksums; the `04 → 06` handoff is a tokenised dataset plus NumPy archives; the `05 → 06` handoff is a single TSV; the `06 → 07` handoff is one `.npz` per patient whose keys are documented in the consumer's docstring. This is the load-bearing pattern of the codebase: no stage parses another stage's logic, only its declared artifacts.

Sources: [01_export.R](scripts/01_export.R#L25-L30), [02_build_h5ad.py](scripts/02_build_h5ad.py#L19-L23), [05_null_genes.py](scripts/05_null_genes.py#L28-L33), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L41-L45), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L12-L25)

## Stages 01–02: The R-to-Python Bridge

Stage 01 is the only R code in the repository, and it is designed to be the *last* thing R touches. It reads the vendor-distributed per-patient `.rds` files, applies the selection rules — the gene panel intersection across all sections, tissue pieces defined as connected regions of occupied 100 µm bins (rook connectivity, ≥ 5 cells per bin, < 10 bins = debris), and cells with ≥ 10 detected genes — and then writes the counts as the raw slots of an R `dgCMatrix` in little-endian int32: `x.bin` (values), `i.bin` (0-based gene indices), `p.bin` (column pointers). Crucially, it also writes a `manifest.txt` with shapes, nnz, and total counts, which becomes the verification instrument for the next stage.

Sources: [01_export.R](scripts/01_export.R#L11-L44)

Stage 02 runs inside the TERRA container and rebuilds the exact sparse matrix with `numpy.fromfile`, asserting every manifest invariant before assembly: nnz match, column-pointer structure, strictly positive counts, gene indices in range, and total-count equality. It then writes one AnnData per patient in the layout TERRA expects. One architectural decision here matters downstream: `obs_names` are set to `"<patient>_<cell_id>"` because Xenium cell IDs repeat across patients and TERRA's perturbation machinery selects cells by ID — IDs must therefore be unique across the entire cohort, with the original ID preserved in `obs['cell_id']`.

Sources: [02_build_h5ad.py](scripts/02_build_h5ad.py#L68-L80), [02_build_h5ad.py](scripts/02_build_h5ad.py#L13-L26)

> [!TIP]
> The manifest-with-checksums bridge means R and Python never share memory, serialisation libraries, or file formats — only a byte-exact contract. If you ever change the export format in `01_export.R`, the assertions at [02_build_h5ad.py](scripts/02_build_h5ad.py#L73-L80) are the contract's enforcement points; they will fail loudly rather than produce a silently misaligned matrix.

## Stages 03–05: Cohort Gate and the Tokenise-Once Foundation

Stage 03 reads every `.h5ad` from stage 02 and applies three pre-specified inclusion rules — median depth ≥ 100 counts, ≥ 50 CSF1⁺ fibroblasts, ≥ 50 target macrophages — reducing the 44 exported patients to **38 included patients**. These inclusion thresholds live in stage 03; a *separate* threshold (`DEEP_DEPTH = 500`) defined in stage 04 assigns each patient a `depth_batch` label ("deep"/"shallow") that is carried through the artifacts and used by stage 07. Stage 03's output also serves a human purpose: it identifies the smallest passing patient for the recommended one-patient GPU smoke test of stage 06.

Sources: [03_sample_table.py](scripts/03_sample_table.py#L20-L31), [03_sample_table.py](scripts/03_sample_table.py#L51-L54), [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L18-L20), [README.md](README.md#L50-L63)

The resulting exclusion set (`P10, P23, P71, P87, P89, P93`) is then pinned as a hard guard in stages 04–07: each downstream script asserts `N_INCLUDED == 38` and exits if the cohort differs. This converts the cohort definition from data into an invariant — the pipeline refuses to run over an unexpected cohort rather than silently including patients.

Sources: [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L60-L66), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L98-L104), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L96)

Stage 04 is the pivot of the whole architecture. For each included patient, it runs `harmonize_adata` once and `tokenize_adata` once per tissue piece, producing TERRA's `cell_graph` layout: 11 blocks × 256 tokens (the cell itself, then its 10 nearest neighbours, nearest first — widths `W=2816, L_CELL=256, N_SEG=11`). Its three artifacts define everything downstream: the tokenised Hugging Face dataset (`tokens/`), per-row annotations and neighbour indices (`meta.npz`), and — the key one — the own 256-token block of every CSF1⁺ fibroblast (`cf_blocks.npz`), which is the raw material for null-gene selection.

Sources: [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L22-L47), [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L74)

Stage 05 consumes `cf_blocks.npz` across all 38 patients and selects the 20 null genes under rules fixed before results are seen: a candidate must lie within ± 0.15 presence and ± 40 rank positions of CSF1 in the fibroblast token blocks, must not be CSF1 itself, and must not appear in a hard-coded list of 50 ligands with established direct effects on macrophages. Twenty genes are drawn with seed 1234, and the script refuses to widen the bands if fewer than 20 candidates exist. Its single output consumed downstream is `05_null_genes.tsv`.

Sources: [05_null_genes.py](scripts/05_null_genes.py#L12-L33), [05_null_genes.py](scripts/05_null_genes.py#L52-L63)

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Once["tokenise once - stage 04, per patient"]
        T["tokens/<br/>11 x 256 token blocks"]
        M["meta.npz<br/>row annotations, neighbour index"]
        CF["cf_blocks.npz<br/>own block of each CSF1+ fib"]
    end
    N["stage 05<br/>rank-matched null selection"] 
    K["stage 06<br/>token-level edits<br/>23 conditions"]
    E["TERRA-112M embed"]
    NPZ["emb_ko.npz"]
    T --> K
    M --> K
    CF --> N
    N -->|"05_null_genes.tsv"| K
    K --> E --> NPZ
```

> [!TIP]
> The "tokenise once, edit many" design is a deliberate workaround for two observed behaviours of the model stack: re-tokenising after zeroing a gene count reshuffles tied genes across the whole sequence, and `terra-st 0.1.13`'s `perturb_dataset` with `perturbation_target="neighborhood"` edits blocks belonging to cells outside the requested list. By editing tokens directly and restricting edits to CSF1⁺ fibroblast neighbour blocks, stage 06 guarantees the perturbation is spatially exact. The full motivation is on [Token-Level Knockout Editing](11-token-level-knockout-editing).

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L65-L83)

## Stage 06: The Token-Level Perturbation Engine

Stage 06 is the compute heart of the pipeline: one GPU array task per patient, it builds every knockout condition at token level from the stage-04 baseline sequences (no re-tokenisation) and embeds the results with TERRA-112M. The edit scope is strictly defined: only neighbour blocks 1–10 belonging to a CSF1⁺ fibroblast are touched; the macrophage's own block and all other neighbours are never modified. A target cell counts as edited by a condition when at least one of its CSF1⁺ fibroblast neighbour blocks contains the relevant gene, with `n_edit` recording how many blocks.

Sources: [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L7-L26)

The 23 conditions form a controlled experiment matrix built into the batch:

| Condition | Token edit in each CSF1⁺ fibroblast neighbour block | Count | Architectural role |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CSF1_remove` | token and value removed; remaining tokens shift up, padding at end | 1 | the test perturbation |
| `CSF1_zero` | value set to 0, token kept | 1 | encoding-sensitivity control |
| `POS_block` | entire block emptied | 1 | positive control |
| `NULL_<gene>` | identical edit to `CSF1_remove` | 20 | rank-matched reference distribution |

Sources: [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L12-L24), [README.md](README.md#L85-L91)

Embedding scope is equally explicit: the baseline is embedded for *all* myeloid cells of the patient (this becomes stage 07's classifier training set), while baseline-plus-all-conditions are embedded for the target macrophages — always the same rows in the same order, so batching is identical across conditions. Three embedding types are captured per cell: `spatial_cell_emb` (primary readout), `neighborhood_emb` (secondary), and `cell_emb`, retained as a built-in negative control.

Sources: [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L28-L34), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L70-L71)

> [!TIP]
> Stage 06 treats verification as a first-class output: after embedding, it checks that each condition changed exactly the cells with `n_edit > 0` and nothing outside the edited blocks, that edited blocks keep their padding at the end, that `cell_emb` deviates by less than 1e-4 (a neighbourhood edit cannot change the cell's own embedding), and that each condition yields one embedding row per sequence. Any failed check is written to the per-patient xlsx *and* forces a non-zero exit — corrupt embeddings can never silently flow into stage 07's statistics.

Sources: [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L36-L39), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L317), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L353-L357)

## Stage 07: Cohort Pooling and Statistical Readout

Stage 07 is the only consumer of `emb_ko.npz`, and its docstring documents the archive's full key contract — the definitive schema for the `06 → 07` handoff:

| Key group | Content |
|---|---|
| `patient`, `depth_batch` | scalars per patient |
| `mye_cell_id`, `mye_state` | all myeloid cells (`n_mye`) |
| `base_mye_spatial`, `base_mye_neigh`, `base_mye_cell` | `n_mye × D` baseline embeddings |
| `t_in_mye` | target rows within the mye arrays |
| `t_cell_id`, `t_state`, `n_cf_nb` | target macrophages (`n_t`) |
| `base_t_spatial`, `base_t_neigh` | `n_t × D` baseline embeddings |
| `cond_names` | `CSF1_remove`, `CSF1_zero`, `POS_block`, 20 × `NULL_<gene>` |
| `n_edit` | `n_t × n_cond`, edited neighbour counts |
| `cond_spatial`, `cond_neigh` | `n_cond × n_t × D` condition embeddings |

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L12-L25)

Functionally, stage 07 scores every target macrophage with a leave-one-donor-out logistic classifier trained on baseline embeddings of all annotated macrophage states (the source/target states come from the shared configuration module, not from hard-coded labels), computes per-cell `dP = P(perturbed) − P(baseline)` and cosine shifts, computes TERRA's Wasserstein-2 distance as a descriptive magnitude, and produces the cohort statistics: per-donor effect sizes against the null median, a two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test across eligible donors (overall and per depth batch), and cohort-wide gene ranks. The statistical interpretation belongs to [Embedding Shift Magnitudes](16-embedding-shift-magnitudes) and [Cohort Summary Statistics](17-cohort-summary-statistics); architecturally, note that stage 07 caches per-donor predictions in `WORK_DIR/ko_pool_cache/<P>.npz` and reuses them when the donor list and classifier settings are unchanged.

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L26-L68), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L69-L75)

## Orchestration Topology

All stages are submitted from the repository root as SGE jobs that source `env/terra_env.sh` for paths and container settings, and the chain is expressed through `-hold_jid` dependencies rather than a monolithic workflow engine — each job starts only when its predecessor's job name has completed. Stages 04 and 06 are array jobs with `-t 1-38`; the task index selects the patient deterministically from the sorted list of the 38 included patients, with a `PATIENT=<id>` environment override for running a single patient first. Stage 06 additionally throttles concurrency with `-tc 8` and requests `gpu=true`.

Sources: [01_export.sh](scripts/01_export.sh#L8-L11), [02_build_h5ad.sh](scripts/02_build_h5ad.sh#L9), [04_tokenise.sh](scripts/04_tokenise.sh#L7-L20), [06_ko_embed.sh](scripts/06_ko_embed.sh#L1-L15), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L107-L110), [README.md](README.md#L200-L218)

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    J1["tlp_01_export"] -.->|"hold_jid"| J2["tlp_02_build_h5ad"]
    J2 -.->|"hold_jid"| J3["tlp_03_sample_table"]
    J3 -.->|"hold_jid"| J4["tlp_04_tokenise<br/>array 1-38, CPU"]
    J4 -.->|"hold_jid"| J5["tlp_05_null_genes"]
    J5 -.->|"hold_jid"| J6["tlp_06_ko_embed<br/>GPU array 1-38, tc 8"]
    J6 -.->|"hold_jid"| J7["tlp_07_ko_pool"]
```

The verified resource profiles from the job headers:

| Job | Memory (`tmem`/`h_vmem`) | Walltime | GPU | Concurrency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tlp_01_export` | 64G / 64G | 06:00:00 | — | single |
| `tlp_02_build_h5ad` | 64G / 64G | 06:00:00 | — | single |
| `tlp_04_tokenise` | 64G / 64G | 06:00:00 | — | array, all 38 |
| `tlp_06_ko_embed` | 32G / 200G | 03:00:00 | `gpu=true` | array 1–38, `-tc 8` |

Sources: [01_export.sh](scripts/01_export.sh#L4-L7), [02_build_h5ad.sh](scripts/02_build_h5ad.sh#L4-L8), [04_tokenise.sh](scripts/04_tokenise.sh#L4-L8), [06_ko_embed.sh](scripts/06_ko_embed.sh#L4-L9)

Note the asymmetry in stage 06's memory request: modest host RAM (32G) but a very large virtual-memory ceiling (200G) for the GPU path. The fixed batch size of 256 requires about 21 GB of GPU memory plus CUDA overhead and fails on 24 GB cards; it is intentionally *not* auto-tuned, so that every patient is embedded identically. Cluster submission mechanics and the one-patient-first workflow are covered in [Cluster Execution and Job Chaining](18-cluster-execution-and-job-chaining).

Sources: [06_ko_embed.sh](scripts/06_ko_embed.sh#L10-L12)

## Configuration Layering

Configuration is split into two files with different consumption mechanisms and different blast radii. `config/paths.cfg` (five keys: `INPUT_DIR`, `WORK_DIR`, `RESULTS_DIR`, `SOFTWARE_DIR`, `BIND_PATHS`) is exported as environment variables by `env/terra_env.sh` and read by *every* stage — including the R script, which fails fast if a variable is missing. `config/analysis.cfg` holds only the analysed cell-state labels (`SOURCE_STATES`, `TARGET_STATES`) and is read exclusively through the `analysis_config.load_states()` module, which validates that the file exists, that no `<placeholder>` remains, and that target states are not duplicated.

Sources: [paths.cfg.example](config/paths.cfg.example#L1-L25), [01_export.R](scripts/01_export.R#L52-L60), [analysis.cfg.example](config/analysis.cfg.example#L1-L12), [analysis_config.py](scripts/analysis_config.py#L1-L35)

| Configuration surface | Keys | Consumed by | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|
| `config/paths.cfg` | `INPUT_DIR`, `WORK_DIR`, `RESULTS_DIR`, `SOFTWARE_DIR`, `BIND_PATHS` | all stages (01–07) | env vars via `env/terra_env.sh` |
| `config/analysis.cfg` | `SOURCE_STATES`, `TARGET_STATES` | stages 03, 04, 07 | `analysis_config.load_states()` |
| `MODEL_DIR` | model weights path | stages 04, 06 | env var set by `env/terra_env.sh` |

Sources: [analysis_config.py](scripts/analysis_config.py#L1-L8), [03_sample_table.py](scripts/03_sample_table.py#L47-L48), [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L59), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L64)

This split is what makes the pipeline's stated generalisation goal tractable: swapping the analysed ligand's source/target states requires editing one git-ignored file plus `analysis_config.py`'s hard-coded ligand constant — no pipeline logic changes. The roadmap for full generalisation is on [Planned Generalisation Roadmap](22-planned-generalisation-roadmap).

Sources: [analysis_config.py](scripts/analysis_config.py#L1-L35), [README.md](README.md#L224-L233)

## Resumability Convention

Resumability follows one uniform convention: a `FORCE_REBUILD = False` constant at the top of each heavy script, and idempotent output naming keyed by patient. Stages 01, 02, 04 and 06 skip patients whose outputs already exist (manifest, `adata.h5ad`, tokenised dataset, `emb_ko.npz` respectively); stage 07 reuses its cached per-donor predictions when the cohort signature is unchanged; stages 03 and 05 are cheap enough to always recompute. Because array tasks are patient-partitioned, re-running a stage after a partial failure only reprocesses the missing patients — the recommended workflow of running patient 1 of stage 06 manually before launching the full array depends entirely on this property.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L179-L183), [01_export.R](scripts/01_export.R#L43), [02_build_h5ad.py](scripts/02_build_h5ad.py#L23), [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L44), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L48-L49), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L72-L75)

## Architectural Invariants

Four invariants hold across the entire pipeline and explain most of its code shape. **First**, the cohort is an invariant, not data: stages 04–07 hard-pin the 38-patient exclusion set and refuse to run otherwise. **Second**, every patient artefact is keyed by patient ID and rebuilt independently, which is what makes array parallelism and resumability the same mechanism. **Third**, stage boundaries are validated contracts — manifests, assertions, and docstring-documented archive schemas — rather than shared code. **Fourth**, verification is fail-hard: stage 06's post-embedding checks exit non-zero on any failure, and downstream stages assert the presence and shape of upstream artifacts before touching them. Understanding these four makes every script in `scripts/` predictable in structure.

Sources: [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L60-L66), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L65-L66), [02_build_h5ad.py](scripts/02_build_h5ad.py#L51-L58), [05_null_genes.py](scripts/05_null_genes.py#L70-L75), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L353-L357)

## Where to Go Next

The natural reading order follows the DAG. For the design decisions behind each stage, continue with [Study Design and Hypothesis](6-study-design-and-hypothesis), then the Data Preparation pair — [R Export and Tissue Pieces](7-r-export-and-tissue-pieces) and [Patient Inclusion Rules](8-patient-inclusion-rules) — followed by the TERRA integration pair, [Cell-and-Neighbour Tokenisation](9-cell-and-neighbour-tokenisation) and [Harmonisation and Model Bundles](10-harmonisation-and-model-bundles). For the perturbation core, read [Token-Level Knockout Editing](11-token-level-knockout-editing) and [Rank-Matched Null Gene Selection](12-rank-matched-null-gene-selection). For operational detail on the orchestration summarised above, see [Cluster Execution and Job Chaining](18-cluster-execution-and-job-chaining) and [Reproducibility and Caching](19-reproducibility-and-caching), and for how to read the stage-07 workbooks, see [Outputs and Result Interpretation](20-outputs-and-result-interpretation).

# Study Design and Hypothesis



This page explains *why* the terra-ligand-perturbation pipeline is structured the way it is: the biological question it answers, the hypothesis architecture, the pre-specified cohort rules, and the control matrix that makes a zero-shot embedding shift interpretable. It is the conceptual foundation for the Deep Dive pages that follow — the operational details of each mechanism live in dedicated pages referenced throughout.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L1-L16)

## The Scientific Question: Ligand Signalling as a Representation Problem

Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are a major source of ligands acting on macrophages within the tumour microenvironment, and CSF1 is the ligand under study here. Because TERRA encodes each cell *together with its spatial neighbours*, the repository can ask an *in silico* question that would otherwise require an experiment: does removing a ligand from the neighbouring cells change the model's representation of the receiving cell? The study uses the public TNBC Xenium cohort of Yan *et al.* (2026) and the pretrained TERRA-112M foundation model (Birk *et al.*, 2026) in zero-shot mode — TERRA is never fine-tuned.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L18-L28), [README.md](README.md#L30-L44)

The hypothesis is stated as two coupled claims: **(H1) existence** — removing CSF1 from CSF1-expressing fibroblast neighbours shifts the TERRA representation of selected target macrophage states; and **(H2) specificity** — any observed shift exceeds what removing a comparable gene at the same positions would produce. This two-part structure is the single most important design decision in the repository: a magnitude change alone can never support H2, so the entire control apparatus exists to separate "the embedding changed" from "CSF1 specifically caused the change."

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L24-L28), [README.md](README.md#L112-L123)

## Hypothesis Architecture: Mapping Claims to Evidence Classes

Every condition in the pipeline exists to adjudicate exactly one branch of the hypothesis. The concept map below shows how the four evidence classes relate to the claims — this is the mental model that makes the seven-script pipeline coherent:

```mermaid
graph TD
    H["Core hypothesis: CSF1 removal from CSF1+ fibroblast<br/>neighbour blocks shifts target-macrophage<br/>representations more than comparable genes"]
    H --> H0["H0 Detection capacity"]
    H --> H1["H1 Existence of a shift"]
    H --> H2["H2 Specificity of the shift"]
    H0 --> E3["POS_block: whole block emptied<br/>positive control"]
    H1 --> E1["CSF1_remove: token and value removed<br/>test condition"]
    H2 --> E2["NULL_gene x 20: same edit, same blocks<br/>reference distribution"]
    H2 --> E4["CSF1_zero: value zeroed, token kept<br/>encoding sensitivity check"]
    H1 --> E5["cell_emb readout: unchanged by<br/>neighbour edits - negative control"]
    E2 --> V["Interpretation gate: CSF1 effects are only<br/>meaningful if POS_block detects change<br/>and nulls stay inside their distribution"]
    E3 --> V
    E4 --> V
```

Two observations of TERRA's current behaviour motivated a further, purely technical design constraint: perturbations are built by **direct token editing** of the tokenised sequences rather than re-tokenisation or the library's `perturb_dataset`. Re-tokenising after zeroing CSF1 counts changes tokens of *non-fibroblast* cells, and in `terra-st 0.1.13` the `perturb_dataset` neighbourhood target also edited blocks belonging to unlisted cells — both would contaminate the contrast between conditions.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L65-L83), [README.md](README.md#L10-L14)

> [!TIP]
> The null genes are not merely "other genes" — each null is knocked out in **exactly the same neighbour blocks as CSF1** (the blocks of CSF1+ fibroblasts), so a null must be visible to the model in those blocks about as often and at about the same rank as CSF1. This is why the design enforces edit-position comparability and why the null set is chosen once for the whole cohort (seed 1234) rather than per patient.

## Cohort Design: Pre-specified Inclusion Rules

The cohort is fixed before any perturbation results are seen. All 44 patients with Xenium data are exported on the gene panel shared by all sections, and tissue pieces are defined as connected regions of occupied 100 µm bins so that spatial neighbourhoods never bridge separate pieces. Three inclusion thresholds, all pre-specified in the step 03 docstring and constants, then determine eligibility — leaving exactly 38 patients, a number the pipeline hard-checks in steps 04, 06 and 07 (`N_INCLUDED = 38`, `EXPECTED_N_DONORS = 38`).

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L48-L54), [scripts/03_sample_table.py](scripts/03_sample_table.py#L20-L23), [scripts/04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L31-L35)

| Threshold | Value | Code constant | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| Median depth | ≥ 100 counts | `MIN_MEDIAN_DEPTH` | Excludes uninformative sections (P10, P23) |
| CSF1+ fibroblasts | ≥ 50 | `MIN_CSF1POS_FIB` | Guarantees enough source blocks to edit (P71, P87, P89, P93) |
| Target macrophages | ≥ 50 | `MIN_TARGET_MAC` | Guarantees enough receiving cells for the readout |

Sources: [scripts/03_sample_table.py](scripts/03_sample_table.py#L12-L23), [scripts/03_sample_table.py](scripts/03_sample_table.py#L48-L53), [scripts/03_sample_table.py](scripts/03_sample_table.py#L99-L103)

The cell definitions themselves are configuration-driven rather than hard-coded: a **CSF1+ fibroblast** is a `Fibro` cell whose `cell_state` is in `SOURCE_STATES` with a raw CSF1 count > 0, and a **target macrophage** is a `Mye` cell in `TARGET_STATES`. Both lists are read from `config/analysis.cfg` at import time by `load_states()`, with validation that placeholders are replaced and no target state is listed twice. This makes the study design a *parameter* of the pipeline, which is the foundation for the planned generalisation to arbitrary ligand–source–target triples.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L56-L60), [scripts/analysis_config.py](scripts/analysis_config.py#L1-L35)

> [!TIP]
> Watch a subtle cohort-design distinction: step 03 reports a *descriptive* depth batch at ≥ 400 counts (`DEEP_DEPTH`, noting the cohort is bimodal ~140 vs ~730), but the **analysis** depth batch actually used by step 07 is defined in step 04 at ≥ 500 counts (`DEPTH_CUT`), splitting the cohort into 12 deep and 26 shallow patients. When reading per-batch statistics, the ≥ 500 definition is the operative one.

## The Perturbation Principle: Edit Tokens, Not Expression

Every patient is tokenised **once**, and every perturbation is built by editing those baseline tokens directly — only in the neighbour blocks (blocks 1–10) that belong to a CSF1+ fibroblast.
