The macrophage's own block and all other neighbours are never touched. Each cell is edited by a condition when at least one of its CSF1+ fibroblast neighbour blocks contains the gene, and `n_edit` counts those blocks — this per-cell edit count later becomes a stratification variable. The one-time tokenisation also avoids re-tokenisation reshuffling tied genes between baseline and perturbed conditions.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L65-L71), [scripts/06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L7-L26), [scripts/04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L6-L11)

| Condition | Edit in each CSF1+ fibroblast neighbour block | Hypothesis role |
|---|---|---|
| `CSF1_remove` (test) | CSF1 token and value removed; remaining tokens move up | The perturbation of interest (H1) |
| `NULL_<gene>` × 20 | Same edit for a rank-matched null gene | Reference distribution for H2 |
| `POS_block` | Whole block emptied | H0: pipeline can detect a neighbourhood change |
| `CSF1_zero` | CSF1 value set to 0, token kept | Checks dependence on how a loss is encoded |
| `cell_emb` readout | (all conditions) | Negative control: neighbour edits cannot change the cell's own embedding |

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L85-L91)

## Why Gene-Level Controls Matter: The Control Matrix

The inference principle is stated unambiguously in the README: changing *any* input changes a model's output, and larger or more prominent changes produce larger effects. Therefore reporting only the magnitude of output change after removing a gene cannot distinguish a gene-specific effect from a generic edit effect. The design's answer is **relational inference**: instead of asking whether removing CSF1 changes the output, the analysis asks whether CSF1's effect *exceeds* that of comparable genes selected the same way but not expected to carry macrophage-directed signal — the candidate pool explicitly excludes 49 ligands with established effects on macrophage recruitment, survival or polarisation.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L112-L123), [scripts/05_null_genes.py](scripts/05_null_genes.py#L6-L24), [scripts/05_null_genes.py](scripts/05_null_genes.py#L43-L58)

Each control class answers a different failure mode of the readout, and the interpretation logic chains them together:

| Control type | Condition | Question it answers | If it fails |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reference distribution | 20 × `NULL_<gene>` | Is CSF1's effect larger than a comparable edit? | CSF1 effect is indistinguishable from generic editing |
| Positive control | `POS_block` | Can the pipeline detect a real neighbourhood change at all? | Small CSF1 effects become uninterpretable |
| Secondary test | `CSF1_zero` | Does the conclusion depend on the edit encoding? | Results are encoding artifacts |
| Negative control | `cell_emb` | Is the readout directionally sensible? | A neighbour edit altered the cell's own embedding |

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L85-L91), [README.md](README.md#L125-L128), [scripts/07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L6-L10)

The interpretation rule that falls out of this matrix is deliberately conservative: if the positive control performs as expected while the test gene produces only a small change, the small effect is interpretable as biologically or functionally **weak** rather than as a failure of the method. This converts a null-ish result from an ambiguity into a finding.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L125-L128)

## Readout Design: Direction from the Classifier, Magnitude from Distances

The primary readout converts embeddings into a *directional* score. A logistic regression is trained on baseline embeddings of all `mac-*` myeloid cells to score P(target) — any target state versus all other macrophage states — fitted **leave-one-donor-out**, so the model scoring a donor never saw that donor's cells. For each edited target macrophage, dP = P(perturbed) − P(baseline). Secondary readouts are purely descriptive magnitudes: per-cell cosine shift, and TERRA's own Wasserstein-2 (W2) distance between baseline and perturbed embeddings per donor.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L99-L110), [scripts/07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L26-L38)

| Readout | Input | Measures | Role in the design |
|---|---|---|---|
| Classifier dP (primary) | `spatial_cell_emb`, LODON logistic regression | Directional shift toward/away target-state identity | Testable statistic for H2 |
| Neighbourhood dP (secondary) | `neighborhood_emb`, same classifier | Directional shift in the neighbourhood channel | Robustness of the primary result |
| Cosine shift (descriptive) | per-cell embeddings | Raw magnitude of embedding movement | No direction information |
| W2 distance (descriptive) | Sinkhorn population distance (p=2, blur 0.01) | Per-donor population displacement | Explicitly never used as evidence of direction |

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L99-L110), [scripts/07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L40-L51)

The cohort-level decision rule makes the specificity claim (H2) operational by subtracting the null reference **before** any testing: each donor's statistic *d* is defined as mean dP(condition) minus the median over the 20 null genes of mean dP(null) — so *d* isolates the component of the shift that is specific to the tested gene rather than generic to editing those blocks. Eligible donors are those with at least `MIN_EDITED = 20` target macrophages edited by `CSF1_remove`; *d* is then tested against zero with a two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test over eligible donors, repeated per depth batch, and every condition is ranked by cohort median donor mean dP among the 21 genes. Crucially, **no automatic call is made** — the statistics are reported for human interpretation.

Sources: [scripts/07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L53-L67), [scripts/07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L91-L96)

```mermaid
graph LR
    B["Baseline mac-* embeddings"] --> C["LODON classifier<br/>P(target)"]
    P["Perturbed target-macrophage<br/>embeddings, same row order"] --> C
    C --> DP["dP per edited cell"]
    DP --> D["donor d = mean dP condition<br/>minus median mean dP null"]
    D --> W["Wilcoxon signed-rank test<br/>overall and per depth batch"]
    D --> R["gene rank among 21 conditions"]
    W --> I["Human interpretation<br/>no automatic call"]
    R --> I
```

Embedding consistency is enforced structurally rather than statistically: baseline and every condition embed the *same target-macrophage rows in the same order*, so batching is identical across conditions, and `cell_emb` is recorded for all conditions as the negative control that a neighbour edit cannot change.

Sources: [scripts/06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L28-L34)

## Design Limitations the Hypothesis Must Live With

Three limitations are documented as part of the design itself, not as afterthoughts. First, **low-count transcripts**: a ligand is represented only if it falls within a cell's 256 most highly expressed genes, so the perturbation only acts where CSF1 is actually tokenised. Second, the **zero-shot setting**: TERRA was never trained to predict perturbation responses, so a representational change is not a predicted biological response — the hypothesis is about the model's encoding, not about cell behaviour. Third, the **readout dependence**: the classifier readout inherits the dataset authors' label-transfer annotations of macrophage states, via the configured `TARGET_STATES`.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L130-L138), [scripts/analysis_config.py](scripts/analysis_config.py#L1-L9)

## Navigating the Deep Dive

The design summarised here decomposes into the operational pages of the Deep Dive section. For the mechanics behind each design decision, follow this progression: start with the overall execution topology in [Pipeline Architecture](5-pipeline-architecture), then see how the cohort rules become enforced code in [Patient Inclusion Rules](8-patient-inclusion-rules) and how the one-time tokenisation works in [Cell-and-Neighbour Tokenisation](9-cell-and-neighbour-tokenisation). The perturbation principle is implemented in [Token-Level Knockout Editing](11-token-level-knockout-editing), with the control apparatus detailed in [Rank-Matched Null Gene Selection](12-rank-matched-null-gene-selection), [Control Conditions Design](13-control-conditions-design), and [Null-Gene Control Rationale](14-null-gene-control-rationale). The readout design unfolds across [Leave-One-Donor-Out Classifier](15-leave-one-donor-out-classifier), [Embedding Shift Magnitudes](16-embedding-shift-magnitudes), and [Cohort Summary Statistics](17-cohort-summary-statistics), and the resulting evidence is consumed in [Outputs and Result Interpretation](20-outputs-and-result-interpretation).


# R Export and Tissue Pieces



Step 01 is the only R stage in the pipeline. It reads the per-patient Xenium RDS objects distributed by the dataset authors and converts them into a plain, language-neutral binary format that the Python side of the pipeline assembles into one `.h5ad` file per patient. Along the way it defines the pipeline's spatial sampling units — **tissue pieces** — which guarantee that TERRA's nearest-neighbour graph is never built across physically separate tissue regions. This page covers the export logic in `scripts/01_export.R`, its SGE job wrapper, the shared-panel and tissue-piece algorithms, the binary file contract, and the job's caching behaviour.

## Where Step 01 Sits in the Pipeline

The script implements a **two-pass architecture**: pass 1 establishes a cohort-wide gene space, pass 2 exports each patient independently against that space. Its inputs are three RDS files per patient directory (`mat_counts.rds`, `df_meta.rds`, `spatial_xy.rds`), and its outputs land in `WORK_DIR/export/` as binary sparse matrices plus per-cell metadata tables, with a summary workbook in `RESULTS_DIR/01_export/`. The downstream consumer is `02_build_h5ad.py`, which reads the binaries with `numpy.fromfile` and validates them against the manifest before assembling the per-patient `.h5ad`.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    M["mat_counts.rds<br/>(genes x cells counts)"] --> P1
    M --> P2
    MD["df_meta.rds<br/>(cell annotations, QC)"] --> P2
    XY["spatial_xy.rds<br/>(x, y coordinates)"] --> P2
    P1["Pass 1: intersect all gene panels,<br/>ordered by first patient"] --> G["genes_shared.tsv"]
    P2["Pass 2: per-patient export"] --> T["tissue_components()"]
    T --> F["keep = finite xy AND piece &gt; 0<br/>AND n_genes_shared &gt;= 10"]
    F --> B["x.bin / i.bin / p.bin<br/>(CSC, int32 little-endian)"]
    F --> C["cells.csv"]
    F --> MA["manifest.txt"]
    B --> H["02_build_h5ad.py<br/>(one .h5ad per patient)"]
    C --> H
    MA --> H
```

Two scope boundaries matter for reading this page. Step 01 exports *all* cells that pass its per-cell thresholds — the cohort-level **patient inclusion rules** (median depth, CSF1+ fibroblast and target-macrophage counts) are applied later, in step 03, and are documented in [Patient Inclusion Rules](8-patient-inclusion-rules). Likewise, the cell states analysed in the study live in `config/analysis.cfg` and are first consumed by step 03; step 01 reads only the path variables from `config/paths.cfg`.

Sources: [01_export.R](scripts/01_export.R#L1-L44), [01_export.sh](scripts/01_export.sh#L1-L20), [README.md](README.md#L50-L54), [paths.cfg.example](config/paths.cfg.example#L8-L17)

## The Shared Gene Panel (Pass 1)

Xenium sections can carry different gene panels, but every downstream representation must live in an identical gene space. Pass 1 reads only the row names of each patient's `mat_counts.rds`, computes their intersection with `Reduce(intersect, ...)`, and then **re-orders the result to match the first patient's panel order** rather than the arbitrary order `intersect` would produce. Two `stopifnot` guards abort the run if the intersection is empty or if any patient panel contains duplicated gene names. The resulting vector is written once to `WORK_DIR/export/genes_shared.tsv`, where the per-patient manifests later point to it as the authoritative gene index.

Sources: [01_export.R](scripts/01_export.R#L118-L132)

## Tissue Piece Segmentation

This is the conceptual core of the step. The study motivates it directly: tissue pieces are "connected regions of occupied 100 um bins, so that spatial neighbourhoods never bridge separate pieces" — since TERRA encodes each cell together with its spatial neighbours, a cell at the edge of one tissue fragment must never have neighbours drawn from an unrelated fragment. The sample identifier handed to TERRA is therefore **patient × piece** (for example `P11_t1`), which confines the kNN graph within a piece.

The `tissue_components()` function turns raw coordinates into piece labels in four stages:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["all cells with finite x, y"] --> B["assign each cell to a 100 um bin:<br/>floor(coordinate / BIN_UM)"]
    B --> C["keep occupied bins:<br/>>= 5 cells per bin (MIN_CELLS_BIN)"]
    C --> D["link bins that share an edge<br/>(rook / 4-connectivity)"]
    D --> E["connected components via igraph"]
    E --> F{"component size<br/>>= 10 bins?"}
    F -- "no (debris)" --> Z["label 0:<br/>cells dropped"]
    F -- yes --> R["renumber 1..k within patient<br/>by decreasing cell count"]
    R --> S["sample_id = patient_t&lt;piece&gt;<br/>e.g. P11_t1"]
```

Concretely, cells are binned by `floor(x / BIN_UM)` and `floor(y / BIN_UM)`; bins with fewer than `MIN_CELLS_BIN` cells are treated as empty; an undirected graph is built over occupied bins using rook adjacency (the `dx = c(1,0), dy = c(0,1)` edge construction covers all four edge-sharing neighbours for an undirected graph; an 8-connectivity king-move variant is provided but disabled); `igraph::components` yields the connected regions; and any region smaller than `MIN_REGION_BINS` bins — i.e. under 0.1 mm² — is relabelled `0` as debris. Cells in empty or sub-threshold bins also receive label `0`. Back in the main loop, surviving components are renumbered `1..k` within each patient by decreasing cell count, so `t1` is always the largest piece.

| Constant | Value | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `BIN_UM` | 100 µm | side length of the spatial binning grid |
| `MIN_CELLS_BIN` | 5 | bins below this density are unoccupied |
| `CONNECTIVITY` | 4 | rook adjacency; edge-sharing bins only |
| `MIN_REGION_BINS` | 10 | regions below 0.1 mm² are classified as debris |
| `MIN_GENES_CELL` | 10 | per-cell gene threshold on the shared panel |
| `FORCE_REBUILD` | FALSE | skip patients whose manifest already exists |

> [!TIP]
> The size-ordered renumbering makes `sample_id` assignment **deterministic**: re-running the export on unchanged data always yields the same `P11_t1` = largest piece mapping, which matters because every downstream step (tokenisation, perturbation caching, per-donor pooling) keys off these identifiers.

Sources: [01_export.R](scripts/01_export.R#L11-L19), [01_export.R](scripts/01_export.R#L62-L70), [01_export.R](scripts/01_export.R#L75-L109), [01_export.R](scripts/01_export.R#L159-L164), [README.md](README.md#L50-L54)

## Cell Retention Rules

Within each patient, a cell is exported only if it satisfies **three conjunctive conditions**: finite coordinates (`ok`), membership in a non-debris piece (`piece > 0`), and at least `MIN_GENES_CELL = 10` genes detected on the shared panel. The gene threshold is deliberate — it matches TERRA's own pretraining QC, which removed cells with fewer than 10 expressed genes, so the exported cohort arrives in the distribution the model was trained to expect. Annotation is *not* required: unannotated cells are exported too, because they are real neighbours whose transcripts shape TERRA's neighbourhood representation of annotated cells.

Two defensive checks protect data integrity before anything is written. First, the three RDS objects must be row-aligned (`stopifnot` on dimensions and row-name identity, plus an explicit column-name check on the count matrix). Second, the script **aborts if any count is non-integer** rather than silently rounding — a guard against float-contaminated inputs producing corrupt sparse payloads. The counts matrix itself is subset to the shared panel, converted to CSC form, and explicit zeros are dropped via `drop0` before `n_genes_shared` is derived from the column-pointer differences.

Sources: [01_export.R](scripts/01_export.R#L20-L23), [01_export.R](scripts/01_export.R#L68), [01_export.R](scripts/01_export.R#L145-L175)

## The Binary Exchange Format

The genes × cells matrix is written exactly as the three slots of an R `dgCMatrix` — a deliberate choice that keeps the format language-neutral and trivially readable from numpy:

| File | Content | Type |
|---|---|---|
| `x.bin` | non-zero count values | int32, little-endian |
| `i.bin` | 0-based gene (row) index of each value | int32, little-endian |
| `p.bin` | CSC column pointers, length `n_cells + 1` | int32, little-endian |

Because the matrix is stored genes × cells (not cells × genes), the Python side reads each column as a cell without transposing. Alongside the binaries, the script writes `cells.csv` (one row per exported cell) and `manifest.txt`, which records `patient`, `n_cells`, `n_genes`, `nnz`, `total_counts`, the layout string, and a pointer to `../genes_shared.tsv`. Step 02 reads the binaries with `numpy.fromfile` and validates them against these manifest numbers, so the manifest functions as the **inter-step integrity contract**.

> [!TIP]
> `manifest.txt` is simultaneously the integrity contract and the **cache sentinel**: the main loop skips any patient whose manifest already exists unless `FORCE_REBUILD` is set to TRUE. This is why deleting a patient's manifest — not its binaries — is the correct way to force a re-export.

Sources: [01_export.R](scripts/01_export.R#L35-L44), [01_export.R](scripts/01_export.R#L111-L116), [01_export.R](scripts/01_export.R#L177-L207)

## The cells.csv Schema

Every exported cell gets a row carrying identity, spatial, annotation, and QC columns — everything later steps need without re-reading the R objects:

| Column | Origin | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `cell_id` | `rownames(df_meta)` | original cell barcode |
| `patient`, `piece`, `sample_id` | directory name + segmentation | sample identity, formatted `<patient>_t<piece>` |
| `x`, `y` | `spatial_xy.rds` | coordinate in the Xenium frame |
| `cell_type`, `cell_state`, `Niche`, `paper_patient_id` | `df_meta.rds` | dataset authors' annotations (may be empty for unannotated cells) |
| `nCount_Xenium`, `nFeature_Xenium` | `df_meta.rds` | raw per-cell QC metrics from the source dataset |
| `n_genes_shared` | computed | genes detected on the shared panel (the retention metric) |

Sources: [01_export.R](scripts/01_export.R#L181-L197)

## Running the Job, Caching, and Reporting

The shell wrapper `01_export.sh` is a Sun Grid Engine CPU job requesting 64 GB (`tmem=64G,h_vmem=64G`) and six hours of wall time. It sources `env/terra_env.sh`, which materialises `INPUT_DIR`, `WORK_DIR`, `RESULTS_DIR` (and `REPO_DIR`) as environment variables from `config/paths.cfg`, then invokes `Rscript` on the host. The R script refuses to start if any of these variables is unset, so it cannot accidentally read from default paths. Runtime dependencies are three R packages — `Matrix`, `igraph`, and `openxlsx` — developed against R 4.4.1.

The job's skip logic means it is **resumable at patient granularity**: interrupted runs re-submit cleanly and redo only the patients lacking a manifest. At the end, all per-patient accounting rows are combined into `RESULTS_DIR/01_export/01_export.xlsx` with two sheets: `per_patient` (cells in, bad coordinates, debris, low-gene drops, cells exported, piece counts and sizes, panel size, nnz) and `parameters` (the six constants of the segmentation plus the shared-panel size), making every export run self-documenting for QC.

| Summary field | What it counts |
|---|---|
| `n_cells_in` | cells read from `df_meta.rds` |
| `n_bad_xy` | cells with non-finite coordinates |
| `n_debris` | valid-coordinate cells in debris or sub-threshold bins |
| `n_low_genes` | cells in a piece but below 10 shared-panel genes |
| `n_cells_exported` | survivors of all three filters |
| `n_pieces` / `cells_per_piece` | piece count and per-piece cell sizes |

Sources: [01_export.sh](scripts/01_export.sh#L1-L20), [01_export.R](scripts/01_export.R#L52-L60), [01_export.R](scripts/01_export.R#L137-L143), [01_export.R](scripts/01_export.R#L209-L244), [README.md](README.md#L185-L199)

## Where to Go Next

Step 01 deliberately exports a *generous* cohort — every cell that passes the per-cell thresholds, in every piece of every patient. The cohort is narrowed to analysable patients by depth and cell-population criteria in the next data-preparation stage, [Patient Inclusion Rules](8-patient-inclusion-rules). For the surrounding context of how this step fits into the seven-stage pipeline, see [Pipeline Architecture](5-pipeline-architecture) and [Configuration Setup](4-configuration-setup); for what happens to the exported pieces once they reach the Python side, continue to [Cell-and-Neighbour Tokenisation](9-cell-and-neighbour-tokenisation).


# Patient Inclusion Rules



Not every patient with exported Xenium data can support a meaningful perturbation experiment. A patient with almost no annotated cells, or with too few CSF1-producing fibroblasts, would contribute noise rather than signal to the ligand-removal analysis. This page explains the **patient inclusion rules**: the three pre-specified, quantitative criteria that decide which patients enter the analysis, how each criterion is computed from the data, and how the decision is recorded and enforced downstream. The implementation lives in a single, small script — `scripts/03_sample_table.py` — making it an ideal place to understand how the pipeline filters its cohort.

## Where Inclusion Fits in the Pipeline

The inclusion step acts as a **gate** between data export and model work. Steps 01 and 02 (covered in [R Export and Tissue Pieces](7-r-export-and-tissue-pieces)) export *every* patient — all 44 with Xenium data — producing one `adata.h5ad` file per patient. Step 03 then reads each of those files, computes summary metrics per patient, applies the three inclusion rules, and writes a decision table. Only patients marked `included = True` proceed to tokenisation in step 04 ([Cell-and-Neighbour Tokenisation](9-cell-and-neighbour-tokenisation)) and everything after it.

```mermaid
graph LR
    A["01_export.R<br/>(all 44 patients)"] --> B["02_build_h5ad.py<br/>(one adata.h5ad per patient)"]
    B --> C["03_sample_table.py<br/>(THIS STEP: apply 3 rules)"]
    C -->|included = True| D["04_tokenise.py<br/>(38 patients tokenised)"]
    C -->|included = False| E["Excluded<br/>(6 patients: P10, P23, P71,<br/>P87, P89, P93)"]
    D --> F["05-07: null genes,<br/>perturbations, statistics"]
```

Note the deliberate design: the filter is **not** a side effect of export. Everything is exported first, so the inclusion decision can be *reviewed in a table* before any expensive model work begins — and so the decision itself becomes documented, reproducible evidence.

Sources: [03_sample_table.py](/scripts/03_sample_table.py#L1-L35), [README.md](/README.md#L50-L54)

## The Inputs: What Each Patient's Metrics Are Computed From

The script loops over every `<WORK_DIR>/export/<PATIENT>/adata.h5ad` file and computes a handful of metrics from the cell-level metadata stored in `adata.obs`. Those metadata fields were created upstream: `01_export.R` wrote them into a per-patient `cells.csv` (including `cell_type`, `cell_state`, `nCount_Xenium`, and a piece-based `sample_id`), and `02_build_h5ad.py` carried them into `obs` — renaming `sample_id` to `sample` along the way. Understanding this provenance matters: the inclusion metrics are only as good as the annotations produced by the dataset authors' label transfer.

The script also asserts that the ligand gene *CSF1* exists in the patient's gene panel — aborting with a clear error if it does not, since without CSF1 counts the fibroblast-source metric cannot be defined.

| `obs` field | Meaning | Used to compute |
|---|---|---|
| `cell_type` | Broad cell class (e.g. `"Fibro"`, `"Mye"`) | Fibroblast and macrophage gating |
| `cell_state` | Fine-grained state label; `NA` if unannotated | State matching + annotated-cell depth |
| `nCount_Xenium` | Total raw counts per cell | Median depth |
| `sample` | Patient × tissue piece identifier (e.g. `P11_t1`) | `n_pieces`, `cells_per_piece` |
| `var_names` (matrix) | Shared gene panel including `CSF1` | CSF1-positive counts |

Sources: [03_sample_table.py](/scripts/03_sample_table.py#L58-L72), [01_export.R](/scripts/01_export.R#L181-L196), [02_build_h5ad.py](/scripts/02_build_h5ad.py#L86-L98)

## The Three Inclusion Rules

The rules are stated in the script's docstring as "all must hold" — a patient is included only if **every** criterion passes. Each is defined by a constant at the top of the script, computed per patient, and stored as a boolean column:

| # | Rule | Metric | Threshold | Constant | Pass column |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Sufficient sequencing depth | Median `nCount_Xenium` over *annotated* cells | ≥ 100 counts | `MIN_MEDIAN_DEPTH = 100` | `pass_depth` |
| 2 | Enough ligand-source cells | CSF1+ fibroblast count | ≥ 50 cells | `MIN_CSF1POS_FIB = 50` | `pass_csf1pos_fib` |
| 3 | Enough target cells | Target macrophage count | ≥ 50 cells | `MIN_TARGET_MAC = 50` | `pass_target_mac` |

The final decision is the logical AND of the three: `T["included"] = T["pass_depth"] & T["pass_csf1pos_fib"] & T["pass_target_mac"]`.

```python
T["pass_depth"]        = T["median_depth_annot"] >= MIN_MEDIAN_DEPTH
T["pass_csf1pos_fib"]  = T["n_csf1pos_fib"]     >= MIN_CSF1POS_FIB
T["pass_target_mac"]   = T["n_target_mac"]      >= MIN_TARGET_MAC
T["included"] = T["pass_depth"] & T["pass_csf1pos_fib"] & T["pass_target_mac"]
```

In this cohort the outcome is **38 of 44 patients included**, with six patients failing: P10 and P23 fail the depth rule, and P71, P87, P89, and P93 fail the CSF1+ fibroblast rule (no patient fails the macrophage rule alone).

Sources: [03_sample_table.py](/scripts/03_sample_table.py#L20-L54), [03_sample_table.py](/scripts/03_sample_table.py#L99-L102), [04_tokenise.py](/scripts/04_tokenise.py#L31-L35)

### How Each Metric Is Actually Computed

The two cell-type metrics are *conjunctions* — a cell must satisfy both a broad-type gate and a fine-state gate. This makes the definitions sensitive to the configured state labels (next section).

**CSF1+ fibroblast** — a cell counted here must be a fibroblast by type (`cell_type == "Fibro"`), belong to one of the configured *source* states (`cell_state` in `FIB_STATES`), **and** carry at least one raw *CSF1* transcript:

```python
fib = ((o["cell_type"] == "Fibro") & o["cell_state"].isin(FIB_STATES)).to_numpy()
n_csf1pos_fib = (fib & (lig > 0)).sum()   # lig = raw CSF1 counts per cell
```

**Target macrophage** — a myeloid cell (`cell_type == "Mye"`) whose state appears in the configured *target* list (`MAC_TARGET`). No count threshold applies; membership in a target state is sufficient.

**Median depth** — the median of `nCount_Xenium` restricted to *annotated* cells (`cell_state` is not `NA`). This restriction is a deliberate methodological choice: raw counts differ by tissue processing batch, and unannotated cells are not part of the readout populations, so they are excluded from the depth summary even though they remain in the exported data as real neighbours.

| Metric | Formula in words | Line |
|---|---|---|
| `median_depth_annot` | median of `nCount_Xenium` where `cell_state` is not NA | [L72](/scripts/03_sample_table.py#L72) |
| `n_fib` | count of (`Fibro` AND state ∈ `FIB_STATES`) | [L70](/scripts/03_sample_table.py#L70) |
| `n_csf1pos_fib` | count of (`n_fib` selection AND raw CSF1 > 0) | [L82](/scripts/03_sample_table.py#L82) |
| `n_target_mac` | count of (`Mye` AND state ∈ `MAC_TARGET`) | [L71](/scripts/03_sample_table.py#L71) |

Sources: [03_sample_table.py](/scripts/03_sample_table.py#L68-L84)

## Configuration-Driven State Labels

Notice that the script never hard-codes *which* fibroblast or macrophage states count. The lists `FIB_STATES` and `MAC_TARGET` are loaded at runtime from `config/analysis.cfg` via a shared helper module, `analysis_config.py` (the config maps to `SOURCE_STATES` and `TARGET_STATES`). This is what makes the pipeline reusable on other datasets: you supply the cell-state labels of *your* annotation scheme, and the same inclusion thresholds apply.

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["config/analysis.cfg<br/>SOURCE_STATES=..., TARGET_STATES=..."] --> B["analysis_config.py<br/>load_states()"]
    B --> C1["FIB_STATES"]
    B --> C2["MAC_TARGET"]
    C1 --> D["03_sample_table.py<br/>n_csf1pos_fib metric"]
    C2 --> E["03_sample_table.py<br/>n_target_mac metric"]
    C1 --> F["04_tokenise.py / 05_null_genes.py<br/>(same definitions reused)"]
    E --> F
```

The loader performs three validations before returning anything, so misconfiguration fails **fast and loudly** rather than producing a silently wrong cohort table:

1. The file must exist — otherwise you are told to copy `analysis.cfg.example`.
2. `SOURCE_STATES` and `TARGET_STATES` must be non-empty and must not still contain `<placeholder>` entries.
3. `TARGET_STATES` must not list the same state twice.

Sources: [analysis_config.py](/scripts/analysis_config.py#L16-L34), [analysis.cfg.example](/config/analysis.cfg.example#L7-L11), [03_sample_table.py](/scripts/03_sample_table.py#L47-L48)

## The Depth Batch: Informational Column, Not an Inclusion Rule

> [!TIP]
> Beginners frequently confuse the two depth-batch definitions in this repository. **Step 03** computes a `depth_batch` column with threshold 400 purely *for information* (the cohort is bimodal, at roughly 140 vs. 730 counts, so a cut near 400 separates the modes). The **analysis-level** depth batch used by downstream statistics is defined separately in step 04 with a stricter threshold of 500 ("deep" ≥ 500: 12 patients; "shallow": 26). The `depth_batch` value in the step-03 table will *not* necessarily match the batch used in final results.

Because depth enters the inclusion rules only through the ≥ 100 gate, the batch label has no effect on who is included. Its purpose in the table is exploratory: seeing which side of the bimodal depth distribution each patient sits on helps you sanity-check the cohort before deeper analysis. The `frac_csf1pos_fib` column (CSF1+ fibroblasts divided by all source-state fibroblasts, rounded to three decimals) serves a similar descriptive role — it is computed and reported but never used in the inclusion decision.

| Aspect | Step 03 `depth_batch` (this page) | Analysis depth batch (step 04) |
|---|---|---|
| Threshold | ≥ 400 (`DEEP_DEPTH = 400`) | ≥ 500 (`DEPTH_CUT = 500`) |
| Purpose | Descriptive, in the cohort table | Stratification of downstream statistics |
| Effect on inclusion | None — informational only | None — but used in step 07 readouts |

Sources: [03_sample_table.py](/scripts/03_sample_table.py#L25-L27), [03_sample_table.py](/scripts/03_sample_table.py#L96-L98), [04_tokenise.py](/scripts/04_tokenise.py#L18-L20), [README.md](/README.md#L61-L63)

## What the Step Produces and How Decisions Are Enforced Later

The script writes two files to `RESULTS_DIR/03_sample_table/`: an Excel workbook `03_sample_table.xlsx` with a `per_patient` sheet (one row per patient) and a `parameters` sheet (a snapshot of every threshold and state list used — a built-in provenance record), plus a plain `03_sample_table.csv` copy that is written even if `openpyxl` is unavailable in the container. The console output ends with an explicit line listing the excluded patients by name, so the decision is visible at a glance without opening the workbook.

> [!TIP]
> Downstream enforcement is deliberately rigid: `04_tokenise.py` hard-codes the expected excluded patients (`EXCLUDED = {"P10": ..., "P71": ...}`) and *refuses to run* unless exactly 38 patients remain after subtraction (`N_INCLUDED = 38`, checked in `included_patients()`). This looks redundant but is a safety property — if the inclusion outcome ever changes (new data, edited thresholds, different state labels), step 04 fails immediately instead of silently tokenising an unexpected cohort. If you adapt this pipeline, update both the thresholds *and* this guard together.

One more beginner-relevant detail: the table is sorted `included` first, then by cell count ascending. This is not cosmetic — the docstring states the smallest passing patient is intended as the single patient for *initial testing*, ideally one that is deep and has more than one tissue piece. Because of the sort, the first included row is precisely that pilot candidate, and in step 04 the smallest included patient also receives array task ID 1.

Sources: [03_sample_table.py](/scripts/03_sample_table.py#L103-L126), [03_sample_table.py](/scripts/03_sample_table.py#L8-L10), [04_tokenise.py](/scripts/04_tokenise.py#L60-L66), [04_tokenise.py](/scripts/04_tokenise.py#L106-L112), [03_sample_table.py](/scripts/03_sample_table.py#L112-L118)

## Running the Step and Common Beginner Questions

The step runs as a single CPU job inside the TERRA container after step 02 completes, chained via `qsub -hold_jid tlp_02_build_h5ad scripts/03_sample_table.sh`. It is fast — one pass over 44 `.h5ad` files — and unlike export/tokenisation steps, it always recomputes (no `FORCE_REBUILD` cache), which keeps the cohort table always in sync with the current configuration.

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| I changed `analysis.cfg` — do I need to re-run anything earlier? | No. Steps 01–02 are annotation-independent; just re-run step 03 to regenerate the table. |
| What if a patient has zero source fibroblasts? | `frac_csf1pos_fib` becomes `NaN` (guarded by `where(n_fib > 0)`); the patient simply fails rule 2. |
| What if `CSF1` is missing from a patient's panel? | The script aborts with an assertion naming the patient — the shared-panel guarantee from step 01 should make this impossible. |
| Where do the excluded cells (debris, sub-threshold bins) fit in? | Those are *cell-level* filters applied in step 01 *before* inclusion; see [R Export and Tissue Pieces](7-r-export-and-tissue-pieces). |

Sources: [03_sample_table.sh](/scripts/03_sample_table.sh#L9-L17), [03_sample_table.py](/scripts/03_sample_table.py#L58-L60), [03_sample_table.py](/scripts/03_sample_table.py#L97), [03_sample_table.py](/scripts/03_sample_table.py#L66), [README.md](/README.md#L179-L183)

## Key Concepts at a Glance

The inclusion system decomposes into four cooperating pieces. The **rules** are quantitative and pre-specified (decided before looking at results — hence "pre-specified"), the **metrics** are per-patient aggregates of cell-level annotations, the **configuration** supplies the state labels that make the pipeline dataset-portable, and the **guard** in step 04 freezes the decision so downstream steps cannot drift from it.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph Inputs["Per-patient adata.h5ad (from 01/02)"]
        O1["cell_type"]
        O2["cell_state"]
        O3["nCount_Xenium"]
        O4["CSF1 raw counts"]
    end
    subgraph Config["config/analysis.cfg"]
        C1["SOURCE_STATES"]
        C2["TARGET_STATES"]
    end
    O1 & O2 & O4 --> M1["n_csf1pos_fib"]
    O1 & O2 --> M2["n_target_mac"]
    O2 & O3 --> M3["median_depth_annot"]
    C1 --> M1
    C2 --> M2
    M1 & M2 & M3 --> R{"03 rules:<br/>depth ≥ 100 ∧ csf1+ fib ≥ 50 ∧ target mac ≥ 50"}
    R -->|all pass| I["included = True → step 04"]
    R -->|any fails| X["excluded → recorded in table"]
```

| Concept | Where it lives | Beginner takeaway |
|---|---|---|
| Thresholds (100 / 50 / 50) | Constants in `03_sample_table.py` | Change them here *and* in the step-04 guard |
| State labels | `config/analysis.cfg` | Placeholders are rejected — fill in real labels |
| `included` flag | Column in `03_sample_table.csv/.xlsx` | Sorted first, smallest patient first |
| Cohort outcome (38/44) | README + step-04 `N_INCLUDED` | A hard invariant, not a soft expectation |

Sources: [03_sample_table.py](/scripts/03_sample_table.py#L51-L54), [analysis.cfg.example](/config/analysis.cfg.example#L7-L11), [04_tokenise.py](/scripts/04_tokenise.py#L60-L63), [README.md](/README.md#L53-L54)

## Where to Go Next

With the cohort now fixed at 38 patients, the natural reading order continues through the data-preparation track: [Cell-and-Neighbour Tokenisation](9-cell-and-neighbour-tokenisation) explains how each included patient is tokenised exactly once, and [Harmonisation and Model Bundles](10-harmonisation-and-model-bundles) covers the model-bundle setup that precedes it. If you want to revisit how the per-patient inputs consumed by the inclusion metrics were produced — shared gene panels and tissue pieces — return to [R Export and Tissue Pieces](7-r-export-and-tissue-pieces). For the cohort-level statistics that later exploit the deep/shallow depth batch, see [Cohort Summary Statistics](17-cohort-summary-statistics).


# Cell-and-Neighbour Tokenisation



This page is a deep dive into step 04 (`scripts/04_tokenise.py`), the stage that converts each harmonised per-patient `adata.h5ad` into TERRA-112M token sequences and freezes them as the immutable baseline of the whole perturbation analysis. It covers the **cell_graph** sequence layout, the runtime contract checks against the model bundle, piece-wise tokenisation, the derivation of the neighbour index (`nb_idx`), and the CSF1⁺ fibroblast blocks that feed downstream steps. It sits between [Patient Inclusion Rules](8-patient-inclusion-rules) (which decides *which* patients enter this stage) and [Harmonisation and Model Bundles](10-harmonisation-and-model-bundles) (which details the harmonisation call invoked here).

Sources: [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L1-L47), [README.md](README.md#L67-L71)

## Why One Tokenisation per Patient: The Determinism Invariant

The script's central design decision is stated in its own docstring: each patient is **harmonised and tokenised exactly once**, and every knockout condition in step 06 is then built by *editing those saved tokens directly* rather than re-tokenising perturbed count matrices. Two empirical observations motivated this. First, setting *CSF1* counts to zero and re-tokenising changes the tokens of non-fibroblast cells beyond those whose CSF1⁺ fibroblast neighbour blocks actually contain *CSF1* — a side effect of re-normalisation reordering genes with tied normalised expression. Second, `terra-st 0.1.13`'s `perturb_dataset` with `perturbation_target="neighborhood"` edited neighbour blocks belonging to unlisted cells, in addition to the intended edits. Tokenising once and editing tokens surgically removes both confounds, which is why the script treats its output as a canonical, versioned artefact rather than an intermediate.

Sources: [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L6-L11), [README.md](README.md#L73-L83)

This invariant also has a cohort-level corollary: because re-tokenisation would reshuffle tied genes non-deterministically, a single materialisation guarantees that the 2,816-token sequence for a given cell is byte-identical across every condition compared later. The `csf1_token` recorded here (looked up from the model's `token_dictionary.pkl` via the harmonised Ensembl ID) is the handle by which steps 05 and 06 locate *CSF1* inside raw token lists.

Sources: [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L193-L194), [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L221-L225)

## The cell_graph Sequence Contract

TERRA-112M's `cell_graph` layout represents each cell as **11 blocks × 256 tokens = 2,816 tokens**: block 0 is the cell itself, and blocks 1–10 are its ten nearest spatial neighbours, **nearest first**. Every block lists that cell's genes as integer token IDs in order of normalised expression, with no special tokens included. The script pins this layout in three module constants — `W, L_CELL, N_SEG = 2816, 256, 11` — and derives all block arithmetic (`starts = np.arange(N_SEG) * L_CELL`) from them instead of hard-coding 2816 elsewhere.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L67-L71), [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L74), [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L148-L151)

Prerequisite for reading the diagram below: a "row" here means one cell in the Hugging Face dataset produced by `tokenize_adata`, not one token; each row is one full 11-block sequence.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph ROW["One tokenised row — 11 × 256 = 2,816 tokens"]
        direction LR
        B0["Block 0<br/>own cell<br/>genes ranked by<br/>normalised expression"] --> B1["Block 1<br/>nearest neighbour"] --> B2["Block 2<br/>2nd neighbour"] --> E["…"] --> B10["Block 10<br/>10th neighbour"]
    end
    ROW --> S["tokens/  — one such row per cell of the patient"]
```

Sources: [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L23-L29), [README.md](README.md#L67-L71)

Before touching any data, the script verifies the installed model actually declares this layout, by loading `model_config.yaml` from `MODEL_DIR` and asserting five keys. A mismatch aborts the run before any expensive I/O.

| Config key | Required value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `tokenizer_type` | `cell_graph` | Sequence layout family |
| `model_input_size` | `2816` | Total sequence width `W` |
| `n_neighs` | `10` | Neighbour blocks (`N_SEG - 1`) |
| `seq_len_cell` | `256` | Per-block width `L_CELL` |
| `seq_len_neighborhood` | `2560` | `L_CELL × 10` neighbour span |

Sources: [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L184-L192)

## Stage 2: Depth Batch, One-Pass Harmonisation, and Cell Definitions

Stage 2 begins by reading `<WORK_DIR>/export/<PATIENT>/adata.h5ad` and requiring three `obs` columns — `cell_type`, `cell_state`, `sample` — to exist. It then computes the **depth batch**: the median total counts over *annotated* cells (`cell_state` not NA) classifies the patient as `deep` (≥ 500, `DEPTH_CUT`) or `shallow`; this label is stored in `meta.npz` and used later for cohort stratification. Crucially, `obs['cell_id']` is overwritten with `obs_names`, because 02 stores the raw Xenium cell ID there, which repeats across patients; a uniqueness check confirms no duplicates remain.

Sources: [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L199-L210), [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L233-L235), [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L60-L66)

Harmonisation then runs **once**, before any tokenisation, via `harmonize_adata` with `min_genes_per_cell=10, min_cells_per_gene=0`, using the model bundle's `ensembl_dictionary.pkl` and `gene_count_dictionary.pkl`. The full mechanics of gene mapping and filtering belong to [Harmonisation and Model Bundles](10-harmonisation-and-model-bundles); what matters here is the downstream dependency: *CSF1* must survive harmonisation (checked explicitly, aborting otherwise), because the CSF1 token and its raw counts anchor all cell-definition flags.

Sources: [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L212-L225)

With raw counts re-extracted as a CSR column slice, the script builds two boolean flags that gate everything downstream:

- **`is_cf_obs`** (ligand source): `cell_type == "Fibro"` **and** `cell_state ∈ SOURCE_STATES` **and** raw CSF1 count > 0.
- **`is_mac_obs`** (perturbation target): `cell_type == "Mye"` **and** `cell_state ∈ TARGET_STATES`.

Both state lists are read from `config/analysis.cfg` through `analysis_config.load_states()`, which validates that placeholders were replaced and `TARGET_STATES` has no duplicates — so this page's logic is dataset-agnostic, parameterised only by cell-state labels.

| Config key | Role in step 04 | Consumed by |
|---|---|---|
| `SOURCE_STATES` | Defines CSF1⁺ fibroblasts together with `cell_type == "Fibro"` and `CSF1 > 0` | steps 03, 04, 07 |
| `TARGET_STATES` | Defines target macrophages read out after perturbation | steps 03, 04, 07 |

Sources: [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L226-L231), [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L68-L74), [analysis_config.py](scripts/analysis_config.py#L16-L34), [analysis.cfg.example](config/analysis.cfg.example#L7-L11)

## Stage 3: Piece-Wise Tokenisation and Persistence

Tokenisation is deliberately executed **per tissue piece** (`obs['sample']`), iterating over `sorted()` piece names so row order is deterministic. This respects the piece topology established in [R Export and Tissue Pieces](7-r-export-and-tissue-pieces): spatial neighbourhoods must never bridge separate pieces, so each piece is tokenised in isolation with its own local neighbour graph. Each `tokenize_adata` call passes `add_neigh_cell_ids=True` (every token is accompanied by the cell ID of its owning block — essential for the neighbour index derived next) and `include_special_tokens=False`. A hard row-count check asserts one dataset row per cell per piece before concatenation.

Sources: [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L232), [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L240-L254), [README.md](README.md#L50-L53)

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Read adata.h5ad<br/>from 02_build_h5ad"] --> B["Depth batch:<br/>median counts of annotated cells<br/>≥ 500 → deep, else shallow"]
    B --> C["harmonize_adata — once<br/>min_genes_per_cell=10, min_cells_per_gene=0"]
    C --> D{"CSF1 survives<br/>harmonisation?"}
    D -- "no" --> Z1["abort"]
    D -- "yes" --> E["Flag CSF1+ fibroblasts<br/>and target macrophages"]
    E --> F["Per tissue piece: tokenize_adata<br/>add_neigh_cell_ids=True<br/>include_special_tokens=False"]
    F --> G["Concatenate sorted pieces<br/>→ save tokens/ (HF dataset)"]
    G --> H["Reload the saved copy<br/>delete build cache"]
    H --> I["Derive nb_idx from cell_ids<br/>+ structural checks"]
    I --> J["meta.npz + cf_blocks.npz"]
    J --> K["04_tokenise_&lt;PATIENT&gt;.xlsx<br/>summary · checks · timing"]
```

Sources: [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L181-L265)

> [!TIP]
> The dataset is **saved to disk first and then reloaded from that copy** before any index derivation. Every validation in stage 4 therefore runs against exactly the bytes step 06 will read — not the in-memory object — and the tokenisation build cache (`tok_cache/`) is deleted only after the reload succeeds. Treat this save-reload-verify order as part of the contract if you refactor the script.

The persisted artefacts, after `restore_format` re-applies the torch format to all numeric columns, are what downstream consumers receive:

| Artefact | Content | Consumer |
|---|---|---|
| `<KO_DIR>/<PATIENT>/tokens/` | Hugging Face dataset, one 2,816-token row per cell | step 06 (token editing) |
| `<KO_DIR>/<PATIENT>/meta.npz` | Row-aligned annotation + neighbour index | steps 05, 06, 07 |
| `<KO_DIR>/<PATIENT>/cf_blocks.npz` | Own 256-token block of each CSF1⁺ fibroblast | step 05 (null gene selection) |
| `<RESULTS_DIR>/04_tokenise/04_tokenise_<PATIENT>.xlsx` | `summary`, `checks`, `timing` sheets | human review |

Sources: [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L127-L130), [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L37-L44)

## Stage 4: Neighbour Index Derivation and Structural Validation

Stage 4 converts the flat 2,816-wide sequences back into a structured **neighbour index**. `gene_tokens` is flattened into an `(n, 2816)` int32 matrix via batched Arrow iteration (`read_list_column`), then reshaped to `(n, 11, 256)`. The companion `cell_ids` column — which repeats one ID per block, 2,816 times per row — is read cheaply by sampling only the *first and last* ID of each 256-token block and requiring them to agree; any disagreement means a misaligned block and the run aborts.

Sources: [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L133-L166), [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L277-L279)

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    DS["tokens/ row<br/>gene_tokens: 2,816 ids<br/>cell_ids: 2,816 ids (1 per token)"] --> F["read_block_ids:<br/>take first + last id of each 256-token block"]
    F --> C{"start id == end id<br/>within every block?"}
    C -- "no" --> X["abort: misaligned block"]
    C -- "yes" --> M["blk_ids: (n, 11) cell ids"]
    M --> N["pd.Index.get_indexer<br/>map each id to a row position"]
    N --> NB["nb_idx: (n, 11) int32"]
    NB --> V{"nb_idx[:, 0] == arange(n)?"}
    V -- "no" --> X2["abort: block 0 is not the own cell"]
    V -- "yes" --> OK["write meta.npz"]
```

Sources: [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L270-L285)

The result, `nb_idx`, is an `(n, 11)` integer matrix where `nb_idx[i, k]` is the **row position** of the cell occupying block *k* of row *i* — a positional index into the concatenated dataset order, not into the original AnnData. Two invariants are asserted before it is trusted: every block ID must resolve to a dataset row, and `nb_idx[:, 0]` must equal `arange(n)`, i.e. **block 0 is always the row's own cell**. If any check fails, the script logs it to the `checks` sheet and exits non-zero, blocking the patient from downstream steps.

| Check | Assertion | On failure |
|---|---|---|
| `cell_id unique` | zero duplicated IDs after patient-prefixing | abort via non-zero exit |
| `cell_ids constant within every block` | first ID == last ID per block | non-zero exit |
| `all block ids resolve to rows` | no `nb_idx` entry is `-1` | non-zero exit |
| `block 0 is the row's own cell` | `nb_idx[:, 0] == arange(n)` | non-zero exit |
| `cells removed by harmonisation` | informational report only | always passes |

Sources: [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L280-L285), [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L99-L103), [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L342-L346)

> [!TIP]
> `nb_idx` is the linchpin for everything downstream: step 06 uses it to locate which neighbour blocks belong to a CSF1⁺ fibroblast (so token edits land only where intended), and the per-macrophage statistics in stage 4 (`mac_cf`, `mac_csf1`) are computed by gathering flags through `nb_idx[:, 1:]`. If you change piece ordering or concatenate pieces differently, `nb_idx` rows move with the dataset — never re-derive it against a differently ordered copy.

Finally, everything row-aligned is persisted to `meta.npz`, together with gene-level lookup tables (`var_symbol`, `var_ensembl`, `var_token`) that let steps 05/06 translate gene symbols ↔ Ensembl IDs ↔ token IDs without re-reading the model dictionary:

| Field | Type/shape | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `cell_id`, `piece`, `cell_type`, `cell_state` | object arrays, `(n,)` | row-aligned annotation |
| `is_cf`, `is_mac`, `is_mye` | bool, `(n,)` | CSF1⁺ fibroblast / target macrophage / myeloid flags |
| `nb_idx` | int32, `(n, 11)` | block → row-position neighbour index |
| `csf1_raw` | float32, `(n,)` | raw CSF1 counts per cell |
| `csf1_token` | int64 scalar | token ID for *CSF1* |
| `var_symbol`, `var_ensembl`, `var_token` | object/int64, `(n_genes,)` | gene lookup tables |
| `depth_median`, `depth_batch` | float64 / str | cohort stratification inputs |

Sources: [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L300-L312)

## CSF1⁺ Fibroblast Blocks: The Bridge to Null-Gene Selection

Stage 4 also extracts `cf_blocks` — the **own block (block 0) only** of every CSF1⁺ fibroblast, i.e. exactly the 256 tokens in which a candidate null gene must be present with a rank comparable to *CSF1* — and stores them in `cf_blocks.npz` alongside the corresponding cell IDs. This is the complete interface to [Rank-Matched Null Gene Selection](12-rank-matched-null-gene-selection): step 05 never re-reads the token dataset, only this compact matrix. Summary statistics computed here for the workbook (fraction of CSF1⁺ fibroblasts whose own block contains *CSF1*, count of target macrophages having a CSF1⁺ fibroblast neighbour, and of those, whether any neighbour block actually contains *CSF1*) quantify how much of the perturbation signal is even representable in the token space — a direct consequence of the 256-token truncation caveat discussed in [Limitations and Caveats](21-limitations-and-caveats).

Sources: [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L287-L298), [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L313-L314), [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L322-L333)

## Orchestration: Array Execution, Patient Selection, and Skip Logic

Execution is an SGE array job — `-t 1-38` matches the 38 included patients — running on CPU inside the TERRA container (`tx python`) with 64 GB memory and a 6-hour wall clock, and `require_avx` guards the node. Patient identity comes either from `SGE_TASK_ID` (indexing the sorted included list) or a `PATIENT=<id>` override; the included set is computed as all `export/<PATIENT>/` directories minus six hard-coded exclusions (`P10`, `P23` for depth < 100; `P71`, `P87`, `P89`, `P93` for < 50 CSF1⁺ fibroblasts — the same rules documented in [Patient Inclusion Rules](8-patient-inclusion-rules)), and the script **stops unless exactly 38 remain**, making silent cohort drift impossible.

Sources: [04_tokenise.sh](scripts/04_tokenise.sh#L1-L21), [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L106-L124), [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L60-L64)

Caching follows the repository-wide pattern described in [Reproducibility and Caching](19-reproducibility-and-caching): with `FORCE_REBUILD = False`, a patient is skipped when all four outputs exist (`tokens/dataset_info.json`, `meta.npz`, `cf_blocks.npz`, and the summary workbook). The stage writes an unformatted `.xlsx` with three sheets — `summary` (cell counts, depth batch, CSF1⁺/target counts), `checks` (every assertion with value/expected/pass), and `timing` (per-stage seconds) — and a non-zero exit code if any check failed, so downstream job chaining in [Cluster Execution and Job Chaining](18-cluster-execution-and-job-chaining) can react to structural failures rather than only crashes.

Sources: [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L169-L179), [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L320-L346), [README.md](README.md#L179-L183)

## Where This Fits in the Pipeline

Step 04 produces the frozen token substrate on which the perturbation framework operates: the neighbour blocks identified by `nb_idx` are what [Token-Level Knockout Editing](11-token-level-knockout-editing) edits in place, the fibroblast blocks define the search space for [Rank-Matched Null Gene Selection](12-rank-matched-null-gene-selection), and the depth batch recorded in `meta.npz` stratifies the cohort summaries in [Cohort Summary Statistics](17-cohort-summary-statistics). To understand the harmonisation call consumed in stage 2, continue to [Harmonisation and Model Bundles](10-harmonisation-and-model-bundles).


# Harmonisation and Model Bundles



This page explains how the pipeline bridges the gap between exported Xenium data and the pretrained **TERRA-112M** foundation model. Two mechanisms do this: *harmonisation*, which maps the study's gene panel onto the model's Ensembl-based vocabulary, and the *model bundle*, a directory of dictionaries, a data configuration, and weights that both step 04 (tokenisation, CPU) and step 06 (embedding, GPU) read from a single location (`MODEL_DIR`). Harmonisation runs exactly once per patient inside step 04; the bundle is referenced read-only by every later stage. This page covers the bundle's anatomy, its runtime validation contract, harmonisation semantics, and token resolution. It does not cover the token sequence layout itself — see [Cell-and-Neighbour Tokenisation](9-cell-and-neighbour-tokenisation) — nor how those tokens are edited, which is [Token-Level Knockout Editing](11-token-level-knockout-editing).

Sources: [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L7-L29), [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L37-L46)

## Why Harmonise Exactly Once

Step 04 harmonises and tokenises each patient **once**, so that every knockout built in step 06 is constructed at token level from the *same* baseline sequences. The docstring is explicit about the failure mode this avoids: re-tokenisation reshuffles tied genes, meaning a baseline re-tokenised after an edit would no longer correspond row-for-row with the original baseline embeddings. Freezing the harmonised, tokenised baseline is therefore a precondition for the condition-vs-baseline comparison design used throughout the perturbation framework.

Sources: [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L7-L9), [README.md](README.md#L68-L72)

Before harmonisation, the script also computes the patient's **depth batch** on the raw shared panel: the median total counts of annotated cells (those with a non-missing `cell_state`), classified as `"deep"` if ≥ 500 (`DEPTH_CUT`) and `"shallow"` otherwise. This value is measured *before* harmonisation by design, stored in `meta.npz`, written to the summary workbook, and later used by step 07 to stratify results. Note that this classification is a study-design stratum, not a bundle property.

Sources: [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L18-L20), [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L64), [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L206-L209), [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L311-L312), [README.md](README.md#L62-L64)

## Anatomy of the Model Bundle

The bundle lives at `MODEL_DIR`, an environment variable set by `env/terra_env.sh` (which sources `config/paths.cfg`); the repository's `paths.cfg.example` documents that `SOFTWARE_DIR` holds the "Container image, Python packages installed into it, model weights, caches". The weights themselves are downloaded from Hugging Face by `env/install.sh` and are **not redistributed** with this repository — the README pins the software environment to `terra-st` 0.1.13 and TERRA-112M at Hugging Face revision `00d1c977`, and warns that TERRA's interface may change on publication.

Sources: [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L59), [paths.cfg.example](config/paths.cfg.example#L19-L20), [README.md](README.md#L12-L14), [README.md](README.md#L43-L44)

Four files in the bundle are read by name in step 04, plus the weights in step 06:

| Bundle file | Role | Consumer |
|---|---|---|
| `model_config.yaml` | Data configuration; its `data` section defines the input layout | Step 04 validation gate |
| `token_dictionary.pkl` | Maps `ensembl_id` → integer token id | Step 04 (CSF1 token, per-gene `var_token` table) |
| `ensembl_dictionary.pkl` | Gene mapping dictionary: panel genes → model vocabulary | `harmonize_adata` |
| `gene_count_dictionary.pkl` | Gene occurrence counts used during mapping | `harmonize_adata` |
| Model weights | TERRA-112M parameters | `embed_dataset` in step 06 |

Sources: [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L185-L194), [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L212-L216), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L198-L199)

## The Layout Contract: Validating the Bundle Before Use

Step 04 opens `model_config.yaml`, reads its `data` section, and checks five keys against the constants hard-coded at the top of the script (`W, L_CELL, N_SEG = 2816, 256, 11`): `tokenizer_type` must be `"cell_graph"`, `model_input_size` must be 2816, `n_neighs` must be 10, `seq_len_cell` must be 256, and `seq_len_neighborhood` must be 2560. If any check fails, the script exits with *"Model config does not match the 11 x 256 cell_graph layout"* — nothing downstream runs against an incompatible bundle. Only after the gate passes is `token_dictionary.pkl` loaded into memory.

> [!TIP]
> The five-key gate converts bundle compatibility from an implicit assumption into an explicit runtime contract. Because the repository hard-codes `W/L_CELL/N_SEG` while TERRA "is under active development and its interface may change", upgrading the bundle requires confirming these keys still match — the gate is your first line of defence against a silently incompatible model version.

Sources: [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L74), [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L185-L194), [README.md](README.md#L12-L14)

## Harmonisation in Practice

The harmonisation call is a single invocation per patient:

```python
adata_h = harmonize_adata(
    adata,
    gene_mapping_dict_file_path=str(MODEL / "ensembl_dictionary.pkl"),
    gene_occurrence_count_file_path=str(MODEL / "gene_count_dictionary.pkl"),
    min_genes_per_cell=10, min_cells_per_gene=0)
```

Its parameters have deliberate semantics: `min_genes_per_cell=10` drops cells with too few genes surviving the vocabulary mapping, while `min_cells_per_gene=0` means **no gene is removed for being rare** — the entire shared panel is preserved. Immediately after the call, the pre-harmonisation object is deleted (`del adata`), and `obs["cell_id"]` is set from `obs_names` (`"<patient>_<xenium id>"`). The number of cells removed by harmonisation is recorded as a report check in the summary workbook rather than enforced as a threshold.

| Parameter | Value | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `min_genes_per_cell` | 10 | Cells with fewer mapped genes are filtered out |
| `min_cells_per_gene` | 0 | Panel is kept intact; no gene dropped for low occurrence |
| `gene_mapping_dict_file_path` | `ensembl_dictionary.pkl` | Aligns panel symbols with the model's Ensembl vocabulary |
| `gene_occurrence_count_file_path` | `gene_count_dictionary.pkl` | Occurrence statistics consulted during mapping |

Sources: [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L210), [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L212-L217), [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L233-L235)

> [!TIP]
> `min_cells_per_gene=0` is not a loose setting — it is what keeps token positions stable. If harmonisation dropped panel genes per patient, the column indexing used for edits in step 06 would drift between patients. The script enforces the one gene that absolutely must survive with a hard exit: if `"CSF1"` is not in `adata_h.var_names`, it aborts with *"CSF1 removed by harmonisation"*, because the entire knockout design depends on resolving CSF1's token.

Sources: [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L212-L216), [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L221-L222)

## Resolving Tokens: Symbol → Ensembl → Token ID

Harmonisation attaches an `ensembl_id` column to `adata.var`, and the token dictionary completes the chain. For the perturbation target this is explicit: the script locates CSF1's column, reads `adata_h.var.loc["CSF1", "ensembl_id"]`, and looks up `token_dict[csf1_ens]` to obtain the integer token used by every knockout condition in step 06. For the whole panel, three parallel arrays are built — `var_symbol`, `var_ensembl`, and `var_token` (using `token_dict.get(e, -1)`, so unmapped genes carry a `-1` sentinel) — and all three are persisted in `meta.npz` alongside `csf1_token`.

Sources: [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L223-L225), [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L300-L302), [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L304-L312)

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["var_names: CSF1"] -->|"adata_h.var.loc"| B["ensembl_id"]
    B -->|"token_dictionary.pkl"| C["integer token id"]
    C --> D["meta.npz: csf1_token<br/>and per-gene var_token"]
    D --> E["step 05: null genes<br/>carry a token column"]
    D --> F["step 06: CSF1_remove,<br/>CSF1_zero, NULL_gene"]
```

Persisting the token table matters for reproducibility: downstream steps never re-open the bundle to resolve genes. Step 06 loads the null-gene table produced by step 05 and finds each null gene's token already materialised as a `token` column, then constructs all conditions (`CSF1_remove`, `CSF1_zero`, `POS_block`, twenty `NULL_<gene>` conditions) from `csf1_token` in `meta.npz` and those precomputed tokens.

Sources: [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L240), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L251-L256)

## Tokenising Against the Bundle and Freezing the Baseline

With harmonisation done, `tokenize_adata` runs per tissue piece (`obs["sample"]`, sorted), passing `model_folder_path=str(MODEL)` so the tokenizer reads its vocabulary from the same bundle, with `add_neigh_cell_ids=True` and `include_special_tokens=False`. The per-piece datasets are concatenated and saved to `<KO_DIR>/<PATIENT>/tokens/`. The script then deletes its build cache, reloads the dataset *from the saved copy*, and works from that — the exact artifact step 06 will read — so the baseline sequences are frozen on disk rather than held only in memory. Hugging Face cache directories (`HF_DATASETS_CACHE`, `HF_HOME`) are redirected into the patient's working directory to keep caches colocated with the outputs.

Sources: [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L232), [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L242-L258), [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L262-L265), [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L77-L78)

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph BUNDLE["MODEL_DIR: the TERRA-112M bundle"]
        CFG["model_config.yaml<br/>data section: layout keys"]
        TD["token_dictionary.pkl<br/>ensembl_id to token id"]
        ED["ensembl_dictionary.pkl<br/>panel gene mapping"]
        GD["gene_count_dictionary.pkl<br/>gene occurrence counts"]
        WT["model weights<br/>downloaded, not in repo"]
    end
    AD["export/PATIENT/adata.h5ad<br/>from step 02"] -->|"input"| H["harmonize_adata<br/>once per patient"]
    ED -->|"mapping dictionary"| H
    GD -->|"occurrence counts"| H
    CFG -->|"5-key layout gate"| H
    H --> AH["harmonised AnnData<br/>var carries ensembl_id"]
    AH --> TK["csf1_token and<br/>var_token table"]
    TD -->|"lookup"| TK
    AH -->|"tokenize_adata per piece"| DS["tokens/ dataset<br/>11 x 256 baseline sequences"]
    DS --> E6["step 06: edit tokens then<br/>embed_dataset model_folder_path=MODEL"]
    WT --> E6
    TK --> E6
```

## Bundle Reuse at Embedding Time (Step 06)

Step 06 resolves the same `MODEL_DIR` and hands it to `embed_dataset` from `terra.inference.embed`: `embed_dataset(ds, model_folder_path=str(MODEL), batch_size=BATCH_SIZE, num_workers=NUM_WORKERS, include_spatial_cell_emb=True)`. Because embedding reads the identical bundle that produced the tokens, vocabulary and layout are guaranteed consistent between baseline and perturbed sequences — this is why the same `model_folder_path` argument appears in both steps. The call returns three embedding kinds checked for one row per sequence: `spatial_cell_emb` (primary readout), `neighborhood_emb` (secondary), and `cell_emb` (negative control). The batch size of 256 is kept fixed so every patient is embedded identically.

Sources: [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L64), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L68), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L82), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L194-L207)

The two steps use the same bundle on very different hardware, which the job scripts make explicit:

| Aspect | Step 04 — tokenise | Step 06 — embed |
|---|---|---|
| Bundle artifacts used | Both harmonisation dictionaries, token dictionary, config | Weights (via `embed_dataset`) + config expectations |
| Hardware | CPU-only, in the TERRA container, 64 GB RAM requested | GPU array job; needs a card with ≥ 40 GB (batch 256 ≈ 21 GB + CUDA overhead) |
| Container runner | `tx python` | `txg python` (GPU-enabled environment) |
| Bundle-derived outputs | `tokens/`, `meta.npz`, `cf_blocks.npz` | `emb_ko.npz` |

Sources: [04_tokenise.sh](scripts/04_tokenise.sh#L6), [04_tokenise.sh](scripts/04_tokenise.sh#L10), [04_tokenise.sh](scripts/04_tokenise.sh#L17), [04_tokenise.sh](scripts/04_tokenise.sh#L20), [06_ko_embed.sh](scripts/06_ko_embed.sh#L8), [06_ko_embed.sh](scripts/06_ko_embed.sh#L12-L14), [06_ko_embed.sh](scripts/06_ko_embed.sh#L26)

## Where the Harmonised Artifacts Flow

Step 04's outputs carry the bundle's influence forward without requiring the bundle again for gene resolution: the tokenised dataset (`tokens/`) holds the frozen 11×256 baseline sequences; `meta.npz` holds the per-row annotation, neighbour index, depth batch, and the `var_symbol`/`var_ensembl`/`var_token` table; `cf_blocks.npz` holds each CSF1+ fibroblast's own 256-token block. Step 06 reads the first two plus the null-gene table, and writes `emb_ko.npz` for step 07. In catalog terms: the token blocks feed [Token-Level Knockout Editing](11-token-level-knockout-editing), `cf_blocks.npz` feeds [Rank-Matched Null Gene Selection](12-rank-matched-null-gene-selection), and the embeddings feed [Embedding Shift Magnitudes](16-embedding-shift-magnitudes) and the [Leave-One-Donor-Out Classifier](15-leave-one-donor-out-classifier), with `depth_batch` used for stratification in [Cohort Summary Statistics](17-cohort-summary-statistics).

Sources: [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L37-L42), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L41-L45)

## Where to Go Next

Upstream, [Cell-and-Neighbour Tokenisation](9-cell-and-neighbour-tokenisation) details the 11×256 `cell_graph` sequences this page's validated bundle produces, and [Patient Inclusion Rules](8-patient-inclusion-rules) explains which patients reach step 04 at all. Configuration of `MODEL_DIR` and the other paths is covered in [Configuration Setup](4-configuration-setup). Downstream, the natural continuation is [Token-Level Knockout Editing](11-token-level-knockout-editing), which consumes the frozen baseline sequences against the CSF1 token resolved here; [Rank-Matched Null Gene Selection](12-rank-matched-null-gene-selection) shows how the `cf_blocks.npz` artifact drives control-gene choice. For cache and skip behaviour around these steps, see [Reproducibility and Caching](19-reproducibility-and-caching).


# Token-Level Knockout Editing



This page explains how `06_ko_embed.py` — the heart of the perturbation framework — constructs every in silico knockout directly on TERRA token sequences and embeds the target macrophages with TERRA-112M. It covers the rationale for token-level editing, the exact edit surface, the 23-condition matrix, the compaction algorithm behind gene removal, the embedding protocol, the in-script verification contract, the artifacts it produces, and how to run it as a GPU array job. Pooling and statistics are deliberately out of scope here — they live in step 07 and are documented in the readouts pages.

## Why Perturbation Happens at the Token Level

The pipeline tokenises each of the 38 included patients exactly once (step 04) and never re-tokenises. Every knockout is manufactured by editing the stored `gene_tokens` / `gene_expr` arrays of the baseline sequences in place, then re-embedding. This is a deliberate architectural decision, motivated by two observed failure modes of the alternatives: setting *CSF1* counts to zero and re-tokenising changes tokens in non-fibroblast cells far beyond the intended CSF1+ fibroblast neighbour blocks (re-tokenisation and re-normalisation reshuffle tied genes and leak the edit outward), and `terra-st 0.1.13`'s `perturb_dataset` with `perturbation_target="neighborhood"` was observed to also edit neighbour blocks belonging to unlisted cells. Direct token editing sidesteps both: the edit is provably confined, because the code itself asserts the confinement (see the verification contract below).

Sources: [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L6-L12), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L8-L18), [README.md](README.md#L67-L83)

## The Edit Surface: 11 Blocks, 10 Editable

To read the editing code you first need TERRA's `cell_graph` layout: each sequence is 2,816 tokens organised as 11 blocks of 256 — block 0 holds the macrophage's own genes, blocks 1–10 hold its 10 nearest neighbours in nearest-first order, each block listing that cell's genes by normalised expression rank. The editor operates on reshaped **views** of this structure (`tok.reshape(n, 11, 256)[:, 1:, :]`), which is what makes "skip block 0, address blocks 1–10" a one-slice operation rather than index arithmetic over a flat array.

The edit surface is further masked by cell identity, not just position. For each target macrophage, the boolean matrix `blk = is_cf[nb_idx[t_rows, 1:]]` (shape: targets × 10) marks exactly which neighbour blocks belong to a CSF1+ fibroblast. A cell is *edited by a condition* if and only if at least one of its CSF1+ fibroblast neighbour blocks contains the condition's gene; `n_edit` counts those blocks per cell and per condition, and becomes a covariate in downstream analysis. The macrophage's own block and every non-CSF1+ fibroblast neighbour block are never touched, under any condition.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    B0["block 0<br>macrophage own genes<br>never edited"] --> B1["block 1<br>nearest neighbour<br>editable iff CSF1+ fibro"] --> B2["block 2<br>2nd nearest<br>same rule"] --> B9["blocks 3-10<br>same rule"] --> B10["block 10<br>10th nearest<br>same rule"]
    style B0 fill:#eeeeee,stroke:#999999
    style B1 fill:#ffd9d9,stroke:#cc0000
    style B2 fill:#ffd9d9,stroke:#cc0000
    style B9 fill:#ffd9d9,stroke:#cc0000
    style B10 fill:#ffd9d9,stroke:#cc0000
```

Red blocks are the candidate edit surface; a red block is actually edited only when it belongs to a CSF1+ fibroblast *and* contains the condition's gene (for `POS_block`: membership alone suffices).

Sources: [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L26-L30), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L147-L157), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L243-L249), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L21-L26)

## The Condition Matrix: 23 Conditions Per Patient

Step 06 builds 23 conditions: three hand-specified plus one per null gene. The condition list is constructed as a table of `(name, token, mode)` triples, where `token = None` signals "whole block" and `mode` selects the edit algorithm. All conditions are applied to the **same** target rows in the **same** order.

| Condition | Count | Edit per eligible CSF1+ fibroblast block | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CSF1_remove` | 1 | CSF1 token **and** value removed; remaining tokens compact upward | Main knockout — the perturbation of interest |
| `CSF1_zero` | 1 | CSF1 value set to 0; token kept in place | Encoding-sensitivity probe |
| `NULL_<gene>` | 20 | Same removal algorithm, applied to the null gene's token | Reference distribution at the same positions |
| `POS_block` | 1 | Entire block emptied — every non-zero token and value zeroed, compacted to pure padding | Positive control: maximal neighbourhood edit |

`POS_block` reuses the removal machinery with `token=None`: the selection becomes `blk & (nt != 0)` — every real token in the block — so the block ends up indistinguishable from a neighbour with no detected genes. The null genes arrive from step 05 as a 20-row TSV (`symbol`, `token`) and are validated (`len(null) == 20`) before use; their selection methodology is the subject of [Rank-Matched Null Gene Selection](12-rank-matched-null-gene-selection), and the design logic behind the full control set is covered in [Control Conditions Design](13-control-conditions-design) and [Null-Gene Control Rationale](14-null-gene-control-rationale).

Sources: [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L251-L256), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L21-L26), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L240-L241), [README.md](README.md#L85-L91)

## Inside `apply_edit`: Removal as Stable Compaction

`apply_edit(tok, expr, blk, token, mode)` is the single function through which all 23 conditions flow, which guarantees algorithmic uniformity. Its mechanics, in order: reshape both token and expression arrays to views of shape `(n, 11, 256)` and slice off block 0; build the boolean selection (`blk[:, :, None] & (nt == token)` for gene-targeted conditions, `blk[:, :, None] & (nt != 0)` for `POS_block`); reduce with `any(axis=2)` to get `edited_blk`, the per-row set of touched blocks. Then the mode diverges:

| Aspect | mode `"zero"` | mode `"remove"` |
|---|---|---|
| Token slot | Kept at original position | Set to 0 |
| Value slot | Set to 0.0 | Set to 0.0 |
| Block length | Unchanged | Remaining tokens compact up; zero-padding grows at the end |
| Ordering effect | None | Preserves relative gene order (stable sort), padding forced to suffix |
| Used by | `CSF1_zero` | `CSF1_remove`, all `NULL_<gene>`, `POS_block` |

The compaction in `"remove"` mode is a three-line vectorised idiom worth studying: for each edited (row, block) pair, `order = np.argsort(sub_t == 0, axis=1, kind="stable")` sorts positions by "is padding" ascending — a **stable** sort, so real tokens keep their original relative order (their expression-rank order from tokenisation) while zeros sink to the end — and `np.take_along_axis` applies the permutation to both token and value arrays simultaneously. This is what keeps the invariant "padding is always a suffix of each block" true, which the padding check later verifies explicitly.

> [!TIP]
> The `kind="stable"` argument is not cosmetic. With a non-stable sort, surviving genes could be permuted within the block, silently changing their positional encoding and conflating "gene removed" with "gene order changed" — precisely the confound the token-level design exists to avoid.

Sources: [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L147-L177), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L290-L295)

## Embedding Discipline: Identical Batches Across Conditions

The embedding protocol has two distinct passes. The **baseline** pass embeds *every Mye cell of the patient* — this is the classifier training set consumed by step 07, not just the targets. The **perturbed** pass embeds only the target macrophages, once for baseline and once per condition, always the same rows in the same order. Row-order invariance is what makes cell-by-cell comparison across conditions valid: since targets occupy identical positions in every pass, fixed batch size 256 produces identical batching composition everywhere, so any embedding difference is attributable to the edit alone — never to batch assembly.

Two implementation details protect numeric integrity in the HF `datasets` plumbing. First, `subset()` strips the dataset format (`with_format(None)`) before `select`/`flatten_indices`, because flattening a torch-formatted dataset re-encodes values through the formatter and loses precision. Second, `replace_arrays()` re-injects edited arrays via a batched `map` with `with_indices=True`, `keep_in_memory=True`, and `load_from_cache_file=False` — the last flag prevents HF's caching layer from serving stale pre-edit columns under the same fingerprint. The embedding call itself delegates to `terra.inference.embed.embed_dataset` (TERRA-112M from `MODEL_DIR`, `include_spatial_cell_emb=True`), collecting three readouts per row: `spatial_cell_emb` (primary), `neighborhood_emb` (secondary), and `cell_emb`, which is retained purely as a negative control — a neighbourhood edit cannot change it, so it doubles as a leak detector.

> [!TIP]
> The `cell_emb` negative control is the cheapest falsification test in the pipeline: since block 0 is provably untouched, any nonzero deviation in `cell_emb` would indicate state leakage through the datasets cache or an edit that escaped its slice. The < 1e-4 threshold on max absolute deviation turns that into a hard pass/fail gate.

Sources: [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L28-L34), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L119-L131), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L180-L207), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L261-L266), [README.md](README.md#L99-L110)

## The Verification Contract

Every run records a battery of named checks (via the `check()` helper, which logs and accumulates them) and **exits with code 1 if any fails** — a failed check invalidates the patient's outputs for the array. The contract covers input integrity, edit confinement, and model-interface sanity:

| Check | Asserts |
|---|---|
| tokens/meta row alignment | `tokens` dataset and `meta.npz` have identical row count and cell-id order |
| null genes | exactly 20 rows in the step 05 TSV |
| targets are Mye cells | target rows are a subset of Mye rows (`searchsorted` membership proof) |
