| own block purity | no padding token appears before a real token in block 0 of targets |
| changed == edited (per condition) | exactly the cells with `n_edit > 0` changed, no others |
| confinement (per condition) | every token/value difference lies inside an edited neighbour block |
| padding suffix (per condition) | within each edited block, zeros form a contiguous suffix |
| `cell_emb` invariance (per condition) | max abs deviation from baseline < 1e-4 |
| one row per sequence | each embedding array has exactly `len(ds)` rows |

The confinement and padding checks deserve emphasis: they are executed *per condition* on the full target matrix, converting the design claim ("only CSF1+ fibroblast neighbour blocks are touched") into a machine-verified property of every artifact the step emits.

Sources: [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L91-L96), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L229-L241), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L267-L269), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L283-L300), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L353-L357)

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    T["04_tokenise outputs<br>KO_DIR/P/tokens + meta.npz"] --> L["Load and align rows<br>csf1_token, is_cf, is_mac, is_mye, nb_idx"]
    N["05_null_genes.tsv<br>20 rank-matched genes"] --> L
    L --> B["blk = is_cf[nb_idx targets, 1:]<br>edit-surface mask"]
    B --> E["apply_edit x 23 conditions<br>remove / zero modes"]
    E --> R["replace_arrays<br>gene_tokens / gene_expr swapped in"]
    R --> M["embed_dataset<br>TERRA-112M, batch 256"]
    M --> C{"check battery"}
    C -->|"all pass"| O["emb_ko.npz + 06_ko_embed_P.xlsx"]
    C -->|"any fail"| X["sys.exit 1"]
```

The diagram shows the module-level data flow of one array task: two upstream artifacts, one mask computation, one edit function applied 23 times, one embedding call per pass, and a gate that decides whether outputs are emitted at all.

Sources: [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L216-L256), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L261-L331)

## Outputs and Interfaces

Step 06 writes two artifacts per patient, both required for the skip logic. **`<KO_DIR>/<P>/emb_ko.npz`** is the machine interface consumed by step 07; **`<RESULTS_DIR>/06_ko_embed_<P>.xlsx`** is the human audit interface, written unformatted (the script suppresses pandas' Excel header styling) with one sheet per concern.

| `emb_ko.npz` key group | Content |
|---|---|
| `patient`, `depth_batch` | Run identity and the depth batch covariate from step 04 |
| `mye_cell_id`, `mye_state`, `base_mye_spatial/neigh/cell` | All macrophages + baseline embeddings (classifier training set for 07) |
| `t_in_mye`, `t_cell_id`, `t_state` | Target indices into the Mye rows, plus identity and state |
| `n_cf_nb`, `base_t_spatial`, `base_t_neigh` | Per-target CSF1+ fibroblast neighbour count; target baseline embeddings |
| `cond_names`, `n_edit` | The 23 condition names; edited-block counts (targets × 23) |
| `cond_spatial`, `cond_neigh` | Perturbed embeddings, `(23, n_targets, dim)` |

The workbook carries `parameters`, `checks`, `negative_control_cell_emb` (the `cell_emb` deviations), `per_cell`, `timing`, and `gpu_memory` sheets. The `per_cell` sheet is where per-cell effect sizes first materialise: for each target and each condition it records `n_edit_<condition>` and the cosine shift against baseline, computed as `1 − cos(spatial)  = 1 − Σ(x̂·ŷ)` for both the spatial and neighbourhood embeddings. Interpretation of these shifts — how they're pooled, tested, and ranked across donors — belongs to [Embedding Shift Magnitudes](16-embedding-shift-magnitudes) and [Cohort Summary Statistics](17-cohort-summary-statistics); step 07 itself is introduced in [Leave-One-Donor-Out Classifier](15-leave-one-donor-out-classifier).

Sources: [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L41-L45), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L210-L213), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L304-L331), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L342-L352)

## Executing Step 06 on the Cluster

The shell wrapper `06_ko_embed.sh` submits an SGE array of 38 tasks (`-t 1-38`, concurrency `-tc 8`), one patient per task. Each task selects its patient as index `SGE_TASK_ID` into the sorted list of the 38 included patients; `PATIENT=<id>` overrides this and is validated against the included set. Both artifacts' existence triggers a skip unless `FORCE_REBUILD = True`, which is how the documented workflow — run patient P12 alone, inspect its log, then submit the full array — avoids recomputation. Chaining from step 05 is mandatory in practice: the null-gene TSV is a hard input. Full job-chain wiring is covered in [Cluster Execution and Job Chaining](18-cluster-execution-and-job-chaining).

| Resource / parameter | Value | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| GPU memory | >= 40 GB card | Batch 256 needs ~21 GB + CUDA overhead; fails on 24 GB cards |
| Batch size | 256, fixed | Held constant so every patient is embedded identically |
| `h_rt` / memory | 03:00:00 / `tmem=32G`, `h_vmem=200G` | Per-task envelope, adapt names to your scheduler |
| Node type | GPU, inside TERRA container, `require_avx` | `terra_env.sh` supplies all paths and `MODEL_DIR` |
| DataLoader workers | `NSLOTS` (default 1) | Fed to `embed_dataset` as `num_workers` |

Sources: [06_ko_embed.sh](scripts/06_ko_embed.sh#L6-L18), [06_ko_embed.sh](scripts/06_ko_embed.sh#L21-L27), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L47-L51), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L98-L116), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L216-L224), [README.md](README.md#L211-L221)

## Position in the Pipeline

Upstream, this step consumes the frozen token sequences and neighbour indices from [Cell-and-Neighbour Tokenisation](9-cell-and-neighbour-tokenisation) and the null-gene set from [Rank-Matched Null Gene Selection](12-rank-matched-null-gene-selection). Downstream, everything it emits flows into the readouts. If you want to understand *why* each of the 23 conditions exists before reading the statistics, continue to [Control Conditions Design](13-control-conditions-design); to see what the embeddings become, continue to [Leave-One-Donor-Out Classifier](15-leave-one-donor-out-classifier).


# Rank-Matched Null Gene Selection



This page documents step 05 of the pipeline (`scripts/05_null_genes.py`), the point in the perturbation framework where the **negative controls for the in silico knockout are fixed**. Before any perturbation is computed, the script selects 20 *null genes* — genes that are not CSF1 and carry no established macrophage signal, but whose visibility inside the model's context is statistically indistinguishable from CSF1's. It is a single, cohort-level job: one run covers all 38 patients and produces one artifact that every per-patient task in step 06 later consumes. The selection rule was fixed before any knockout result was seen, which is what makes the nulls usable as a pre-registered reference distribution.

Sources: [05_null_genes.py](scripts/05_null_genes.py#L1-L37), [README.md](README.md#L93-L97)

## Role in the Perturbation Framework

Step 05 sits at the boundary between data preparation and perturbation. It reads only frozen outputs of step 04 — the own 256-token block of every CSF1+ fibroblast (`cf_blocks.npz`), the harmonised panel metadata (`meta.npz`), and the per-patient 04 summary sheets — and it never touches the model. Because it must summarise the *whole cohort*, it runs as one CPU-only SGE job that is chained behind every 04 array task via `-hold_jid tlp_04_tokenise`, requesting 16 GB RAM and one hour. Its outputs are a six-sheet audit workbook and a machine-readable TSV that step 06 reads to build the `NULL_*` knockout conditions.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph S04["Step 04 · tokenise — per patient, ×38"]
        B["meta.npz<br/>panel symbol/ensembl/token · csf1_token"] --- C["cf_blocks.npz<br/>own 256-token block of each CSF1+ fibroblast"]
    end
    subgraph S05["Step 05 · null genes — one cohort job, CPU"]
        D["pool all blocks:<br/>n_cf × 256 matrix"]
        E["presence + median rank<br/>per gene over the cohort"]
        F["band filters ·<br/>ligand exclusion ·<br/>seeded draw of 20"]
    end
    subgraph S06["Step 06 · ko_embed — per patient, GPU"]
        G["NULL_ conditions ×20<br/>same remove-edit, same CSF1+ fibroblast blocks"]
    end
    C --> D
    B --> D
    D --> E --> F
    F -- "05_null_genes.tsv" --> G
```

The cohort definition is inherited, not re-derived: the script rediscovers patient directories, excludes the same six patients removed in step 03, and hard-asserts that exactly 38 remain before doing any work.

Sources: [05_null_genes.py](scripts/05_null_genes.py#L28-L36), [05_null_genes.py](scripts/05_null_genes.py#L63-L73), [05_null_genes.sh](scripts/05_null_genes.sh#L1-L17), [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L8-L10)

## The Matching Statistics and Bands

A null gene must be *seen by the model in the same blocks as CSF1, about as often, and at about the same rank*. Both statistics are computed over the pooled own-blocks of all CSF1+ fibroblasts across the 38 patients. **Presence** is the fraction of CSF1+ fibroblast blocks that contain the gene at all; **median rank** is the median 1-based position of the gene within those blocks (rank 1 = highest normalised expression), computed only over blocks where the gene is present. CSF1's reference values are presence 0.66 and median rank 60, and a candidate must fall within ±0.15 presence and ±40 rank positions of those targets.

| Statistic | Definition over CSF1+ fibroblast own-blocks | CSF1 value | Tolerance for a candidate |
|---|---|---|---|
| `presence` | fraction of CSF1+ fibroblasts whose block contains the gene | 0.66 | absolute difference ≤ `PRESENCE_BAND` (0.15) |
| `median_rank` | median position (1 = highest) in the block, when present | 60 | absolute difference ≤ `RANK_BAND` (40 positions) |

| Constant | Value | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `GENE` | `"CSF1"` | test ligand whose visibility defines the match target |
| `N_NULL` | `20` | number of null genes drawn |
| `SEED` | `1234` | seed of `np.random.default_rng` for the draw |
| `RANK_BAND` | `40` | maximum rank deviation from CSF1 |
| `PRESENCE_BAND` | `0.15` | maximum presence deviation from CSF1 |
| `N_INCLUDED` | `38` | asserted cohort size |
| `EXCLUDED_LIGANDS` | 50 entries | biologically active ligands barred from the null |

Sources: [05_null_genes.py](scripts/05_null_genes.py#L12-L26), [05_null_genes.py](scripts/05_null_genes.py#L46-L59), [05_null_genes.py](scripts/05_null_genes.py#L93-L112), [README.md](README.md#L93-L97)

## The Exclusion List: Keeping Real Signal Out of the Null

Band matching alone is not enough — a gene that mimics CSF1's token statistics could still *cause* a real macrophage effect when removed, which would silently contaminate the reference distribution. The script therefore excludes 50 ligands with established direct effects on macrophage recruitment, survival, or polarisation: colony stimulating factors (`CSF1`, `IL34`, `CSF2`, `CSF3`), interleukins (`IL1A/B`, `IL4`, `IL6`, `IL10`, `IL13`, `IL18`, `IL33`), inflammatory cytokines (`TNF`, `IFNG`, `TGFB1-3`), chemokines (`CCL2-CCL22`, `CXCL8-CXCL12`, `CX3CL1`), and matrix/scar and clearance ligands (`SPP1`, `THBS1`, `GAS6`, `PROS1`, `VEGFA/FC`, `HGF`, `IGF1`, `PDGFB`, `CD47`, among others). CSF1 itself is additionally removed by name. The full list is written verbatim into the workbook so the exclusion is auditable, not folklore.

Sources: [05_null_genes.py](scripts/05_null_genes.py#L20-L22), [05_null_genes.py](scripts/05_null_genes.py#L57-L59), [05_null_genes.py](scripts/05_null_genes.py#L148-L149)

## Algorithm Walkthrough

The script is four explicit stages, and every stage ends in an assertion or an early exit rather than a silent fallback.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Stage 1 · pool cf_blocks across 38 patients<br/>assert harmonised panel identical · M = n_cf × 256"] --> B["Stage 2 · long table (token, rank 1..256)<br/>drop token 0 = padding · groupby token"]
    B --> C["presence = n_present / n_cf<br/>median_rank over present blocks<br/>merge panel symbols · sort by median_rank"]
    C --> D["Stage 3 · candidate flags:<br/>|Δrank| ≤ 40 · |Δpresence| ≤ 0.15<br/>not CSF1 · not in EXCLUDED_LIGANDS"]
    D --> E{"≥ 20 candidates?"}
    E -- "no" --> Z["sys.exit —<br/>bands are NOT widened"]
    E -- "yes" --> F["rng.choice(seed=1234), size=20,<br/>without replacement, then sorted"]
    F --> G["Stage 4 · 6-sheet xlsx audit trail<br/>+ 5-column TSV for step 06"]
```

**Stage 1 — cohort assembly.** Each patient's `cf_tokens` array is loaded and vertically stacked into one `(n CSF1+ fibroblasts, 256)` matrix; the panel mapping (symbol, ensembl, token) is loaded once from the first patient and asserted identical across all others, and the CSF1 token id is captured from `meta.npz`. This is where the per-patient 04 summaries are also collected into the cohort table (depth batch, cell counts, CSF1 visibility).

Sources: [05_null_genes.py](scripts/05_null_genes.py#L63-L91), [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L35-L39)

**Stage 2 — visibility statistics.** The pooled matrix is melted into a long `(token, rank)` table, rank positions 1–256 being broadcast per block; padding tokens (`token == 0`) are dropped before grouping. `groupby("token")` then yields `n_present`, `median_rank`, and `mean_rank`, presence is normalised by the total fibroblast count, and every surviving token is asserted to map onto a panel gene. The table is sorted by median rank and CSF1's row is extracted with an assertion that it was seen at least once in the blocks.

Sources: [05_null_genes.py](scripts/05_null_genes.py#L93-L112)

**Stage 3 — candidates and the seeded draw.** Boolean flags per gene (`in_rank_band`, `in_presence_band`, `excluded_ligand`) are combined into a single `candidate` column; candidates are sorted by symbol, and if fewer than 20 exist the script exits rather than widening the bands. Otherwise 20 genes are drawn without replacement from `np.random.default_rng(1234)` and the picked indices are re-sorted into a canonical order.

Sources: [05_null_genes.py](scripts/05_null_genes.py#L114-L130)

**Stage 4 — write-out.** The workbook records the full decision chain: `parameters` (all eleven run constants including `n_candidates` and the deep/shallow depth-batch counts, 12/26), `selected`, `candidates`, `all_genes` (every panel gene's statistics), `excluded_ligands`, and `patients`. Excel header styling is deliberately suppressed to keep the files machine-diffable. The TSV keeps only what step 06 needs.

Sources: [05_null_genes.py](scripts/05_null_genes.py#L132-L158), [README.md](README.md#L61-L63)

> [!TIP]
> Candidates are sorted by symbol *before* `rng.choice` is applied, so the selected set is a pure function of (candidate set, seed) — directory iteration order, mount order, or process scheduling cannot change the draw. Combined with the `parameters` sheet (seed + bands + `n_candidates`) and the full `candidates` sheet, anyone can re-derive the exact 20 genes from the audit workbook alone.

## Determinism and Fail-Fast Semantics

Every branch that could silently degrade control quality fails loudly instead. A missing per-patient `cf_blocks.npz` aborts the job up front; a panel mismatch between patients aborts at merge time; CSF1 never appearing in the blocks aborts at reference extraction; a token without a panel gene aborts at join time. Most importantly, the candidate shortfall is a hard `sys.exit` — the rank and presence bands are *pre-registered parameters*, and widening them after seeing a shortfall would break the "fixed before results are seen" contract stated in the module docstring.

Sources: [05_null_genes.py](scripts/05_null_genes.py#L12-L26), [05_null_genes.py](scripts/05_null_genes.py#L66-L72), [05_null_genes.py](scripts/05_null_genes.py#L104-L109), [05_null_genes.py](scripts/05_null_genes.py#L125-L126)

## The Output Contract Consumed by Step 06

Step 06 reads `05_null_genes.tsv` with a plain tab-separator parse and immediately asserts the row count is exactly 20. Each TSV row becomes one knockout condition, wired as a `(symbol, token)` pair: the condition named `NULL_<symbol>` edits the `token` value, not the symbol string. The edit itself uses the same `remove` mode as `CSF1_remove` — token and value deleted, remaining tokens of the block shifted up with stable ordering so padding stays at the end — and is applied to exactly the same neighbour blocks 1..10 that belong to CSF1+ fibroblasts. This symmetry is the entire point: the nulls are *edits of comparable size at the same positions*, differing from the test only in the gene identity.

| Contract field | Content | Consumer-side check in step 06 |
|---|---|---|
| `symbol` | null gene symbol | condition name `NULL_<symbol>` |
| `token` | harmonised panel token id | passed as the edit target token |
| `ensembl` | Ensembl id | carried for provenance/readouts |
| `presence`, `median_rank` | selection statistics | audit context for per-condition results |
| row count | exactly 20 | `check("null genes", len(null), 20, ...)` |

> [!TIP]
> The TSV carries *token ids* rather than symbols, which is only safe because stage 1 asserts the harmonised panel is byte-identical across all 38 patients — one shared token id therefore denotes the same gene everywhere in the cohort. If step 04 ever regenerates with a different bundle dictionary, step 05 and step 06 must be re-run together, never mixed.

Sources: [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L11-L19), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L18-L25), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L226-L260), [05_null_genes.py](scripts/05_null_genes.py#L151-L152)

## Where This Fits and What to Read Next

The selection answers one design question — *what is a fair negative control for removing CSF1?* — by matching model visibility (presence and rank) and excluding biological confounders. What the nulls do *not* fix is decided elsewhere in the framework: the token-level edit mechanics they reuse are specified in [Token-Level Knockout Editing](11-token-level-knockout-editing); how they sit alongside `CSF1_zero`, `POS_block`, and the `cell_emb` negative control is covered in [Control Conditions Design](13-control-conditions-design); how the null distribution is turned into a decision rule in step 07 is the subject of [Null-Gene Control Rationale](14-null-gene-control-rationale); and the reproducibility guarantees touched on here (seeded draw, cached 04 inputs) are elaborated in [Reproducibility and Caching](19-reproducibility-and-caching).


# Control Conditions Design



Every in silico perturbation in this pipeline is only as credible as the set of conditions it is compared against. This page explains the **catalogue of 23 conditions** that `06_ko_embed.py` attaches to each target macrophage — one test condition, 20 rank-matched null genes, and two standalone controls — how each is constructed from the same token sequence, and the distinct role each plays in the step 07 readout. It sits between the selection of the null genes themselves ([Rank-Matched Null Gene Selection](12-rank-matched-null-gene-selection)) and the statistical justification for gene-level controls ([Null-Gene Control Rationale](14-null-gene-control-rationale)).

The unifying constraint of the design is that **all conditions operate on the identical tokenised sequence** produced once by step 04. No condition re-tokenises, re-normalises, or re-derives its input; each is a deterministic token edit restricted to the same neighbourhood blocks, so any downstream difference between conditions is attributable to the edit itself, not to upstream variation.

Sources: [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L12-L27), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L251-L255), [README.md](README.md#L67-L71)

## The Condition Catalogue

Each target macrophage is embedded once unedited (the baseline) and once per condition. The condition list is constructed explicitly in step 06 as `(name, token, mode)` triples: `CSF1_remove` and `CSF1_zero` act on the CSF1 token, `POS_block` acts on the whole block, and the 20 `NULL_<gene>` entries are read from the cohort-level null gene table produced by step 05. The resulting 23 names are stored in `cond_names` inside each patient's `emb_ko.npz`, and step 07 verifies that every patient carries the identical list before pooling.

| Condition | Count | Token edit per CSF1+ fibroblast neighbour block | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CSF1_remove` | 1 | *CSF1* token and value removed; remaining tokens compact upward | The perturbation of interest |
| `NULL_<gene>` | 20 | Same removal semantics for a rank-matched null gene | Reference distribution for an edit of comparable size at the same positions |
| `POS_block` | 1 | Entire block emptied (all tokens and values → padding) | Positive control: proves the pipeline can detect a neighbourhood change |
| `CSF1_zero` | 1 | *CSF1* value set to 0, token kept | Checks whether the conclusion depends on how a loss is encoded |
| `cell_emb` readout | — (readout, not a condition) | None — the cell's own embedding | Negative control: a neighbour edit cannot change it |

Sources: [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L251-L255), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L21-L24), [README.md](README.md#L85-L91)

The flow below shows how one tokenised sequence fans out into the condition family and converges again into paired comparisons:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    TOK["Step 04 output: tokenised sequences<br/>gene_tokens + gene_expr, built once per patient"]
    TOK --> BASE["Baseline embedding:<br/>all Mye cells + target macrophages"]
    TOK --> SEL["apply_edit: edits restricted to<br/>neighbour blocks 1..10 flagged as CSF1+ fibroblast"]
    SEL --> C1["CSF1_remove (test)"]
    SEL --> C2["CSF1_zero (control)"]
    SEL --> C3["POS_block (positive control)"]
    SEL --> C4["NULL_gene x 20 (null controls)"]
    C1 --> EMB["TERRA-112M embedding<br/>same rows, same order, same batching"]
    C2 --> EMB
    C3 --> EMB
    C4 --> EMB
    BASE --> PAIR["Paired per-cell comparison:<br/>condition vs its own baseline"]
    EMB --> PAIR
    PAIR --> S07["Step 07: classifier dP,<br/>cosine shift, W2, null-relative statistics"]
```

Sources: [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L251-L266), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L296-L299)

## Anatomy of an Editable Block

TERRA-112M represents each cell as 11 blocks of 256 gene tokens (`W=2816`): block 0 is the cell's own genes and blocks 1–10 are its nearest neighbours. The design draws a hard boundary here: **no condition ever touches block 0 or any block that does not belong to a CSF1+ fibroblast**. The editable blocks are precomputed per target macrophage as the boolean matrix `blk`, built by indexing the `is_cf` flag (written by step 04) through the neighbour index table; `n_cf_nb` is the row sum, i.e. the number of CSF1+ fibroblast neighbours per cell.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph SEQ["One target macrophage sequence: 11 blocks x 256 tokens"]
        B0["Block 0: the cell's own 256 genes<br/>NEVER edited by any condition"]
        B1["Blocks 1..10: the 10 nearest neighbours"]
    end
    B1 --> Q{"Neighbour is a CSF1+ fibroblast?<br/>source state AND raw CSF1 count > 0"}
    Q -- "yes" --> OK["blk is True for this block:<br/>editable by every condition"]
    Q -- "no" --> NO["Untouched by every condition"]
    B0 -.->|"own block is outside the edit scope"| SEL["apply_edit slices blocks 1..10 only"]
```

The CSF1+ fibroblast definition — a fibroblast in one of the configured source states with a raw *CSF1* count > 0 — is inherited from the study design rather than re-derived in step 06, and the source/target states themselves are read from `config/analysis.cfg` via the shared `analysis_config.py` module.

Sources: [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L70), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L236-L249), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L147-L157), [analysis_config.py](scripts/analysis_config.py#L7-L9), [README.md](README.md#L56-L58)

## Three Edit Semantics, One Code Path

All 23 conditions flow through a single `apply_edit` function that differs only in its *selection* and *mode*. The selection narrows to tokens inside blocks where `blk` is true: for gene-targeted conditions it matches the gene's token ID, while for `POS_block` (`token=None`) it matches every non-padding token in the eligible blocks. The two modes then diverge:

| Mode | Used by | Token after edit | Value after edit | Block layout after edit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `remove` (gene token) | `CSF1_remove`, all 20 nulls | Set to 0 (padding) | Set to 0 | Remaining tokens compact upward; padding pushed to block end |
| `zero` | `CSF1_zero` | Kept | Set to 0 | Unchanged |
| `remove` (whole block, `token=None`) | `POS_block` | All set to 0 | All set to 0 | Block fully emptied into padding |

> [!TIP]
> The compaction in `remove` mode uses `np.argsort(sub_t == 0, kind="stable")` on each edited block: a *stable* sort that moves padding to the end while preserving the original expression-ranked order of surviving tokens. This is the invariant the downstream check `padding stays at block ends` relies on — a naive `argsort` without `stable` could reorder surviving tokens and silently change the semantics of the knockout for every condition using this mode.

Sources: [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L147-L177)

## Which Cells Count as Edited

Membership in a condition is defined per cell, not per gene: **a target macrophage is edited by a condition when at least one of its eligible blocks contains that condition's gene** (`POS_block`: when it has at least one CSF1+ fibroblast neighbour at all), and `n_edit` stores the count of edited blocks per cell and condition. This has an important asymmetry across the catalogue. Because a CSF1+ fibroblast is defined by having raw *CSF1* > 0, *CSF1* is present in every eligible block by construction, so `n_edit(CSF1_remove)` equals `n_cf_nb` exactly — a property step 07 audits as the QC column `frac_nedit_CSF1_remove_eq_n_cf_nb`. Null genes, by contrast, are only rank-*matched* to CSF1's presence (about 0.66 of blocks, band ±0.15), so their per-cell `n_edit` genuinely varies, and a null gene may edit no target cell in a given donor at all — which is why step 07 reports `n_null_used` alongside every null median.

Sources: [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L24-L26), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L276-L284), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L56-L59), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L247-L249), [05_null_genes.py](scripts/05_null_genes.py#L8-L10), [README.md](README.md#L93-L97)

## Paired Embedding Protocol

The control design only works if condition embeddings are directly comparable to the baseline, and step 06 enforces this structurally. The baseline is embedded once for every myeloid cell (the classifier training set for step 07) and once for the target macrophages; every condition then embeds **exactly the same target rows in the same order**, so batching is identical across conditions and any row index refers to the same cell in baseline and all 23 condition arrays. Three embedding types are collected per pass: `spatial_cell_emb` (the primary readout), `neighborhood_emb` (secondary), and `cell_emb` — the last kept purely as a negative control, since a neighbourhood edit cannot change the cell's own embedding.

Sources: [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L28-L34), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L261-L266), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L296-L299), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L26-L33)

## Built-In Verification of Every Condition

Each condition embedding pass is followed by a battery of structural checks that are recorded per patient and abort the task on failure: (1) the set of changed rows equals the set of rows with `n_edit > 0` — an edit must change precisely its members and nobody else; (2) nothing changed outside the edited blocks; (3) padding remains at block ends after removal; and (4) `cell_emb` is unchanged versus baseline (max absolute difference < 1e-4). The last check operationalises the negative control: if the pipeline ever produced a non-zero `cell_emb` deviation, the neighbourhood-isolation premise of the whole design would be broken and the run would fail loudly rather than produce misleading shifts.

Sources: [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L36-L39), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L283-L300), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L315-L317), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L353-L357)

## How Each Control Enters the Statistics

Step 07 does not treat the catalogue uniformly — each condition earns a distinct analytical role, encoded in the `role` column of the summary sheet (`test`, `control`, or `null gene`). The 20 nulls are *quantitative instruments*: the donor-level effect of any reported condition is defined as `d = mean dP(condition) − median over the nulls of mean dP(null)`, the same null median anchors the `W2(condition) − median W2(null)` magnitude comparison, and the test gene is ranked among the 21-gene set (test + nulls; `POS_block` and `CSF1_zero` are explicitly excluded from the rank set). `CSF1_zero` and `POS_block` are *qualitative instruments*: they are reported descriptively — same eligible donors, same null median — but never enter significance testing. Donor eligibility itself is tied to the test condition only: a donor is eligible when `CSF1_remove` edits at least `MIN_EDITED = 20` target macrophages.

| Control | Where it acts in step 07 | What it guards against |
|---|---|---|
| 20 `NULL_<gene>` | `d` subtraction, `n_null_used`, 21-gene ranks, W2-vs-null | A generic edit of comparable size at the same positions producing a similar output change |
| `POS_block` | Descriptive magnitude reporting only | An insensitive readout / pipeline failure to detect any neighbourhood change |
| `CSF1_zero` | Descriptive magnitude reporting only | Conclusions that depend on the token-removal encoding rather than the biology |
| `cell_emb` readout | Hard check in step 06 (< 1e-4) | Edits leaking outside the neighbourhood into the cell's own representation |
| `MIN_EDITED` on `CSF1_remove` | Eligible-donor filter for all statistics | Donors contributing noisy `d` from too few edited cells |

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph CAT["23 conditions in emb_ko.npz"]
        TEST["CSF1_remove"]
        NULLS["NULL_gene x 20"]
        POS["POS_block"]
        ZERO["CSF1_zero"]
    end
    TEST -->|"mean dP per donor"| D["d = mean dP - median null mean dP<br/>Wilcoxon over eligible donors"]
    NULLS -->|"median of the 20"| D
    TEST -->|"W2 per donor"| W2["W2 - median null W2<br/>rank largest of 21"]
    NULLS -->|"median of the 20"| W2
    TEST -->|"cohort median mean dP"| GR["Rank most negative of 21"]
    NULLS -->|"cohort median mean dP"| GR
    POS -->|"descriptive only"| DESC["Reported, never tested"]
    ZERO -->|"descriptive only"| DESC
    TEST -->|"n_edit >= 20"| ELIG["Eligible-donor filter"]
```

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L53-L67), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L100-L104), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L257-L263), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L442-L447), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L474-L482), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L486-L504), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L513-L531)

> [!TIP]
> When reading `07_summary.xlsx`, the `role` column is the authoritative map from condition to interpretation: `null gene` rows form the reference distribution, the single `test` row is the only object of the Wilcoxon test, and `control` rows (`POS_block`, `CSF1_zero`) exist solely to be eyeballed against expectation. Because all non-null conditions share the same eligible donors and the same null median, any difference between `CSF1_remove`, `CSF1_zero`, and `POS_block` rows reflects the condition edit itself — not cohort composition.

## Why This Particular Control Set

The catalogue is not generic best practice — each element answers a specific failure mode. Two observed behaviours of the model/tooling motivated building edits directly on step 04's tokens instead of re-tokenising or using the library's perturbation helper: re-tokenising after zeroing counts leaked changes into cells outside the intended neighbourhood, and `perturb_dataset` with `perturbation_target="neighborhood"` additionally edited blocks belonging to unlisted cells in `terra-st 0.1.13`. Token-level editing in pinned blocks removes both confounds at the source, which in turn makes the fine-grained control set meaningful. The gene-level controls address the remaining, subtler problem: changing *any* input changes a foundation model's output, so raw shift magnitude alone cannot distinguish a CSF1-specific effect from the effect of removing any comparably ranked gene at the same positions — hence the nulls; and a positive control distinguishes "small biological effect" from "broken measurement" — hence `POS_block`.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L73-L83), [README.md](README.md#L112-L128), [05_null_genes.py](scripts/05_null_genes.py#L12-L24)

## Where to Go Next

The construction details of the removal semantics and the edit-invariant checks are elaborated in [Token-Level Knockout Editing](11-token-level-knockout-editing); the candidate bands, exclusion list, and seed behind the 20 nulls are covered in [Rank-Matched Null Gene Selection](12-rank-matched-null-gene-selection), and their statistical rationale in [Null-Gene Control Rationale](14-null-gene-control-rationale). How `dP` is produced by the classifier that scores every condition, and how the per-donor `d` values are tested and summarised across the cohort, are documented in [Leave-One-Donor-Out Classifier](15-leave-one-donor-out-classifier) and [Cohort Summary Statistics](17-cohort-summary-statistics).

# Null-Gene Control Rationale



This page explains the *why* behind the pipeline's central inferential device: every CSF1 knockout is compared against 20 rank-matched null-gene knockouts rather than judged on its raw embedding shift. It covers the statistical problem the nulls solve, the properties a null gene must match, why the selection rules are fixed before any result is seen, and how the null distribution is consumed downstream to turn magnitudes into relative evidence. The mechanical selection procedure is documented in [Rank-Matched Null Gene Selection](12-rank-matched-null-gene-selection), and the full set of experimental conditions in [Control Conditions Design](13-control-conditions-design).

## The inference problem: a raw shift is not evidence of specificity

The premise of the study is that removing a ligand from the *neighbour* blocks of a target macrophage may shift the TERRA representation of that macrophage. But TERRA is a foundation model evaluated zero-shot: **changing any input changes its output**, and larger or more prominent input changes tend to produce larger output changes. A shift observed after removing CSF1 therefore admits two competing explanations — CSF1 carries specific signal for the target macrophage states, or the model simply responds to *any* comparable edit made at the same positions in the token sequence. Reporting only the magnitude of the output change cannot separate these two hypotheses.

The design consequence is precise: rather than assessing whether removal of the test gene changes the output, the analysis evaluates **whether its effect exceeds that of comparable genes** — genes removed in the same way, at the same positions, with comparable prominence in the block, but with no expectation of a macrophage-specific effect.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L112-L123), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L40-L51)

## What a valid null must match

A null gene is knocked out **in exactly the same neighbour blocks as CSF1** — the blocks belonging to CSF1+ fibroblasts within each target macrophage's 10-neighbour context. Since the identical intervention is applied to identical token positions, the remaining confound is the *characteristics of the gene itself* inside those blocks. The pipeline fixes this with two statistics computed over the own 256-token block of every CSF1+ fibroblast across all 38 included patients:

| Statistic | Definition | Confound it equalises |
|---|---|---|
| **presence** | fraction of CSF1+ fibroblasts whose block contains the gene | how *often* the knockout edit actually fires per cell |
| **median rank** | median position (1 = highest) when present, in the expression-ordered token list | how *salient* the removed token is within the 256-token block |

TERRA blocks list each cell's genes in order of normalised expression, so token position encodes expression prominence — removing a top-ranked token is not the same intervention as removing a rank-250 token. CSF1's reference values in this cohort are presence 0.66 and median rank 60; a gene present in only 10% of blocks, or living at rank 200, would be a structurally different edit even if removed from the same blocks.

> [!TIP]
> The rank band is compensating for a subtle property of sequence models: within a 256-token block, the same deletion at different positions is not necessarily an equally "visible" edit to the network. Matching median rank makes the null edit positionally indistinguishable from the CSF1 edit, on average.

Sources: [05_null_genes.py](scripts/05_null_genes.py#L6-L19), [05_null_genes.py](scripts/05_null_genes.py#L99-L114), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L19-L20), [README.md](README.md#L67-L71), [README.md](README.md#L93-L97)

## Selection rules: fixed before results, with signal leakage excluded

A null is only a valid baseline if the null genes themselves carry no real macrophage signal. Candidate genes must satisfy **|median rank − CSF1 median rank| ≤ 40 positions** and **|presence − CSF1 presence| ≤ 0.15**, must not be CSF1, and must not appear in `EXCLUDED_LIGANDS` — a list of 49 ligands with established direct effects on macrophage recruitment, survival or polarisation (e.g. `CCL2`, `SPP1`, `VEGFA`, `TGFB1`, `CXCL12`), each of which would risk the null containing exactly the signal the design is trying to subtract.

Two procedural commitments make the selection statistically defensible. First, the docstring states the rules were **"fixed before results are seen"** — the bands and exclusion list are pre-specified, not tuned against outcomes. Second, the draw is mechanical and fail-fast: exactly 20 genes are drawn from the candidate pool with `np.random.default_rng(1234)`, and if fewer than 20 candidates exist the script **exits without widening the bands**, eliminating data-dependent flexibility at the point of failure. The full audit trail (parameters, selected genes, all candidates, all-gene statistics, excluded ligands, per-patient cohort table) is written to `05_null_genes.xlsx`, and the 20 selected genes travel forward as a single TSV consumed by step 06.

| Funnel stage | Criterion | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Band — rank | \|Δ median rank\| ≤ 40 | equalise positional salience |
| Band — presence | \|Δ presence\| ≤ 0.15 | equalise edit frequency |
| Exclusion — identity | ≠ CSF1 | null must not be the test gene |
| Exclusion — biology | ∉ `EXCLUDED_LIGANDS` (49 ligands) | null must contain no macrophage signal |
| Draw | 20 of the candidates, seed 1234 | deterministic, pre-registered pick |
| Guard | exit if < 20 candidates; bands never widened | no outcome-driven relaxation |

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    CF["Step 04: cf_blocks.npz<br/>(own 256-token block of every<br/>CSF1+ fibroblast, 38 patients)"] --> ST["Presence + median rank<br/>of every gene in those blocks"]
    ST --> REF["CSF1 reference:<br/>presence 0.66, median rank 60"]
    ST --> BAND{"\u0394rank \u2264 40<br/>and \u0394presence \u2264 0.15?"}
    REF --> BAND
    BAND --> EXCL["not CSF1, not in<br/>EXCLUDED_LIGANDS"]
    EXCL --> DRAW["Seeded draw, seed 1234:<br/>20 null genes"]
    DRAW --> EDIT["Step 06: NULL_&lt;gene&gt; conditions<br/>identical remove-edit,<br/>identical CSF1+ fibroblast blocks"]
    EDIT --> D["Step 07: d = mean dP(CSF1_remove)<br/>\u2212 median of mean dP(NULL_*)"]
    EDIT --> RANK["Step 07: rank of CSF1<br/>among the 21 genes"]
```

Sources: [05_null_genes.py](scripts/05_null_genes.py#L12-L24), [05_null_genes.py](scripts/05_null_genes.py#L50-L63), [05_null_genes.py](scripts/05_null_genes.py#L119-L131), [05_null_genes.py](scripts/05_null_genes.py#L155-L156)

## How the nulls convert magnitude into relative evidence

Step 06 guarantees the intervention is identical: each `NULL_<gene>` condition removes the gene's token *and* value and shifts the remaining tokens up — exactly the `CSF1_remove` edit, applied in exactly the CSF1+ fibroblast neighbour blocks. The loader asserts exactly 20 null conditions reach the embedding stage. Step 07 then uses the 20 null knockouts as a **paired reference distribution** at three levels:

| Readout | Null-relative form | Guardrail it enforces |
|---|---|---|
| `d` (per donor, primary) | mean dP(`CSF1_remove`) − median over the 20 nulls of mean dP(null) | CSF1 must beat *comparable* edits, not zero |
| Donor test | two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank of d = 0 over eligible donors | cohort-level significance of the null-relative effect |
| Gene rank | cohort median donor mean dP per condition, ranked among the 21 genes | CSF1's standing in the full gene set, not just vs the null median |
| W2 (descriptive) | raw, as W2(condition) − median W2(null), and rank among 21 | magnitude-only metric never used for direction |

A donor-level subtlety is worth noting: a null gene contributes to the median only when it actually edited at least one target macrophage in that donor (since applicability requires a CSF1+ fibroblast neighbour block containing the gene). The number of nulls used is reported per donor as `n_null_used`, so donors where few null genes fire remain interpretable rather than silently degraded.

> [!TIP]
> The null median in step 07 is computed per donor via `null_tab.median(axis=1, skipna=True)` over donor-level *mean* dP values — not pooled across cells. This keeps the test statistic at the donor level, matching the Wilcoxon unit and avoiding pseudo-replication from treating cells as independent.

Sources: [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L229-L256), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L55-L64), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L257-L263), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L429-L458)

## Position among the control family

The null genes answer one specific question — *is CSF1's effect specific relative to comparable edits?* — and are designed to interlock with the other controls, each of which answers a different failure mode:

| Control | Question it answers | Consequence if it behaves unexpectedly |
|---|---|---|
| 20 × `NULL_<gene>` | Is the CSF1 effect above comparable edits at the same positions? | Effect is not specific to CSF1's biology |
| `POS_block` (whole block emptied) | Can the pipeline detect a real neighbourhood change at all? | A small CSF1 effect could be a sensitivity failure, not weak biology |
| `CSF1_zero` (value zeroed, token kept) | Does the result depend on how the loss is encoded in tokens? | `CSF1_remove` result is an artefact of the edit encoding |
| `cell_emb` readout | Does a neighbour edit improperly leak into the cell's own embedding? | Premise of the whole neighbourhood design breaks |

The logic is asymmetric and diagnostic: if the positive control fires as expected while CSF1's effect stays within the null distribution, the small effect can be read as biologically or functionally weak rather than as a method failure — the inference the null design exists to license. Notably, step 07 makes **no automatic call** from these statistics; interpretation is deferred to the analyst, with the summary tables produced in [Cohort Summary Statistics](17-cohort-summary-statistics) and caveats discussed in [Limitations and Caveats](21-limitations-and-caveats).

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L85-L97), [README.md](README.md#L123-L128), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L53-L54), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L21-L26)

## Summary: the rationale in one chain

The null-gene control exists because a zero-shot model guarantees *some* shift for *any* edit. The pipeline therefore never asks "did removing CSF1 shift the embedding?" — that answer is trivially yes — but "does removing CSF1 shift it more than removing a rank- and presence-matched, macrophage-signal-free gene from the same blocks?" The answer is constructed by (1) pre-specifying matching rules before results exist, (2) excluding all ligands with known macrophage activity so nulls carry no true signal, (3) applying the byte-identical edit to the identical blocks, and (4) reporting CSF1 only relative to the null distribution — as donor-level d, as a rank among 21 genes, and as null-relative W2. Every element downstream of step 05 inherits the validity of these pre-commitments.

Sources: [05_null_genes.py](scripts/05_null_genes.py#L6-L24), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L12-L26), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L55-L67), [README.md](README.md#L112-L128)

**Continue reading**: the selection mechanics behind these rules in [Rank-Matched Null Gene Selection](12-rank-matched-null-gene-selection), how each condition is constructed at token level in [Token-Level Knockout Editing](11-token-level-knockout-editing), and how the null-relative statistics surface in the final outputs in [Cohort Summary Statistics](17-cohort-summary-statistics).

# Leave-One-Donor-Out Classifier



This page explains the **leave-one-donor-out (LODO) classifier** — the directional readout of the perturbation framework, implemented in the final pipeline step `scripts/07_ko_pool.py`. While the upstream in-silico knockout produces perturbed embeddings and W₂ distances quantify *how far* embeddings move, only the classifier answers *in which direction*: it converts TERRA embeddings into a probability that a macrophage belongs to the target states, then measures whether in-silico CSF1 knockout displaces target macrophages beyond what 20 rank-matched null genes do — with each donor serving as an independent replicate.

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L6-L10), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L26-L34)

## Position in the Readout Stack

The script declares the classifier as the **primary readout**: `PRIMARY = ("target", "spatial")` — the target-state classifier evaluated on the spatial cell embedding. Two classifiers × two embeddings are computed (`CLASSIFIERS = ["target"]`, `EMBEDDINGS = ["spatial", "neigh"]`), but the summary is anchored on the spatial variant; the neighbourhood embedding is retained as a secondary readout. The script's docstring is explicit about the division of labour: W₂ is *magnitude only* — it cannot distinguish a shift towards the target states from one away from it — so it is never used as directional evidence. The classifier exists precisely to fill that gap.

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L120-L123), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L48-L52)

## Why Leave One Donor Out

The core threat to validity is **donor-level confounding**: baseline embedding structure varies across donors, and a classifier trained on cells from donor P would partially memorise P-specific geometry, inflating `P(target)` for P's own cells and contaminating `dP`. The design eliminates this by construction: for each held-out donor P, the training split is `donor_all != p` — the model that scores a donor **never saw that donor's cells**. Each of the 38 donors therefore receives a model fitted exclusively on the other 37, and any per-cell probability difference is attributable to the embedding content itself, not to donor-shared training signal.

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L31-L33), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L312)

## Architecture and Module Interactions

The diagram below shows the full data flow. Read it left to right: per-donor knockout files from step 06 feed both the cohort-wide baseline pool (training material) and the scoring stage; donor-specific models emit held-out AUCs and per-cell probabilities that cascade into donor-level statistics and the final workbooks. The donor loop (second diagram) then shows how the 38 fits are orchestrated and cached.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph IN["Per-donor inputs from step 06"]
        KO["emb_ko.npz: baseline myeloid and target<br/>embeddings + 23 condition embeddings + n_edit"]
    end
    subgraph POOL["Cohort baseline pool"]
        MAC["All mac-* cells across 38 donors<br/>spatial and neighbourhood embeddings"]
    end
    subgraph LODO["Per held-out donor P"]
        TR["Training split: baseline mac-* cells<br/>of the other 37 donors"]
        SC["StandardScaler, fit on training donors only"]
        LR["LogisticRegression lbfgs, C=1.0,<br/>class_weight=balanced"]
        M["Donor-P-specific model: P target, embedding"]
    end
    subgraph OUT["Scoring and aggregation"]
        AUC["Held-out AUC on P's baseline mac-* cells"]
        PB["pb: P target given baseline, per target cell"]
        PC["pc: P target given condition, per target cell"]
        DP["dP = pc - pb, edited cells only"]
        D["d = mean dP condition - median null mean dP"]
        W["Two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank<br/>across eligible donors"]
        RK["Cohort rank among the 21 genes"]
    end
    KO --> MAC
    KO --> PB
    KO --> PC
    MAC --> TR
    TR --> SC --> LR --> M
    M --> AUC
    M --> PB
    M --> PC
    PB --> DP
    PC --> DP
    DP --> D
    D --> W
    D --> RK
```

Module-level dependencies are deliberately narrow: the classifier uses only `sklearn` primitives plus one TERRA inference helper for W₂, and reads the cell-state definitions from the shared configuration module used by steps 03, 04 and 07. The script aborts at start-up if the TERRA `perturb` extra (`geomloss`) is missing, so a partially installed environment fails fast rather than producing partial results.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    CFG["config/analysis.cfg<br/>TARGET_STATES"] --> AC["analysis_config.load_states"]
    S6["06_ko_embed outputs<br/>terra_ko/P/emb_ko.npz"] --> MAIN["07_ko_pool.py"]
    AC --> MAIN
    TERRA["terra.inference.token_distance<br/>_geomloss_distance_pointcloud<br/>needs geomloss extra"] --> MAIN
    SK["sklearn: StandardScaler,<br/>LogisticRegression, roc_auc_score"] --> MAIN
    SCI["scipy.stats.wilcoxon"] --> MAIN
    MAIN --> CACHE["ko_pool_cache/P.npz"]
    MAIN --> XS["openpyxl workbooks:<br/>07_summary.xlsx and 07_details.xlsx"]
```

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L128-L142), [analysis_config.py](scripts/analysis_config.py#L1-L9), [07_ko_pool.sh](scripts/07_ko_pool.sh#L9-L19)

## Training Data and Label Construction

Training uses **baseline embeddings only** — no perturbed embedding ever enters a training set. For each donor, every myeloid cell whose state starts with the `mac-` prefix contributes its baseline spatial and neighbourhood embeddings to the cohort pool, together with its state label. The binary label is defined by `clf_labels`: `1` if the cell's state is in `TARGET_STATES`, `0` for all other `mac-*` states. `TARGET_STATES` is read from `config/analysis.cfg` through `analysis_config.load_states()`, which validates that the placeholder file has been replaced and that no state is listed twice — so retraining the classifier on a different target definition is a pure configuration change.

Before any fit, the script enforces cohort integrity: exactly `EXPECTED_N_DONORS = 38` patient folders with `emb_ko.npz`, identical `cond_names` across patients, `n_edit` shape consistency, and a cross-check that `mye_state[t_in_mye]` equals `t_state`. A mismatch on any of these aborts the run.

| Parameter | Value | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Task | any `TARGET_STATES` vs other `mac-*` states | Binary target-membership probability |
| Training cells | baseline embeddings of all `mac-*` cells | Per-embedding matrices, stacked cohort-wide |
| Scaler | `StandardScaler`, fit on training donors only | Prevents donor-specific moments leaking into evaluation |
| Model | `LogisticRegression` (lbfgs), `C=1.0`, `tol=1e-4` | Regularised linear probe |
| Class weights | `balanced` | Corrects target-state prevalence imbalance |
| Max iterations | 5000, with `hit_max_iter` flagged per donor | Convergence audit |
| Replications | 38 donor-specific fits × 2 embeddings | Donor = statistical replicate |
| Primary variant | `target` classifier on `spatial` embedding | Anchors all headline statistics |

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L233-L237), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L279-L282), [analysis_config.py](scripts/analysis_config.py#L16-L34), [analysis.cfg.example](config/analysis.cfg.example#L10-L11), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L96-L104), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L109-L123), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L206-L255)

## The Donor Loop: Fit, Score, Cache

Each donor is processed independently by `fit_predict(P)`, which performs four operations per embedding: fit the scaler and logistic regression on the 37-donor training split, compute the held-out AUC on P's own baseline `mac-*` cells, score P's baseline target macrophages (`pb`), and score the same cells under all 23 condition embeddings (`pc`). The critical subtlety is the **scaler fit location**: `StandardScaler` is fitted on `base[e][tr]` — the training donors only — so held-out cells are standardised with donor-foreign statistics. This closes the last leakage channel: even the mean/variance used to transform P's cells come from other donors.

> [!TIP]
> The scaler is fitted on the training split only (line 334), not on the full cohort. Fitting it on all donors would leak donor-P's embedding moments into the transform of P's held-out cells — a subtle but real source of optimistic AUC bias that this implementation explicitly avoids.

Per-donor predictions are cached in `ko_pool_cache/<P>.npz`. Cache validity is governed by an MD5 **settings signature** computed over the entire analytical context: the donor list, logistic-regression hyperparameters, `TARGET_STATES`, the condition name set, and W₂ parameters. On rerun with `FORCE_REBUILD = False`, a matching signature loads predictions from cache; a mismatch triggers a re-fit with a "cache stale" message. Every cached record embeds this signature, so any cohort or configuration change silently invalidates old caches while remaining fully auditable.

> [!TIP]
> The signature (line 287-291) covers not just hyperparameters but the donor roster and condition set — meaning the cache also protects against silently mixing predictions computed under an edited cohort definition, which is exactly the failure mode donor-level statistics are most sensitive to.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Discover emb_ko.npz files,<br/>assert exactly 38 donors"] --> B["Assemble mac-* baseline pool<br/>plus input QC"]
    B --> C{"ko_pool_cache/P.npz exists<br/>and signature matches?"}
    C -- yes --> E["Load cached per-donor predictions"]
    C -- no or stale --> D["fit_predict P: train on 37 donors,<br/>score P, compute AUC"]
    D --> F["Write ko_pool_cache/P.npz"]
    F --> G["Next donor, all 38"]
    E --> G
    G --> H["Per-donor summaries:<br/>dP, cosine shift, strata"]
    H --> I["Eligibility, d, Wilcoxon, ranks"]
    I --> J["07_summary.xlsx and 07_details.xlsx"]
```

| Population | Donors seen | Consumed by | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| Training split | 37 others' baseline `mac-*` | Scaler + logistic fit | Learn target-state boundary |
| Held-out QC set | donor P's baseline `mac-*` | `roc_auc_score` | Generalisation gate |
| Scored baseline | donor P's target macrophages | `pb` | Per-cell reference probability |
| Scored conditions | donor P's targets × 23 conditions | `pc`, cosine distance | Perturbation response |

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L287-L293), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L308-L352), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L355-L367), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L95)

## Per-Cell Readout: dP

The classifier's raw output is a per-cell probability difference: **`dP = P(target | condition) − P(target | baseline)`**, computed with the *same* donor-held-out model scoring both the baseline embedding and the perturbed embedding of each target macrophage. Restriction matters: `dP` is only summarised for cells with `n_edit > 0` under that condition — cells whose neighbourhoods were actually edited by the in-silico knockout. Alongside it, the cosine distance `1 − cos(condition, baseline)` is recorded for the same cells as a pure magnitude companion. The donor-level aggregation then takes the mean over that donor's edited cells.

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L35-L38), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L344-L348), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L403-L410)

## Held-Out AUC as a Quality Gate

Every donor fit records a full audit row per embedding: `heldout_AUC`, held-out cell count, held-out positive count, training size, lbfgs iteration count, and a `hit_max_iter` convergence flag. The AUC is computed on the held-out donor's baseline `mac-*` cells and is set to **NA when one class is absent** in that donor (`0 < yh.sum() < yh.size` guard) — a scenario the pipeline handles gracefully rather than crashing. These rows populate the `classifier_auc` sheet, and the per-embedding median surfaces directly in the summary workbook as `median_heldout_AUC`. Before trusting any headline statistic, this column answers the prerequisite question: does the target-state boundary generalise to unseen donors at all?

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L338-L343), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L397-L402), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L512-L531)

## Donor-Level d, Null Calibration, and the Wilcoxon Test

Raw `dP` means are not comparable across donors, so each donor's CSF1 effect is **calibrated against its own null distribution**: `d = mean dP(condition) − median over the 20 null genes of mean dP(null)`. Null genes in which no target cell was edited contribute nothing to that donor's median, and the count actually used is reported as `n_null_used`. Donors are eligible for inference only if `CSF1_remove` edited at least `MIN_EDITED = 20` target macrophages — a floor that prevents donors with almost no edited targets from contributing noise.

The inferential test is a **two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test of `d = 0`** across eligible donors, treating the donor as the independent unit. The test is repeated within each depth batch to expose batch sensitivity, and each run reports the direction counts (`n_d_negative`), median and mean `d` alongside the statistic and p-value. A guard skips the test when no non-zero `d` exists, writing NA rather than a degenerate p-value. Because the null calibration is donor-specific and the test is donor-level, no pooled-cell pseudo-replication inflates significance — the sample size is the cohort, not the cell count.

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L53-L59), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L104), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L428-L433), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L442-L473)

## Gene Ranking Among the 21 Conditions

Beyond the hypothesis test, the classifier output supports a non-parametric ranking: for each condition, the cohort median of donor-mean `dP` over eligible donors is computed and ranked among the 21-gene set (`CSF1_remove` + 20 nulls), with `rank(method="min", ascending=True)` so that **rank 1 = most negative displacement** — the strongest shift away from target states. This rank is reported for every condition including the descriptive controls (`CSF1_zero`, `POS_block`), giving a single glanceable position of CSF1 within its calibrated null landscape. The W₂ analogue ranks in the opposite direction (1 = largest magnitude), reinforcing that the two metrics answer different questions.

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L263), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L474-L482), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L498-L504)

## Direction vs Magnitude: Why Both Metrics Exist

| Dimension | LODO classifier (`dP`, `d`) | W₂ distance |
|---|---|---|
| Evidence type | **Directional** — probability displacement relative to baseline | Magnitude only — cannot resolve shift direction |
| Granularity | Cell → donor → cohort inference | Per donor × condition, descriptive |
| Calibration | vs median of 20 null genes per donor | vs median null W₂; rank of 21 |
| Statistical test | Two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank | None (never used as evidence of direction) |
| Implementation | sklearn logistic probe | TERRA Sinkhorn via `token_distance` |

The docstring states the division of responsibility unambiguously: W₂ is reported raw, as `W2(condition) − median W2(null)`, and as a rank — but it is *never* used as evidence of direction. The directional claim rests entirely on the classifier. For the full treatment of the magnitude side, see [Embedding Shift Magnitudes](16-embedding-shift-magnitudes).

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L40-L52), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L485-L504)

## Outputs: Where Each Artefact Lives

The step writes two unformatted Excel workbooks plus the per-donor prediction cache. The summary workbook is intentionally small — one row per embedding × condition with the headline statistics and a `role` column distinguishing `test`, `null gene` and `control` — while the details workbook preserves every intermediate table for audit. Execution is a single CPU-only SGE job (32 GB, 24 h wall clock) submitted with `hold_jid tlp_06_ko_embed`, so it starts only after every per-patient knockout embedding has finished.

| Sheet (07_details.xlsx) | Content |
|---|---|
| `settings` | Provenance: script, date, donor counts, every metric definition, settings signature |
| `wilcoxon` | Per classifier/embedding/condition/batch: n, median/mean `d`, `n_d_negative`, statistic, p |
| `gene_rank` | Cohort median donor-mean `dP` and rank among the 21 genes |
| `donor_d` | Per donor: `mean_dP_condition`, `median_null_mean_dP`, `n_null_used`, `d`, eligibility |
| `donor_condition` | Per donor × condition × embedding: `n_edited`, `mean_dP`, `median_dP`, `mean_cos_shift` |
| `strata_n_edited` | `dP`/cosine summaries stratified by edited-neighbour count (1, 2, 3+) |
| `by_target_state` | Same summaries stratified by target cell state |
| `classifier_auc` | Per donor: held-out AUC, class counts, train size, lbfgs iterations, convergence flag |
| `input_qc` | Per donor: cell counts, target-state composition, edit coverage, embedding dimensions |
| `w2_*` sheets | W₂ magnitudes, null differences and ranks (see [Embedding Shift Magnitudes](16-embedding-shift-magnitudes)) |

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L69-L75), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L506-L532), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L581-L588), [07_ko_pool.sh](scripts/07_ko_pool.sh#L1-L19)

## Reading Progression

To understand what the classifier scores, read upstream first: [Token-Level Knockout Editing](11-token-level-knockout-editing) explains how `cond_spatial`/`cond_neigh` are produced, [Rank-Matched Null Gene Selection](12-rank-matched-null-gene-selection) justifies the 20-gene calibration set, and [Control Conditions Design](13-control-conditions-design) covers `CSF1_zero` and `POS_block`. From here, continue to [Embedding Shift Magnitudes](16-embedding-shift-magnitudes) for the magnitude readout, [Cohort Summary Statistics](17-cohort-summary-statistics) for how these tables aggregate, [Reproducibility and Caching](19-reproducibility-and-caching) for the signature mechanics, and finally [Outputs and Result Interpretation](20-outputs-and-result-interpretation) for how to read the workbooks without over-calling results.

# Embedding Shift Magnitudes



This page explains the **magnitude readouts** of the perturbation pipeline: how far the TERRA representation of a target macrophage moves when a ligand token is knocked out, and how those movements are aggregated from single cells up to cohort-level summaries. Magnitudes are *descriptive* — they measure how much the representation changes, never in which direction. They complement the primary classifier readout ([Leave-One-Donor-Out Classifier](15-leave-one-donor-out-classifier)) and feed the cohort tables described in [Cohort Summary Statistics](17-cohort-summary-statistics). Both readouts are computed downstream of the knockout embedding step ([Token-Level Knockout Editing](11-token-level-knockout-editing)): per-cell cosine shifts in step 06, and the Wasserstein-2 population distance in step 07.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L99-L110), [06_ko_embed.py](/scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L2-L10), [07_ko_pool.py](/scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L6-L10)

## Two magnitudes, two granularities

The pipeline reports exactly two magnitude measures, each at a different granularity and with a different tool. The **cosine shift** is a per-cell quantity: for every edited target macrophage, it measures the angular displacement between its baseline embedding and its perturbed embedding, computed independently for the spatial cell embedding (`spatial_cell_emb`, primary) and the neighbourhood embedding (`neighborhood_emb`, secondary). The **Wasserstein-2 distance (W2)** is a per-donor quantity: it compares the *distribution* of baseline embeddings of all edited target macrophages of a donor against the distribution of their perturbed embeddings, using TERRA's own distance metric.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L101-L110), [07_ko_pool.py](/scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L40-L51)

| Property | Cosine shift | Wasserstein-2 (W2) |
|---|---|---|
| Granularity | Per target macrophage | Per donor (population) |
| Definition | `1 − cos(condition, baseline)` | GeomLoss Sinkhorn distance, p = 2 |
| Implementing step | 06 (per-cell sheet) and 07 (summaries) | 07 only |
| Normalisation | Row unit-vectors before dot product | Row L2-normalisation, matching TERRA |
| Point clouds compared | Each cell with itself (paired) | Edited cells of one donor, baseline vs condition (paired) |
| Embeddings covered | spatial and neighbourhood | spatial and neighbourhood |
| Can express direction | No (magnitude only) | No (magnitude only) |
| Role in outputs | `mean_cos_shift` in per-donor summary sheets | `w2_donor`, `w2_vs_null`, `w2_rank` sheets and summary columns |

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](/scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L36-L51), [06_ko_embed.py](/scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L303-L314), [07_ko_pool.py](/scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L585-L586)

Because both are pure magnitudes, neither can tell a shift *towards* the target states from a shift *away* from them. The docstring is explicit: W2 is "magnitude only (it cannot tell a shift towards the target states from one away from it), so it is never used as evidence of direction." Directional evidence comes exclusively from the classifier's dP statistic on the primary readout.

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](/scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L48-L51), [README.md](/README.md#L101-L110)

## Where the magnitudes live in the pipeline

Step 06 embeds every target macrophage under baseline and under each of the 23 conditions (CSF1_remove, CSF1_zero, POS_block, and 20 null-gene knockouts), storing raw embeddings in `emb_ko.npz` for step 07, and writing per-cell cosine shifts immediately to the step-06 workbook. Step 07 re-loads the cached embeddings, recomputes the cosine distances, computes W2 per donor and condition, and aggregates everything into the cohort workbooks.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph S06["Step 06 — 06_ko_embed.py (GPU, one patient per task)"]
        B["Baseline embeddings of target macrophages<br/>base_t_spatial, base_t_neigh"] --> E["Perturbed embeddings per condition<br/>cond_spatial, cond_neigh (23 × n_t × D)"]
        E --> C1["cos_shift → per-cell columns<br/>shift_spatial_&lt;cond&gt;, shift_neigh_&lt;cond&gt;"]
        C1 --> X1["06_ko_embed_&lt;P&gt;.xlsx (per_cell sheet)"]
        B --> N1["emb_ko.npz (raw arrays for step 07)"]
        E --> N1
    end
    subgraph S07["Step 07 — 07_ko_pool.py (CPU, cohort)"]
        N1 --> C2["cos_dist recomputed per cell<br/>and per condition"]
        N1 --> W2["W2 per donor × condition × embedding<br/>Sinkhorn p=2, blur 0.01"]
        C2 --> A1["donor_condition / strata / by_target_state<br/>(mean_cos_shift)"]
        W2 --> A2["w2_donor → w2_vs_null → w2_rank"]
        A2 --> S["07_summary.xlsx + 07_details.xlsx"]
        A1 --> S
    end
```

Sources: [06_ko_embed.py](/scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L261-L331), [07_ko_pool.py](/scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L309-L329), [07_ko_pool.py](/scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L485-L504)

## Cosine shift per cell

For a condition `c` and target macrophage `i`, the cosine shift is `1 − cos(emb_c[i], emb_base[i])`, computed after normalising each embedding to unit length. Step 06 implements this as `cos_shift`, applied condition-wise to both embedding types immediately after each knockout is embedded, and stores the result as `shift_spatial_<condition>` and `shift_neigh_<condition>` columns of the per-cell sheet — one row per target macrophage, annotated with cell id, sample/piece, cell state, and the number of CSF1+ fibroblast neighbours.

Sources: [06_ko_embed.py](/scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L210-L213), [06_ko_embed.py](/scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L303-L314)

Step 07 does not parse the step-06 workbook; it recomputes the identical quantity from the raw arrays in `emb_ko.npz` as `cos_dist`, this time guarding the denominator with an epsilon (`np.maximum(na * nb, 1e-12)`). Restricting to edited cells happens only at summary time: for each donor × condition × embedding, `summ()` reports `mean_cos_shift` over exactly the cells with `n_edit > 0` for that condition — the same cell-selection rule as the classifier's dP — stratified overall, by number of edited neighbours (1, 2, 3+), and by target state.

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](/scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L296-L299), [07_ko_pool.py](/scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L320), [07_ko_pool.py](/scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L377-L381), [07_ko_pool.py](/scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L403-L418)

> [!TIP]
> The per-cell cosine-shift columns in `06_ko_embed_<P>.xlsx` cover *all* target macrophages, including those with `n_edit = 0` (whose embeddings are necessarily unchanged, cosine shift ≈ 0). Only step 07's summaries restrict to edited cells — so if you read the step-06 sheet directly, filter on `n_edit_<condition> > 0` first.

## Wasserstein-2 distance per donor

W2 answers a different question: taken together, how far did the *population* of edited target macrophages of one donor move? For each donor, each condition, and each embedding, step 07 builds two point clouds from the **same cells** — the baseline embeddings of all target macrophages edited by that condition, and their perturbed embeddings — and computes the optimal-transport distance between the two clouds. Pairing the identical cells on both sides keeps the comparison strictly within-donor and within-cell-set; there is no subsampling.

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](/scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L40-L47), [07_ko_pool.py](/scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L321-L329)

The computation deliberately delegates to TERRA's own helper, `_geomloss_distance_pointcloud` from `terra.inference.token_distance` — the same function behind TERRA's `summarize_w2_by_label` — so the numbers are directly comparable with what the model itself reports. Before calling it, rows are L2-normalised exactly as in TERRA's `_l2_normalize_rows`. The distance is the GeomLoss Sinkhorn loss with p = 2, blur 0.01, on the tensorized backend, all matching TERRA's defaults. If a condition edits no target cell in a donor, the W2 value is `NA` (the gate `W2_MIN_CELLS = 1`).

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](/scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L114-L118), [07_ko_pool.py](/scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L138-L142), [07_ko_pool.py](/scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L302-L305), [07_ko_pool.py](/scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L322-L329)

| W2 parameter | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `W2_P` | 2 | Order of the Sinkhorn loss (Wasserstein-2) |
| `W2_BLUR` | 0.01 | GeomLoss entropic regularisation scale (TERRA default) |
| `W2_BACKEND` | `tensorized` | GeomLoss backend (TERRA default) |
| `W2_MIN_CELLS` | 1 | Minimum edited targets required; fewer → W2 = NA |
| `device` | `None` | CPU — step 07 runs outside the GPU |

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](/scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L114-L118), [07_ko_pool.py](/scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L76-L79)

Because GeomLoss is a TERRA optional dependency, step 07 refuses to start unless the model was installed with the `perturb` extra, which pulls in `geomloss`.

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](/scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L76-L77), [07_ko_pool.py](/scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L138-L142)

## From per-donor W2 to cohort summaries

The W2 sheets form a three-stage pyramid. The `w2_donor` sheet is the raw layer: one row per donor × embedding × condition with the donor's W2 and the number of cells edited by that condition. The `w2_vs_null` sheet places CSF1_remove, CSF1_zero and POS_block in context: for each of them it reports the donor's `W2_condition`, the median W2 across the 20 null-gene knockouts in that donor (`n_null_used` counts nulls with at least one edited cell), and the difference `W2_minus_null_median`. The `w2_rank` sheet collapses the cohort: `cohort_median_W2` is the median over **eligible donors** (those with ≥ 20 target macrophages edited by CSF1_remove), and `rank_largest_of_21` ranks that median among the 21 genes (CSF1 + 20 nulls), with rank 1 = largest shift. Ties use minimum rank, and POS_block/CSF1_zero appear in the tables but are excluded from the 21-gene rank set.

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](/scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L384-L393), [07_ko_pool.py](/scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L485-L504), [07_ko_pool.py](/scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L429-L433), [README.md](/README.md#L144-L158)

The single-row summary table carries two magnitude columns forward: `cohort_median_W2` and `W2_rank_largest_of_21`, sitting next to the classifier columns so the reader sees magnitude and direction evidence side by side. Note the deliberate asymmetry with the classifier: the classifier rank rewards the *most negative* dP (rank 1 = most negative), while the W2 rank rewards the *largest* shift (rank 1 = largest) — direction and magnitude are kept conceptually separate all the way into the final workbook.

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](/scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L499), [07_ko_pool.py](/scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L513-L531), [07_ko_pool.py](/scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L533-L551)

The `settings` sheet of both workbooks records the exact W2 configuration in prose ("descriptive only; TERRA Sinkhorn p=2 blur=0.01 tensorized on L2-normalised rows … rank 1 = largest"), and the whole analysis is checksummed into a settings signature that also invalidates the per-donor prediction cache when cohort or W2 settings change.

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](/scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L560-L579), [07_ko_pool.py](/scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L287-L293)

## How to read magnitudes: controls and caveats

The gene-level-control design (see [Null-Gene Control Rationale](14-null-gene-control-rationale)) applies to magnitudes with full force: changing *any* input changes the model's output, so a large cosine shift or W2 for CSF1_remove is only meaningful relative to the rank-matched null genes edited at the same positions in the same blocks. The intended inference pattern is therefore relative: CSF1's magnitude exceeds the null distribution (high `W2_minus_null_median`, small `rank_largest_of_21`) *and* the positive control `POS_block` — emptying an entire fibroblast neighbour block — produces the large shift that certifies the pipeline can detect a real neighbourhood change at all.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L112-L128), [README.md](/README.md#L85-L91), [06_ko_embed.py](/scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L20-L22)

A negative control guards the embeddings themselves: because edits touch only neighbour blocks, the cell's *own* embedding (`cell_emb`) must not change at all. Step 06 verifies per condition that the maximum absolute difference of `cell_emb` is below 1e-4 and records the values in the `negative_control_cell_emb` sheet; any failure aborts the patient's run with a non-zero exit.

Sources: [06_ko_embed.py](/scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L31-L34), [06_ko_embed.py](/scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L299), [06_ko_embed.py](/scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L315-L317), [06_ko_embed.py](/scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L353-L357)

> [!TIP]
> Interpret W2 ranks jointly with the classifier ranks of the summary table: a CSF1_remove with `W2_rank_largest_of_21` = 1 but a middling dP rank means the representation moved strongly in a direction unrelated to the target states — a specificity signal, not a positive result. This is precisely why the repository labels both magnitude readouts "descriptive".

Two structural caveats bound what the magnitudes can mean. First, TERRA is a zero-shot model: a change in its representation is not a predicted biological response, only evidence that the model's encoding of the receiving cell is sensitive to the ligand token. Second, the null genes were matched to CSF1's *presence and rank* within the fibroblast token blocks ([Rank-Matched Null Gene Selection](12-rank-matched-null-gene-selection)), so the magnitude comparison is fair only to the extent that token-level edit size is the dominant confounder — which is exactly the hypothesis the design tests.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L130-L138), [README.md](/README.md#L93-L97)

## Where to go next

With magnitudes understood, the natural reading path continues through how all readouts are rolled up per donor and per cohort in [Cohort Summary Statistics](17-cohort-summary-statistics), how the outputs are packaged in [Outputs and Result Interpretation](20-outputs-and-result-interpretation), and which interpretive limits apply in [Limitations and Caveats](21-limitations-and-caveats). To revisit the perturbation conditions that generate the embeddings being compared, see [Token-Level Knockout Editing](11-token-level-knockout-editing) and [Control Conditions Design](13-control-conditions-design).


# Cohort Summary Statistics



The *Cohort Summary Statistics* page explains **step 07** of the pipeline (`scripts/07_ko_pool.py`), the stage where per-patient knockout results from step 06 are pooled into cohort-level statistical evidence. It covers donor discovery and input validation, the leave-one-donor-out classifier that converts embedding shifts into directional probabilities, the per-cell and per-donor summaries, the null-gene-normalised cohort statistic `d`, the Wilcoxon signed-rank test and gene ranks, the W2 magnitude statistics, and the two Excel workbooks the step produces. The step deliberately makes **no automatic significance call**: every quantity is reported, and interpretation is left to the analyst (see [Outputs and Result Interpretation](20-outputs-and-result-interpretation)).

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L1-L80), [README.md](README.md#L99-L110)

## Position in the Pipeline

Step 07 is the terminal, CPU-only stage. It consumes one `emb_ko.npz` file per patient — produced by the GPU array job of step 06 — and requires **all** patients to be present before it starts. Per donor, the input carries baseline embeddings of all myeloid cells, the subset of target macrophages, the perturbed embeddings for 23 conditions (`CSF1_remove`, `CSF1_zero`, `POS_block`, and 20 `NULL_<gene>` files), and `n_edit`, the count of edited neighbours per target cell per condition. The step fits classifiers, computes all readouts, and writes two workbooks plus a per-donor prediction cache.

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L12-L33), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L69-L78)
