To read the diagram: solid arrows are data flow through the six internal stages of `07_ko_pool.py`; the stage numbers 1–6 match the section headers printed in the script's own log output.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    NPZ["emb_ko.npz<br/>(one per patient, from step 06)"] --> QC["1. Donor discovery<br/>+ structure QC"]
    QC --> FIT["2-3. Leave-one-donor-out<br/>classifier fits (cached)"]
    FIT --> CELL["4. Per-cell dP, cosine<br/>per-donor summaries"]
    CELL --> COHORT["5. d, Wilcoxon, gene ranks,<br/>W2 vs nulls"]
    COHORT --> OUT["6. 07_summary.xlsx<br/>07_details.xlsx"]
    FIT -.-> CACHE["ko_pool_cache/&lt;P&gt;.npz"]
    CACHE -.-> FIT
```

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L163-L171), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L285-L296), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L369-L382), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L425-L504)

Execution is orchestrated by `scripts/07_ko_pool.sh`: a single Sun Grid Engine job requesting 32 GB memory and 24 hours, submitted with `qsub -hold_jid tlp_06_ko_embed` so it runs only after every step-06 task has finished. Inside the TERRA container it runs `tx python scripts/07_ko_pool.py` — no GPU is requested, because inference already happened in step 06; this stage is classification and bookkeeping.

Sources: [07_ko_pool.sh](scripts/07_ko_pool.sh#L1-L21)

## Input Validation and Cohort QC

Before any statistics are computed, the step asserts that the cohort is structurally complete. It globs `<KO_DIR>/<P>/emb_ko.npz` and aborts unless exactly `EXPECTED_N_DONORS = 38` patients are found — the number guaranteed by the inclusion rules of step 03 (median depth ≥ 100 counts, ≥ 50 CSF1+ fibroblasts, ≥ 50 target macrophages, as described in [Patient Inclusion Rules](8-patient-inclusion-rules)). Loading uses `allow_pickle=True` because step 06 stores some string arrays as object arrays.

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L95-L96), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L163-L186), [README.md](README.md#L53-L54)

Each patient file then passes a battery of cross-checks: the folder name must match the embedded `patient` key; `cond_names` must be identical across all patients (the cohort-wide condition set is established by the first file); `n_edit` must have shape `(n_targets, n_conditions)`; embedding row counts must match state counts; and `mye_state[t_in_mye]` must equal `t_state`. Simultaneously, the step builds baseline training matrices by extracting all `mac-*` cells from both embeddings across the full cohort — these are what the classifiers train on — and records a per-patient QC row (myeloid/mac/target counts, target-state composition, fraction where `n_edit` for `CSF1_remove` equals the cell's CSF1+ neighbour count, and max absolute difference between the target-row and full-array baseline embeddings, a consistency probe).

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L200-L276), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L241-L254)

## The Leave-One-Donor-Out Classifier Readout

The **primary readout** is directional and probabilistic. For each donor *p*, a binary logistic regression is trained on baseline embeddings of `mac-*` cells from **all other donors** (`tr = tr_donor & m_all`) and scores held-out probabilities on donor *p*'s cells. The classifier predicts P(target): any state in `TARGET_STATES` (read from `config/analysis.cfg` via `analysis_config.load_states`) versus all other macrophage states. Features are `StandardScaler`-scaled with the scaler fit on training donors only, and the logistic regression uses `class_weight="balanced"`, `C=1.0`, `max_iter=5000`, `tol=1e-4`. Because the model scoring donor *p* never saw any of *p*'s cells, donor-level means are not contaminated by within-donor leakage — the foundation of the paired cohort test below. Held-out AUC is computed on the held-out donor's baseline `mac-*` cells and reported as NA when one class is absent; the record also stores `n_train`, `lbfgs_iter`, and a `hit_max_iter` convergence flag.

> [!TIP]
> The `StandardScaler` is fitted **inside** the leave-one-donor-out loop on training donors only (`scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L334`). Reusing a cohort-wide scaler would leak held-out donor statistics into the transform and invalidate the independence assumption behind the Wilcoxon test.

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L279-L281), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L308-L352), [analysis_config.py](scripts/analysis_config.py#L16-L34)

The classifier is applied twice per donor: once to the **baseline** embeddings of the target macrophages (`pb`), once to every **perturbed** embedding (`pc`, shape `n_conditions × n_targets`). The per-cell score is `dP = P(condition) − P(baseline)`, computed only for target cells with `n_edit > 0` in that condition — cells whose neighbourhood contained no editable CSF1+ fibroblast are excluded, since an edit of zero tokens cannot be interpreted. A secondary magnitude score, `cosd = 1 − cosine(condition, baseline)`, is computed on the same cell set. The classifier/embedding pair `("target", "spatial")` is flagged `PRIMARY`; the neighbourhood embedding serves as a secondary readout, reported identically for comparison.

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L120-L123), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L403-L410)

## Per-Donor Summaries and Strata

Donor-level aggregation is deliberately simple and transparent: for every donor × condition × classifier × embedding, the `summ` helper reports `n_edited`, `mean_dP`, `median_dP`, and `mean_cos_shift` over the edited target cells. The same summaries are additionally broken out along two prespecified strata — by number of edited neighbours (`1`, `2`, `3+`) and by target-state label — producing the `strata_n_edited` and `by_target_state` sheets. These strata exist to reveal dose–response (cells with more edited neighbours should shift more if the neighbourhood signal is real) and state heterogeneity without being part of the primary test.

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L377-L423)

## The Primary Statistic: Null-Normalised Shift `d`

The cohort analysis starts with **donor eligibility**: a donor is eligible when at least `MIN_EDITED = 20` target macrophages were edited by `CSF1_remove`, ensuring each donor's contribution rests on a meaningful cell count. Then, per donor, the raw effect is normalised against the null-gene reference distribution:

> **d = mean dP(CSF1_remove) − median over the 20 null genes of mean dP(NULL_<gene>)**

This construction is the statistical heart of the step. It answers the question posed in the study design — *does removing CSF1 shift the representation more than removing a comparable gene at the same token positions?* — rather than asking whether any shift occurs at all (see [Null-Gene Control Rationale](14-null-gene-control-rationale) and [Rank-Matched Null Gene Selection](12-rank-matched-null-gene-selection)). A null gene with no edited target cell in that donor contributes nothing to the median (`skipna=True`), and the number actually used is reported as `n_null_used`. The same `d` is computed for the descriptive conditions `CSF1_zero` and `POS_block` over the identical eligible donors and null median, so all conditions are compared on equal footing.

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L429-L458), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L100-L104)

## Cohort Tests: Wilcoxon Signed-Rank and Gene Ranks

Because each eligible donor contributes one paired value of `d` (its own CSF1 effect minus its own null median), the cohort test is a **two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test of d = 0** — a distribution-free test appropriate for a modest donor count (n = 38 maximum) with no normality assumption. It is run over all eligible donors and repeated within each depth batch (`deep`/`shallow`, defined in step 04), exposing whether the effect is driven by sequencing depth. Each test record stores `n_donors`, `n_d_negative` (donors shifted *away* from the target states beyond the null median), `median_d`, `mean_d`, the statistic `wilcoxon_V`, and `p_two_sided`; if a group has fewer than one non-zero value the test is reported as NA rather than fabricated.

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L459-L473), [README.md](README.md#L61-L63)

The second cohort-level view is the **gene rank**. For each condition, the cohort median of donor `mean_dP` (over eligible donors) is computed and ranked among the 21 genes in `RANK_SET` (CSF1 + 20 nulls) with `method="min", ascending=True`, so **rank 1 = most negative median shift**. This reframes the result as a placement question: does CSF1_remove sit at the extreme of the null distribution, or in its middle? It is robust to the absolute calibration of the classifier probabilities and is the figure the summary workbook surfaces first.

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L474-L482)

## Magnitude Statistics: W2 Relative to the Nulls

Alongside the directional readout, the step computes TERRA's own population distance: per donor × condition × embedding, **W2** between the L2-normalised baseline and condition embeddings of the edited target cells, via `terra.inference.token_distance._geomloss_distance_pointcloud` (Sinkhorn, p=2, blur 0.01, tensorized backend — TERRA's defaults, no subsampling). W2 requires the TERRA `perturb` extra (`geomloss`); the script exits at start-up if it is missing. W2 is NA when a condition edits no target in that donor.

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L114-L118), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L302-L329), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L138-L142)

W2 is **magnitude only** — it cannot distinguish a shift toward the target states from one away from them — so it is never used as evidence of direction. It is reported three ways: raw per donor, as `W2(condition) − median null W2` per donor (with `n_null_used`), and as the cohort median W2 ranked among the 21 genes with **rank 1 = largest** (note the inverted convention relative to the dP rank, documented explicitly in the columns sheet). The cosine shift `cosd` plays the same descriptive-magnitude role at per-cell resolution.

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L48-L51), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L485-L504)

| Readout | Direction? | Level | Cohort aggregation | Rank convention |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dP` via classifier | Yes (toward/away target states) | Per edited cell | `d` → Wilcoxon + median rank | Rank 1 = most negative |
| `W2` (Sinkhorn) | No (magnitude only) | Per donor's edited cells | Median vs null, rank | Rank 1 = largest |
| `cosd` | No (magnitude only) | Per edited cell | `mean_cos_shift` per donor | Not ranked |

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L40-L51), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L533-L551)

## The Summary Table and Workbook Outputs

All statistics converge into `07_summary.xlsx`: one row per embedding × condition (ordered `CSF1_remove`, controls, then nulls), a `role` column labelling each row `test`/`control`/`null gene`, and a `columns` sheet explaining every field. The `settings` sheet records the run's provenance — script, timestamp, donor and eligibility counts, readout definitions, classifier settings, W2 parameters, and the settings signature — so a workbook is self-describing years later. The console log also prints a one-line headline for the primary readout: CSF1_remove on the spatial embedding, with median d, two-sided p, and rank of 21.

> [!TIP]
> The summary workbook uses only the `depth_batch == "all"` Wilcoxon rows (`scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L509`). The per-batch tests exist only in `07_details.xlsx` — if a reviewer asks whether the effect holds in both depth strata, the answer is in the details workbook, not the summary.

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L505-L554), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L560-L581)

`07_details.xlsx` carries every intermediate table, so any summary number can be traced back to per-donor values:

| Sheet | Content |
|---|---|
| `settings` | run metadata, definitions, settings signature |
| `wilcoxon` | signed-rank tests, overall and per depth batch, all classifier × embedding × condition combinations |
| `gene_rank` | cohort median `mean_dP` and rank of 21 per condition |
| `donor_d` | per-donor `d`, null median, `n_null_used`, eligibility flags |
| `donor_condition` | per-donor × condition summaries (`mean_dP`, `median_dP`, `mean_cos_shift`, `n_edited`) |
| `strata_n_edited` / `by_target_state` | the same summaries stratified by edited-neighbour count / target state |
| `w2_donor` / `w2_vs_null` / `w2_rank` | W2 per donor, minus null median, and cohort rank |
| `classifier_auc` | held-out AUC, train/held-out sizes, lbfgs convergence per donor |
| `input_qc` | per-patient structural checks of the step 06 files |

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L581-L588), [README.md](README.md#L144-L158)

## Caching and the Settings Signature

The expensive part of step 07 is the 38 leave-one-donor-out fits plus the Sinkhorn distances, so per-donor predictions are cached in `WORK_DIR/ko_pool_cache/<P>.npz`. Cache validity is governed by an MD5 **settings signature** computed from the donor list, classifier hyperparameters (`C`, `max_iter`, `tol`), the target states, the condition set, and the W2 parameters. On re-run with `FORCE_REBUILD = False`, a cached file whose stored signature matches is reused as-is; a mismatch (changed cohort, classifier, or W2 settings) marks the cache stale and refits that donor. This means silently changing `MIN_EDITED` or cohort composition invalidates the cache correctly, while pure summary-layer tweaks (e.g., eligibility threshold alone, which is *not* in the signature) reuse fits legitimately — a deliberate separation of fit-time from summary-time parameters.

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L285-L296), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L355-L367), [README.md](README.md#L179-L183)

## Configuration Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `TEST_COND` | `CSF1_remove` | the test perturbation |
| `DESCR_CONDS` | `CSF1_zero`, `POS_block` | descriptive controls, same `d` machinery |
| `NULL_PREFIX` / `N_NULL` | `NULL_` / 20 | null-gene conditions, asserted exactly |
| `MIN_EDITED` | 20 | eligibility: ≥ this many targets edited by `TEST_COND` |
| `TARGET_STATES` | from `config/analysis.cfg` | target macrophage states (classifier labels) |
| `MAC_PREFIX` | `mac-` | classifier training population |
| `LR_C` / `LR_MAX_ITER` / `LR_TOL` | 1.0 / 5000 / 1e-4 | logistic-regression hyperparameters |
| `W2_P` / `W2_BLUR` / `W2_BACKEND` | 2 / 0.01 / tensorized | Sinkhorn W2 settings (TERRA defaults) |
| `PRIMARY` | `("target", "spatial")` | primary classifier × embedding pair |
| `STRATA` | `1`, `2`, `3+` | edited-neighbour strata |
| `EXPECTED_N_DONORS` | 38 | hard cohort-size assertion |
| `FORCE_REBUILD` | False | ignore/delete per-donor prediction cache |

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L95-L123), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L105-L107)

## Reading the Results and Where to Go Next

The step's contract is descriptive-plus-inferential, not verdict-rendering: it reports `d`, the Wilcoxon p-value, the rank of CSF1 among 21 genes, and the magnitude ranks, but never prints an automatic "effect/no effect" call. Interpretation requires reading the pieces together — a convincing CSF1-specific result needs a negative median `d` with a low p-value in *both* depth batches, a rank of 1 against the null distribution, a `POS_block` that demonstrates detectability, and `classifier_auc` values showing the classifier itself is informative. Field-by-field guidance lives in the `columns` sheet of the summary workbook and in [Outputs and Result Interpretation](20-outputs-and-result-interpretation); known limits of the zero-shot readout are catalogued in [Limitations and Caveats](21-limitations-and-caveats).

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L53-L67), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L533-L554)

Recommended reading order from here: the statistical context for `dP` and W2 is developed in [Leave-One-Donor-Out Classifier](15-leave-one-donor-out-classifier) and [Embedding Shift Magnitudes](16-embedding-shift-magnitudes); the nulls that anchor `d` come from [Rank-Matched Null Gene Selection](12-rank-matched-null-gene-selection) and [Control Conditions Design](13-control-conditions-design); and the scheduler mechanics behind the `-hold_jid tlp_06_ko_embed` submission shown above are covered in [Cluster Execution and Job Chaining](18-cluster-execution-and-job-chaining).


# Cluster Execution and Job Chaining



This page documents how the seven pipeline steps run on a cluster: the SGE (Sun Grid Engine) wrapper scripts that define resources and job names, the shared environment layer that bridges the scheduler to a Singularity container, and the `-hold_jid` mechanism that chains jobs into a strict linear sequence. It also covers array-job parallelism, the resumability contract between steps, and the smoke-test workflow used before committing expensive GPU time. The computational content of each step is out of scope here — see [Pipeline Architecture](5-pipeline-architecture) — as is the configuration file format, covered in [Configuration Setup](4-configuration-setup).

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L185-L199), [env/terra_env.sh](/env/terra_env.sh#L1-L15)

## Three-Layer Execution Architecture

Every pipeline step is separated into three layers with a strict one-directional dependency: the **scheduler layer** (a `qsub` invocation carrying SGE resource requests), the **wrapper layer** (one `.sh` script per step, identical in shape), and the **environment layer** (`env/terra_env.sh`, sourced by every wrapper, which translates paths and scheduler state into a containerized execution). The compute scripts themselves contain no cluster code and no paths — they read locations exclusively from environment variables injected by the environment layer (`WORK_DIR`, `RESULTS_DIR`, `MODEL_DIR`, etc.). This means a step's Python or R code is identical whether it runs interactively on a login node or as job task 17 of an array; only the wrapper differs.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph L1["Scheduler layer"]
        Q["qsub -hold_jid ..."]
    end
    subgraph L2["Wrapper layer (scripts/NN_*.sh)"]
        W["SGE directives<br/>set -euo pipefail<br/>source env/terra_env.sh<br/>require_avx"]
    end
    subgraph L3["Environment layer (env/terra_env.sh)"]
        E["reads config/paths.cfg<br/>exports REPO_DIR, MODEL_DIR,<br/>TERRA_CENV · defines tx / txg"]
    end
    subgraph L4["Container layer"]
        S["Singularity .sif image<br/>PyTorch 2.6 / CUDA 12.4<br/>+ pinned pip packages"]
    end
    P["Compute script<br/>(01_export.R ... 07_ko_pool.py)"]
    Q --> W --> E --> S --> P
```

The environment layer is itself bootstrapped by a one-off install: `env/install.sh` pulls the pinned container image, installs locked Python packages into a user directory mounted into the container, downloads the TERRA-112M checkpoint at a pinned Hugging Face revision, and verifies the model checksum — all safe to re-run because each artifact is skipped when already present. Installation is deliberately kept outside the job chain: it requires internet access and runs once on a suitable node, while every later job is fully offline.

Sources: [env/terra_env.sh](/env/terra_env.sh#L17-L69), [env/terra_env.sh](/env/terra_env.sh#L80-L110), [env/install.sh](/env/install.sh#L1-L17), [env/install.sh](/env/install.sh#L35-L84), [README.md](/README.md#L160-L177)

> [!TIP]
> The design invariant worth internalizing: **`terra_env.sh` is the single point where the cluster meets the code**. All paths reach Python through one exported variable, `TERRA_CENV`, so moving the pipeline to a different cluster or storage layout touches only `config/paths.cfg` — never the step scripts.

## Anatomy of a Job Wrapper

All seven wrappers follow one template: an SGE directive block (`#$ ...`), a comment header documenting the submission command, `set -euo pipefail` for fail-fast shell semantics, `source env/terra_env.sh`, an optional hardware gate, a diagnostic `echo` line, and finally the compute invocation. The directives request a job **name** (which the chaining mechanism depends on), merged stdout/stderr logging, memory, and a wall-clock limit. Each wrapper is submitted from the repository root so that relative paths (`env/terra_env.sh`, `logs/`) resolve identically in every job.

| Directive | Purpose | Set in |
|---|---|---|
| `#$ -N tlp_01_export` | Stable job name; the anchor for `-hold_jid` dependencies | all wrappers |
| `#$ -cwd` | Run in the submission directory (repository root) | all wrappers |
| `#$ -j y` | Merge stderr into stdout so each job has one log | all wrappers |
| `#$ -l tmem=..G,h_vmem=..G` | Memory request (site-specific resource names) | all wrappers |
| `#$ -l h_rt=HH:MM:SS` | Wall-clock limit | all wrappers |
| `#$ -t 1-38` | Array job: one task per included patient | 04, 06 |
| `#$ -tc 8` | Cap concurrent array tasks at 8 (GPU pool sizing) | 06 only |
| `#$ -l gpu=true` | Request a GPU slot | 06 only |

Sources: [scripts/01_export.sh](/scripts/01_export.sh#L2-L18), [scripts/06_ko_embed.sh](/scripts/06_ko_embed.sh#L2-L10), [scripts/04_tokenise.sh](/scripts/04_tokenise.sh#L2-L14)

Step 01 is the deliberate exception to the template: R runs **on the host**, not in the container, so it invokes `Rscript` directly and skips both the container runner and the `require_avx` gate. Its only software requirement is R 4.4.1 with the `Matrix`, `igraph`, and `openxlsx` packages available to the job. Every other step runs inside the container via `tx` (CPU steps 02–05, 07) or `txg` (GPU step 06). Every wrapper also carries the portability note *"Adapt resource names (tmem, h_vmem, gpu) to your scheduler"* — `tmem`/`h_vmem` are SGE-site conventions, not standards.

Sources: [scripts/01_export.sh](/scripts/01_export.sh#L9-L18), [README.md](/README.md#L185-L190), [scripts/02_build_h5ad.sh](/scripts/02_build_h5ad.sh#L11)

## Resource and Topology Profile

The seven steps divide into two shapes: **serial checkpoints** (01, 02, 03, 05, 07) that aggregate or decide something cohort-wide, and **array jobs** (04, 06) that process one patient per task. Memory and wall-clock requests track each step's actual workload — from the light 16 GB / 1 h null-gene selection up to step 06's 200 GB host-memory request and step 07's 24 h classification budget.

| Step | Job name | Topology | CPU mem | GPU | Runtime | Holds on |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 01 export | `tlp_01_export` | single, host R | 64 G | — | 6 h | — |
| 02 build h5ad | `tlp_02_build_h5ad` | single | 64 G | — | 6 h | `tlp_01_export` |
| 03 sample table | `tlp_03_sample_table` | single | 32 G | — | 2 h | `tlp_02_build_h5ad` |
| 04 tokenise | `tlp_04_tokenise` | array, 38 tasks | 64 G | — | 6 h | `tlp_03_sample_table` |
| 05 null genes | `tlp_05_null_genes` | single | 16 G | — | 1 h | `tlp_04_tokenise` (all tasks) |
| 06 ko embed | `tlp_06_ko_embed` | array, 38 tasks, ≤8 concurrent | 32 G (+200 G host) | ≥40 GB card | 3 h | `tlp_05_null_genes` |
| 07 ko pool | `tlp_07_ko_pool` | single | 32 G | — | 24 h | `tlp_06_ko_embed` (all tasks) |

Sources: [scripts/01_export.sh](/scripts/01_export.sh#L2-L7), [scripts/02_build_h5ad.sh](/scripts/02_build_h5ad.sh#L2-L10), [scripts/03_sample_table.sh](/scripts/03_sample_table.sh#L2-L10), [scripts/04_tokenise.sh](/scripts/04_tokenise.sh#L2-L13), [scripts/05_null_genes.sh](/scripts/05_null_genes.sh#L2-L10), [scripts/06_ko_embed.sh](/scripts/06_ko_embed.sh#L2-L10), [scripts/07_ko_pool.sh](/scripts/07_ko_pool.sh#L2-L13)

The 200 GB host-memory request on step 06 is not the GPU memory — it is the host-side working set needed to load tokenised patients alongside the model. The GPU requirement itself is a hardware floor, not a scheduler attribute: the script requests only `gpu=true` (any card), and the README instructs you to restrict the queue or host list so the job lands on a card with at least 40 GB. The batch size of 256 is kept **fixed across all patients** precisely so every patient is embedded identically — lowering it to fit smaller cards would change the numerics of the comparison.

Sources: [scripts/06_ko_embed.sh](/scripts/06_ko_embed.sh#L6-L14), [README.md](/README.md#L220-L222)

## The Dependency Chain: `-hold_jid` by Job Name

Job chaining uses SGE's name-based hold: each submission names the **job name** (not the numeric job ID) of its predecessor, so submission order is free and the scheduler enforces ordering. A hold on an array job name releases only when *every* task of that array has finished — which is exactly the semantics steps 05 and 07 need, since they consume cohort-wide outputs of the preceding arrays. The full run is therefore seven `qsub` lines, each adding one `-hold_jid` link:

```bash
qsub -o logs/ scripts/01_export.sh
qsub -o logs/ -hold_jid tlp_01_export      scripts/02_build_h5ad.sh
qsub -o logs/ -hold_jid tlp_02_build_h5ad  scripts/03_sample_table.sh
qsub -o logs/ -hold_jid tlp_03_sample_table scripts/04_tokenise.sh   # array, 38 tasks
qsub -o logs/ -hold_jid tlp_04_tokenise    scripts/05_null_genes.sh
```

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L201-L209), [scripts/02_build_h5ad.sh](/scripts/02_build_h5ad.sh#L9-L10), [scripts/07_ko_pool.sh](/scripts/07_ko_pool.sh#L9-L13)

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["01_export<br/>tlp_01_export · host R"] -->|"hold_jid"| B["02_build_h5ad<br/>tlp_02_build_h5ad"]
    B -->|"hold_jid"| C["03_sample_table<br/>tlp_03_sample_table"]
    C -->|"hold_jid"| D["04_tokenise<br/>tlp_04_tokenise · array 1-38"]
    D -->|"hold_jid (all 38 tasks)"| E["05_null_genes<br/>tlp_05_null_genes"]
    E -->|"submit manually<br/>after smoke test"| F["06_ko_embed<br/>tlp_06_ko_embed · array 1-38 · ≤8 GPU concurrent"]
    F -->|"hold_jid (all 38 tasks)"| G["07_ko_pool<br/>tlp_07_ko_pool"]
```

Step 06 breaks the pure fire-and-forget pattern by design: it is expensive (38 GPU tasks) and is submitted only after a **single-patient smoke test**. You first run one task on the GPU, inspect its log, and only then submit the full array — the array re-detects the already-processed patient and skips it. Step 05's hold, by contrast, submits straight after step 04 because its inputs (the per-patient `cf_blocks.npz` files) are cheap to re-derive and the step itself runs in one hour.

```bash
qsub -o logs/ -t 1-1 -v PATIENT=P12 scripts/06_ko_embed.sh   # smoke test: one patient
qsub -o logs/ scripts/06_ko_embed.sh                         # full array (skips P12)
qsub -o logs/ -hold_jid tlp_06_ko_embed scripts/07_ko_pool.sh
```

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L211-L218), [scripts/06_ko_embed.sh](/scripts/06_ko_embed.sh#L12-L18), [scripts/06_ko_embed.py](/scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L47-L49)

> [!TIP]
> The `-hold_jid` targets are **string-matched against the `#$ -N` job names**, which are hardcoded in each wrapper. If you override a name on the `qsub` command line (e.g. `qsub -N my_04 ...`), a successor holding on `tlp_04_tokenise` will wait forever or fail against a name that never exists — keep the `tlp_*` names intact unless you retarget every downstream hold.

## Environment Bootstrap: What `source env/terra_env.sh` Actually Does

Every wrapper's first real action is sourcing the environment layer, which performs four operations in order. First, it derives `REPO_DIR` from its own location, so jobs work from any checkout path. Second, it loads `config/paths.cfg` with `set -a` (auto-exporting every variable) and **fails immediately with a named variable** if the file is missing or if any of `INPUT_DIR`, `WORK_DIR`, `RESULTS_DIR`, `SOFTWARE_DIR`, `BIND_PATHS` is unset — turning configuration errors into instant, readable job failures rather than mid-pipeline crashes. Third, it exports the container image path, the pinned model identity (`MODEL_REPO`, `MODEL_REVISION`, `MODEL_SHA256`), and builds `TERRA_CENV`, a single comma-separated `--env` payload that carries every path *into* the container. Fourth, it defines and exports the three functions the wrappers call: `tx`, `txg`, and `require_avx`.

Sources: [env/terra_env.sh](/env/terra_env.sh#L17-L46), [env/terra_env.sh](/env/terra_env.sh#L48-L69), [env/terra_env.sh](/env/terra_env.sh#L110)

The two runner functions are where the container boundary is negotiated, and both use `singularity exec --cleanenv` — the host environment is dropped entirely and replaced by an explicit, audited set of variables. `tx` binds `BIND_PATHS` and injects `TERRA_CENV`; `txg` additionally passes `--nv` for GPU access and sets `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1` / `TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1`, since the model is pre-downloaded and verified by `install.sh`. The scheduler handshake lives in `_terra_job_env`: SGE's slot count, array task ID, and the `PATIENT` override are re-exported as `SINGULARITYENV_*` variables because `--cleanenv` would otherwise erase them inside the container.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Host["Host (inside the job)"]
        CFG["config/paths.cfg"]
        TE["terra_env.sh"]
        SGE["SGE vars:<br/>NSLOTS · SGE_TASK_ID ·<br/>PATIENT · CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES"]
    end
    subgraph Container["Singularity container"]
        PY["python script"]
    end
    CFG -->|"set -a source,<br/>validated"| TE
    TE -->|"TERRA_CENV --env"| PY
    SGE -->|"SINGULARITYENV_* passthrough"| PY
    SGE -->|"CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES via SINGULARITYENV_CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES"| TXG["txg --nv"] --> PY
```

Sources: [env/terra_env.sh](/env/terra_env.sh#L56-L83), [env/terra_env.sh](/env/terra_env.sh#L85-L99), [env/install.sh](/env/install.sh#L58-L75)

> [!TIP]
> The GPU path in `txg` solves a subtle multi-tenant failure mode: SGE assigns a card by setting `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` on the host, and `--cleanenv` drops it — the container would then see every card on the node and grab card 0, **which may belong to another job**. Forwarding it as `SINGULARITYENV_CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` preserves the scheduler's assignment, including multi-card lists like `"4,5"` that the comma-separated `--env` string cannot carry. `txg` also refuses to run outside a GPU job, failing with a clear message if `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` is unset.

## Array Jobs and the Task-to-Patient Contract

Steps 04 and 06 request `-t 1-38`, one task per included patient, and both Python scripts implement the same deterministic contract: **task N processes the Nth patient of the sorted list of the 38 included patients** (P10, P23 and the four low-inclusion patients are excluded upstream in step 03). A `PATIENT` environment variable overrides the mapping — this is the mechanism behind the `-t 1-1 -v PATIENT=P12` smoke test. The `PATIENT` value reaches the Python process only because `terra_env.sh` forwards it as `SINGULARITYENV_PATIENT`; likewise, SGE slot counts become `SINGULARITYENV_NSLOTS`, which the scripts read as `NUM_WORKERS` / `NPROC` for intra-job parallelism, so scheduler slot requests directly control DataLoader and process threading.

| Variable | Set by | Forwarded as | Consumed by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SGE_TASK_ID` | SGE array scheduler | `SINGULARITYENV_SGE_TASK_ID` | 04, 06 → patient index |
| `PATIENT` | operator (`-v PATIENT=P12`) | `SINGULARITYENV_PATIENT` | 04, 06 → single-patient override |
| `NSLOTS` | SGE slot request | `SINGULARITYENV_NSLOTS`, `OMP_NUM_THREADS` | 04 (`NPROC`), 06 (`NUM_WORKERS`) |
| `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` | SGE GPU assignment | `SINGULARITYENV_CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` | 06 via `txg` |

Sources: [scripts/04_tokenise.py](/scripts/04_tokenise.py#L31-L36), [scripts/04_tokenise.py](/scripts/04_tokenise.py#L63-L66), [scripts/06_ko_embed.py](/scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L47-L49), [scripts/06_ko_embed.py](/scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L67-L69), [env/terra_env.sh](/env/terra_env.sh#L73-L78)

Both wrappers print the mapping context at startup — host, job ID, task ID, and the patient override — so a log line like `task: 17 patient override: none` is enough to reconstruct which patient produced any given log file. Step 06 additionally probes the assigned hardware with `nvidia-smi` before starting work, recording the card name and total memory in the log.

Sources: [scripts/04_tokenise.sh](/scripts/04_tokenise.sh#L19-L20), [scripts/06_ko_embed.sh](/scripts/06_ko_embed.sh#L24-L26)

## Resumability: What Reruns Skip and What Recomputes

The chain is built to be **re-runnable in place** rather than resubmitted from scratch. Steps 01, 02, 04 and 06 carry `FORCE_REBUILD = False` and skip any patient whose outputs already exist on disk; step 07 reuses cached per-donor predictions under the same flag. Steps 03 and 05 are cheap, cohort-wide decisions and always recompute. This has direct operational consequences: after a single array task crashes (say, task 22 of step 06 on an OOM), you resubmit the array and only the failed patients actually run; after editing step 07's analysis logic, resubmitting it is nearly free because the expensive embeddings from step 06 are untouched on disk.

| Step | On rerun | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| 01, 02 | Skips patients with existing outputs | Export/assembly is expensive and deterministic per patient |
| 03 | Always recomputes | Cohort-wide inclusion decision, cheap |
| 04 | Skips tokenised patients | Tokenisation is done exactly once per patient by design |
| 05 | Always recomputes | Null-gene draw is cheap; reruns reflect any step 04 changes |
| 06 | Skips embedded patients | Each GPU task costs ~21 GB and hours of compute |
| 07 | Reuses cached per-donor predictions | Classification is the analysis layer; embeddings are the data layer |

Sources: [scripts/04_tokenise.py](/scripts/04_tokenise.py#L44-L64), [scripts/06_ko_embed.py](/scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L47-L49), [README.md](/README.md#L179-L183)

Note the one asymmetry to plan around: steps 01 and 02 run *before* step 03's exclusion decision, exporting all 44 patients, while 04/06 arrays cover only the 38 included ones — a rerun of 01/02 reprocesses the full cohort. The full data-lineage between steps (which files each hold consumes) is documented in [Pipeline Architecture](5-pipeline-architecture), and the interaction of these skips with config changes is covered in [Reproducibility and Caching](19-reproducibility-and-caching).

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L48-L54), [scripts/04_tokenise.py](/scripts/04_tokenise.py#L31-L35)

## Monitoring and Failure Triage

Observability is built from three cheap mechanisms rather than a monitoring stack: `#$ -j y` gives every job exactly one log under `logs/`; each wrapper echoes `host / job / task / timestamp` at start (and most at end); and `set -euo pipefail` plus `require_avx` convert the two most common silent failure classes — a failed intermediate command, and an incompatible CPU node — into immediate, explicitly worded job exits. The AVX gate exists because the container's jaxlib (imported by TERRA) requires AVX; on a node lacking it, the job fails at startup with *"resubmit excluding this node"* instead of a deep import traceback.

| Symptom in `logs/` | Likely cause | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Job stuck in `qw` state, never starts | `-hold_jid` target name doesn't match any job | Check `qstat`; keep `tlp_*` names unchanged |
| `terra_env.sh: .../paths.cfg not found` | Config not created before submission | Copy and edit the `.cfg.example` files, resubmit |
| `terra_env.sh: WORK_DIR is not set` | Incomplete `paths.cfg` | Fill all five required paths |
| `txg: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES is not set` | Step 06 submitted without a GPU slot | Verify the queue/complex grants `gpu=true` |
| `ERROR: <host> has no AVX` | Old CPU node without AVX | Resubmit excluding that host |
| Task 06 fails on an ≥24 GB card | Card below the 40 GB floor at batch size 256 | Target an ≥40 GB queue; do not lower batch size |
| `the repository is not visible in the container` | Repo path missing from `BIND_PATHS` | Add it to `paths.cfg`, re-run `env/install.sh` checks |

Sources: [env/terra_env.sh](/env/terra_env.sh#L18-L33), [env/terra_env.sh](/env/terra_env.sh#L90-L94), [env/terra_env.sh](/env/terra_env.sh#L101-L108), [scripts/06_ko_embed.sh](/scripts/06_ko_embed.sh#L12-L14), [env/install.sh](/env/install.sh#L44-L45)

Before the first submission of any session, the README's setup sequence ends with `bash env/check_config.sh` (run once normally and once inside a GPU session), which validates configuration, software, inputs, and model presence — catching environment drift before it becomes a 38-task array failure. For what those checks verify and how caching interacts with reruns, continue to [Reproducibility and Caching](19-reproducibility-and-caching); for interpreting what the chained run ultimately produces, see [Outputs and Result Interpretation](20-outputs-and-result-interpretation).


# Reproducibility and Caching



This page explains how *terra-ligand-perturbation* makes its results traceable and its reruns cheap. The pipeline is a linear chain of seven steps (see [Pipeline Architecture](5-pipeline-architecture)) whose heaviest stages — tokenisation and GPU embedding — can take hours per patient, so the repository separates **what guarantees a result can be reproduced** (pinned versions, validated configuration, deterministic algorithms, provenance written into outputs) from **what makes a rerun fast** (three cache layers with different granularity and invalidation rules). Everything on this page concerns the mechanics of repetition and traceability; how to submit and chain the jobs on the cluster is covered in [Cluster Execution and Job Chaining](18-cluster-execution-and-job-chaining).

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L9-L14), [README.md](README.md#L179-L183)

## The Reproducibility Contract: Pinned Versions and Validated Configuration

Reproducibility in this repository rests on pinning the two things most likely to drift: the model and the analysis parameters. The analysis was developed and run with `terra-st` 0.1.13 and the TERRA-112M weights at Hugging Face revision `00d1c977`; the weights are downloaded once by the install script (not redistributed), and the README warns that later `terra-st` versions may change the interface and require adjustments. The recorded environment and pinned package list live in `env/versions/`, so the exact software stack of the original run can be inspected rather than guessed.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L9-L14), [README.md](README.md#L166-L168)

The second half of the contract is the two configuration files you create from the `config/*.cfg.example` templates (set up in [Configuration Setup](4-configuration-setup)). `paths.cfg` fixes the five absolute locations the whole pipeline shares — `INPUT_DIR`, `WORK_DIR`, `RESULTS_DIR`, `SOFTWARE_DIR`, and `BIND_PATHS` — and is verified by `env/check_config.sh`, which also confirms the software, input data and model are present before any job runs. `analysis.cfg` fixes the `SOURCE_STATES` and `TARGET_STATES` cell-state labels.

Sources: [config/paths.cfg.example](config/paths.cfg.example#L8-L24), [README.md](README.md#L187-L199)

Configuration is not merely read — it is **enforced at every point of use**. Steps 03, 04 and 07 import `analysis_config.load_states()`, which fails immediately if `config/analysis.cfg` is missing, if a required key is absent, if a value still contains a `<placeholder>`, or if `TARGET_STATES` lists the same state twice. The heavy scripts never fall back to defaults: each resolves its directories from environment variables (`WORK_DIR`, `RESULTS_DIR`, `MODEL_DIR`) exported by the shared `env/terra_env.sh`, and exits if they are unset. This fail-fast posture means a half-configured checkout cannot silently produce results under different parameters than the original run.

Sources: [scripts/analysis_config.py](scripts/analysis_config.py#L13-L34), [scripts/04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L44-L59)

| Configuration key | File | Role in reproducibility |
|---|---|---|
| `INPUT_DIR` | `paths.cfg` | Fixes the exact version of the distributed Xenium objects |
| `WORK_DIR` | `paths.cfg` | Single location for every intermediate and cache (several hundred GB) |
| `RESULTS_DIR` | `paths.cfg` | Fixed home of the per-step summary workbooks |
| `SOFTWARE_DIR` | `paths.cfg` | Container image, packages, model weights and caches |
| `BIND_PATHS` | `paths.cfg` | Container mounts, verified to cover the repo and all paths above |
| `SOURCE_STATES` / `TARGET_STATES` | `analysis.cfg` | The analysis definition; enters the step-07 settings signature |

Sources: [config/paths.cfg.example](config/paths.cfg.example#L8-L24), [config/analysis.cfg.example](config/analysis.cfg.example#L7-L12)

## Determinism by Construction: Tokenise Once, Edit Tokens, Seed the Draw

Beyond pinning versions, the pipeline removes three known sources of nondeterminism by design rather than by configuration. First, each patient is tokenised **exactly once** in step 04, and every knockout in step 06 is built by editing those baseline token sequences in place — deliberately avoiding re-tokenisation, which reshuffles genes tied in expression rank. This single-tokenisation rule means the perturbed and baseline inputs differ *only* at the edited positions, which is both a scientific requirement (see [Cell-and-Neighbour Tokenisation](9-cell-and-neighbour-tokenisation)) and a reproducibility guarantee: the same `tokens/` directory feeds every condition.

Sources: [scripts/04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L7-L11), [README.md](README.md#L69-L71)

Second, the GPU embedding step fixes `BATCH_SIZE = 256` as a constant, kept fixed explicitly "so that every patient is embedded identically" — batching is otherwise a silent source of variation across runs and hardware. Within step 06, the Hugging Face `datasets` `.map` call used to substitute edited tokens is invoked with `load_from_cache_file=False`, so the library's own automatic map-caching (which could silently reuse a stale transform) is disabled; the script manages its caching explicitly instead.

Sources: [scripts/06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L68), [scripts/06_ko_embed.sh](scripts/06_ko_embed.sh#L12-L14), [scripts/06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L180-L191)

Third, the one stochastic element of the analysis — drawing 20 rank-matched null genes from the candidate pool — is seeded with `np.random.default_rng(1234)`, with candidate rules (rank band 40, presence band 0.15, excluded-ligand list) fixed before any results were seen. The bands are *not* widened automatically if too few candidates exist; the script exits instead, preserving the pre-specified design. The seed, the bands and the candidate count are recorded in the output workbook, so the draw can be re-executed bit-for-bit.

Sources: [scripts/05_null_genes.py](scripts/05_null_genes.py#L12-L24), [scripts/05_null_genes.py](scripts/05_null_genes.py#L128-L130), [scripts/05_null_genes.py](scripts/05_null_genes.py#L137-L143)

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph P["Pinned inputs"]
        A["terra-st 0.1.13<br/>HF rev 00d1c977"]
        B["env/versions/<br/>pinned packages + recorded env"]
        C["config/paths.cfg<br/>config/analysis.cfg"]
    end
    subgraph D["Determinism mechanisms"]
        D1["Tokenise each patient ONCE (04)<br/>knockouts edit tokens in place (06)"]
        D2["BATCH_SIZE = 256 fixed"]
        D3["Null draw seeded: rng(1234)<br/>bands not auto-widened"]
        D4["HF map cache disabled:<br/>load_from_cache_file=False"]
    end
    subgraph T["Traceability"]
        T1["Model config checked vs 11x256 layout"]
        T2["Provenance sheets in every xlsx:<br/>parameters, checks, settings signature"]
    end
    A --> D1
    A --> T1
    C --> D3
    C --> T2
    D1 --> D4
    D2 --> T2
```

The diagram summarises how the three mechanisms connect: pinned inputs feed the determinism mechanisms, which in turn feed the provenance trail. Note that the model-config check in step 04 (verifying the `cell_graph` 11 × 256 layout against `model_config.yaml` before tokenising) belongs to traceability: it ensures the recorded outputs were produced under the layout the rest of the analysis assumes, as described in [Harmonisation and Model Bundles](10-harmonisation-and-model-bundles).

Sources: [scripts/04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L184-L192)

## Three Cache Layers

The caching system is deliberately layered, because different steps have different cost profiles. **Layer 1** is *existence-based patient-level skipping* in the expensive steps (01, 02, 04, 06): each script starts with a `FORCE_REBUILD = False` constant and checks whether the patient's outputs already exist, exiting immediately if so. The checks are conservative — step 04 requires **all four** outputs (`tokens/dataset_info.json`, `meta.npz`, `cf_blocks.npz`, and the summary xlsx) before skipping, and step 06 requires both `emb_ko.npz` and its xlsx. Steps 03 and 05 are quick and always recompute.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L179-L183), [scripts/04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L174-L179), [scripts/06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L219-L224)

**Layer 2** is the *signature-checked prediction cache* inside step 07, the only layer that validates content rather than existence. Before fitting, step 07 builds a `SETTINGS` dictionary — the donor list, classifier hyperparameters (`C`, `max_iter`, `tol`), the target states from `analysis.cfg`, the condition list, and the W2 distance parameters — and reduces it to an MD5 `SIG`. Per-donor classifier predictions are cached as `<WORK_DIR>/ko_pool_cache/<P>.npz` with the signature embedded inside; on rerun a cached donor is reused only if its stored `sig` equals the current one, otherwise it is reported as "cache stale (settings or cohort changed)" and refitted in place.

Sources: [scripts/07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L287-L293), [scripts/07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L355-L367)

**Layer 3** is *provenance written into the outputs themselves*. Every step records a `parameters` sheet: step 05 logs the seed, bands and candidate count; step 06 logs the patient, model path, batch size, GPU name and torch version alongside its structural `checks`, timing, and GPU-memory sheets; and step 07's settings sheet carries the full parameter documentation plus the `settings_signature`. Because the signature is a digest of the effective settings, any output can be matched to the run configuration that produced it without consulting job logs.

Sources: [scripts/05_null_genes.py](scripts/05_null_genes.py#L137-L143), [scripts/06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L334-L352), [scripts/07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L560-L579)

| Layer | Where | Granularity | Hit condition | Invalidation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Existence skip | Steps 01, 02, 04, 06 | Per patient | All designated output files exist | Manual (delete outputs, or set `FORCE_REBUILD = True`) |
| 2. Signature cache | Step 07 only | Per donor | Cache `.npz` exists **and** embedded `sig` matches current MD5 | Automatic (stale entries refit and overwritten) |
| 3. Provenance sheets | All steps' outputs | Per run / per patient | — (always written, never read back) | — |

Sources: [scripts/04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L64-L179), [scripts/07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L89-L96)

> [!TIP]
> The two layers behave oppositely on upstream edits: changing a setting that feeds the step-07 signature (e.g. `TARGET_STATES` in `analysis.cfg`) **automatically** invalidates the prediction cache, but editing upstream data (say, an input matrix for one patient) does **not** invalidate the existence-based caches of steps 04/06 — you must delete that patient's outputs in `WORK_DIR` yourself, or the skip guard will happily reuse them.

## What Gets Reused: A Rerun Walkthrough

Because the repository's skip guards are keyed on outputs rather than timestamps, a rerun after an interruption resumes exactly where it stopped. This is visible in the recommended workflow for the GPU array: submit one patient first (`-t 1-1 -v PATIENT=P12`), inspect its log, then submit the full 38-task array — the array tasks for already-finished patients exit at the skip guard within seconds. The same semantics make a crashed step 04 array safe to resubmit: only patients with genuinely missing outputs are recomputed.

Sources: [scripts/06_ko_embed.sh](scripts/06_ko_embed.sh#L15-L18), [README.md](README.md#L211-L218)

Step 07 adds a cohort-level consistency check on top of its cache: it requires exactly the expected 38 donors to be present, verifies every patient's `cond_names` match the first patient's, and exits otherwise — so a partially completed step 06 cannot produce a summary workbook over an unintended cohort subset. The following flowchart traces a step-07 rerun; the signature decision is the interesting branch.

Sources: [scripts/07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L165-L171), [scripts/07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L211-L215)

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    S(["Step 07 starts<br/>FORCE_REBUILD = False"]) --> G["Glob KO_DIR/*/emb_ko.npz<br/>require exactly 38 donors"]
    G -->|count mismatch| X1["sys.exit: cohort incomplete"]
    G --> OK["Build SETTINGS:<br/>donors, C, max_iter, tol,<br/>target states, conditions, W2 params"]
    OK --> SIG["SIG = md5(json(SETTINGS))"]
    SIG --> L{"Cache file exists<br/>and not FORCE_REBUILD?"}
    L -->|no| F["fit_predict(donor)"]
    L -->|yes| V{"stored sig == SIG?"}
    V -->|yes| H["Reuse cached npz<br/>'donor cached'"]
    V -->|no| F2["Refit and overwrite:<br/>'cache stale (settings or cohort changed)'"]
    F --> W["np.savez cache/<P>.npz<br/>with sig embedded"]
    F2 --> W
    H --> P["Pool, tests, workbook<br/>settings sheet records SIG"]
    W --> P
```

Sources: [scripts/07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L287-L367)

| Step | Outputs in `RESULTS_DIR/<step>/` | Large intermediates in `WORK_DIR` | Rerun behaviour |
|---|---|---|---|
| 01 export | per-step xlsx | per-patient exported matrices | skips finished patients |
| 02 build_h5ad | per-step xlsx | one `adata.h5ad` per patient | skips finished patients |
| 03 sample_table | per-step xlsx | — | always recomputes |
| 04 tokenise | `04_tokenise_<P>.xlsx` | `tokens/`, `meta.npz`, `cf_blocks.npz` | skips patient only when **all 4** outputs exist |
| 05 null_genes | `05_null_genes.xlsx` + `.tsv` | — | always recomputes (seeded, so identical) |
| 06 ko_embed | `06_ko_embed_<P>.xlsx` | `emb_ko.npz` per patient | skips patient when npz **and** xlsx exist |
| 07 ko_pool | `07_summary.xlsx`, `07_details.xlsx` | `ko_pool_cache/<P>.npz` | reuses donors whose `sig` matches; refits stale ones |

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L179-L183), [scripts/07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L69-L75)

## Changing Settings Without Corrupting the Record

The layering gives you a precise vocabulary for partial reruns. To refit the step-07 classifiers under new hyperparameters, edit the constants at the top of `07_ko_pool.py` (or `TARGET_STATES` in `analysis.cfg`) and rerun — the signature changes, every donor cache is marked stale, and each is refit and overwritten, with no manual deletion. To force a clean rebuild of the whole cohort, flip the `FORCE_REBUILD` constant at the top of the relevant script (`04_tokenise.py`, `06_ko_embed.py`, or `07_ko_pool.py`); this is why the flag is a conspicuous single line rather than a buried CLI option.

Sources: [scripts/07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L74-L96), [scripts/07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L355-L367)

> [!TIP]
> The settings signature deliberately includes the **donor list**, not just model hyperparameters. If step 06 has produced outputs for only 35 of 38 patients, those 35 cached predictions stay valid, and the remaining donors are simply fitted on the next run — the cache survives incomplete cohorts. But because the signature also embeds the condition list, a change to the knockout conditions defined upstream (step 06) would *not* be caught by the step-07 existence check on `emb_ko.npz`; step 06 outputs must be rebuilt manually in that case.

The final guard against silent inconsistency is structural rather than cache-related: step 06 runs a battery of per-condition checks (only edited cells change, nothing changes outside edited blocks, padding stays at block ends, `cell_emb` negative control is unchanged) and exits non-zero if any fail, and step 07 re-verifies each input file's shape and cross-references before pooling. A cached artifact that predates a bug fix therefore cannot flow into results unnoticed — it either fails a check on load or is overwritten by a refit. For how to read the resulting workbooks, continue to [Outputs and Result Interpretation](20-outputs-and-result-interpretation).


# Outputs and Result Interpretation



This page documents every artifact the pipeline produces and how to read them. The pipeline separates **intermediate data products** (large files in `WORK_DIR`) from **human-readable summaries** (unformatted `.xlsx` workbooks in `RESULTS_DIR/<step>/`). The decisive results live in two workbooks written by step 07, and the page focuses on their structure, the statistical definitions behind each column, and the control logic needed to interpret a result as evidence — or absence of evidence — for a CSF1-specific effect.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L140-L158), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L69-L79)

## The Output Landscape

Every step writes its summary into `RESULTS_DIR/<step>/`, while bulk intermediates (tokenised datasets, per-patient embedding arrays, the prediction cache) accumulate under `WORK_DIR`. Steps 01, 02, 04 and 06 skip patients whose outputs already exist, and step 07 reuses cached per-donor predictions unless the cohort or classifier settings changed. This means the `RESULTS_DIR` tree is the canonical place to inspect results, and `WORK_DIR` is an implementation detail you should rarely need to open.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L179-L183)

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph WORK_DIR["WORK_DIR (intermediates)"]
        NPZ["terra_ko/&lt;P&gt;/emb_ko.npz<br/>(per-patient embeddings)"]
        CACHE["ko_pool_cache/&lt;P&gt;.npz<br/>(cached predictions)"]
    end
    subgraph RESULTS_DIR["RESULTS_DIR (summaries)"]
        X06["06_ko_embed/<br/>06_ko_embed_&lt;P&gt;.xlsx"]
        SUM["07_ko_pool/<br/>07_summary.xlsx"]
        DET["07_ko_pool/<br/>07_details.xlsx"]
    end
    NPZ -->|step 07 loads + QC| CACHE
    NPZ --> X06
    NPZ --> SUM
    NPZ --> DET
```

The per-step summary inventory is deliberately uniform:

| Step | Artifact | Content |
|---|---|---|
| 03 | `03_sample_table/03_sample_table.xlsx` (+ `.csv`) | `per_patient` sheet with inclusion flags (`pass_depth`, `pass_csf1pos_fib`, `pass_target_mac`, `included`), `depth_batch`; `parameters` sheet with thresholds |
| 04 | `04_tokenise/04_tokenise_<P>.xlsx` | per-patient tokenisation summary |
| 05 | `05_null_genes/05_null_genes.xlsx` + `.tsv` | the 20 rank-matched null genes (the `.tsv` is consumed by step 06) |
| 06 | `06_ko_embed/06_ko_embed_<P>.xlsx` | per-patient checks, per-cell shifts, negative control, timing, GPU memory |
| 07 | `07_summary.xlsx`, `07_details.xlsx` | the final cohort-level results (detailed below) |

Sources: [03_sample_table.py](scripts/03_sample_table.py#L105-L118), [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L37-L42), [05_null_genes.py](scripts/05_null_genes.py#L28-L37), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L344-L352)

## Per-Patient Artifacts from Step 06

Each GPU array task writes one `emb_ko.npz` per patient under `WORK_DIR/terra_ko/<P>/` — this is the single input of step 07. It stores baseline embeddings for **all myeloid cells** (the classifier training set: `mye_cell_id`, `mye_state`, `base_mye_spatial`, `base_mye_neigh`), baseline and condition embeddings for the **target macrophages** (`t_*` keys; `cond_spatial` and `cond_neigh` shaped `n_cond × n_t × D`), the condition list (`CSF1_remove`, `CSF1_zero`, `POS_block`, 20 × `NULL_<gene>`), and `n_edit`, the per-cell count of edited neighbour blocks per condition. A separate `base_mye_cell` key and the `cell_emb` readout exist as a negative control, since a neighbourhood edit cannot change a cell's own embedding.

Sources: [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L319-L331), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L12-L25)

The human-readable companion, `06_ko_embed_<P>.xlsx`, contains six sheets: `parameters` (patient, depth batch, model, cell counts, GPU and torch version), `checks`, `negative_control_cell_emb` (`max_abs_diff_cell_emb` per condition), `per_cell` (one row per target macrophage with `shift_spatial_<cond>` and `shift_neigh_<cond>` cosine shifts plus `n_edit_<cond>`), `timing`, and `gpu_memory`. Before trusting any downstream result, verify the `checks` sheet: the run logs structural assertions — each condition changes exactly the cells with `n_edit > 0`, nothing changes outside the edited blocks, padding stays at block ends, and `cell_emb` is unchanged (< 1e-4) — and the script **exits with status 1 if any check fails**.

Sources: [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L303-L317), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L292-L300), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L353-L357)

> [!TIP]
> The `per_cell` sheet of `06_ko_embed_<P>.xlsx` is the only place where single-cell cosine shifts are exported; step 07 aggregates them as `mean_cos_shift` but never writes the per-cell values back out. If you need cell-level magnitudes for a specific donor, read them here.

## Cohort Results: `07_summary.xlsx`

Step 07 refuses to run unless it finds exactly 38 patient files and consistent condition names across patients, then writes two workbooks into `RESULTS_DIR/07_ko_pool/`. `07_summary.xlsx` holds three sheets: `summary` (one row per embedding × condition), `columns` (a data dictionary explaining every column), and `settings` (a key–value record of the run). The design intent is that the summary workbook alone answers "what happened", while `columns` and `settings` make it self-documenting.

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L166-L170), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L560-L588), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L590-L607)

The `summary` sheet, ordered `CSF1_remove`, `CSF1_zero`, `POS_block`, then the 20 nulls, carries these columns:

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `embedding` / `primary_embedding` | `spatial` (from `spatial_cell_emb`) or `neigh` (from `neighborhood_emb`); flag 1 marks the primary embedding |
| `condition` / `role` | condition name and its role: `test`, `null gene`, or `control` |
| `n_donors` | eligible donors with a value of `d` (≥ 20 targets edited by `CSF1_remove`) |
| `median_d` | median over donors of d = mean dP(condition) − median over the null genes of mean dP(null) |
| `n_d_negative` | donors with d < 0, i.e. shift away from the target states beyond the null median |
| `p_two_sided` | two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test of d = 0 across eligible donors |
| `cohort_median_mean_dP` / `rank_most_negative_of_21` | median of donor mean dP, and its rank among the 21 genes (CSF1 + 20 nulls; 1 = most negative) |
| `cohort_median_W2` / `W2_rank_largest_of_21` | median of TERRA's Wasserstein-2 distance, and rank (1 = largest); **magnitude only** |
| `median_heldout_AUC` | median over donors of the held-out AUC of the leave-one-donor-out classifier |

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L506-L532), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L533-L551)

## Deep Dive: `07_details.xlsx`

The details workbook has twelve sheets, all unformatted and machine-readable. The `settings` sheet doubles as a provenance record: script name, timestamp, donor counts, the full null-gene list, `MIN_EDITED`, plain-language definitions of `dP`, `cos_shift`, `d`, the donor test and gene rank, classifier hyperparameters, W2 parameters, and an MD5 **settings signature** of the run.

| Sheet | Content |
|---|---|
| `settings` | run provenance and definitions (incl. `settings_signature`) |
| `wilcoxon` | the two-sided signed-rank test of d = 0, overall and per depth batch (`all`, `deep`, `shallow`), with `n_donors`, `n_d_negative`, `median_d`, `mean_d`, `wilcoxon_V`, `p_two_sided` |
| `gene_rank` | cohort median of donor mean dP per condition with `rank_most_negative_of_21` and `n_donors_nonNA` |
| `donor_d` | per-donor d for every test/control condition, with `eligible`, `n_edited_CSF1_remove`, `median_null_mean_dP`, `n_null_used` |
| `donor_condition` | per-donor × condition summaries: `n_edited`, `mean_dP`, `median_dP`, `mean_cos_shift` |
| `strata_n_edited` | the same summaries stratified by edited neighbours (1, 2, 3+) |
| `by_target_state` | the same summaries per target macrophage state |
| `w2_donor` | raw W2 per donor × condition × embedding |
| `w2_vs_null` | `W2_condition` − `median_null_W2` per donor |
| `w2_rank` | cohort median W2 ranked among the 21 genes (1 = largest) |
| `classifier_auc` | held-out AUC per donor, with `n_heldout`, `n_heldout_pos`, `n_train`, `lbfgs_iter`, `hit_max_iter` |
| `input_qc` | per-patient structure checks of the step 06 files |

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L582-L588), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L560-L579)

The `input_qc` sheet deserves attention before any biological interpretation. Per patient it reports `n_myeloid`, `n_mac`, `n_target`, per-state target counts, `n_target_other_state` (targets outside the configured states — a warning is printed if any exist), `n_target_cf_nb_gt0`, `frac_nedit_CSF1_remove_eq_n_cf_nb` (consistency between edits and CSF1+ fibroblast neighbours), the maximum absolute difference between target and myeloid baseline embeddings, and embedding dimensionalities.

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L241-L254), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L274-L276)

> [!TIP]
> `hit_max_iter` in `classifier_auc` flags donors whose logistic regression did not converge within `LR_MAX_ITER = 5000`. A systematically high value across donors suggests the classifier readout itself is unstable and should temper any interpretation of `median_heldout_AUC`.

## How to Read the Primary Readout

The **primary readout** is the target classifier on the spatial embedding (`PRIMARY = ("target", "spatial")`). The classifier is a StandardScaler + L2 logistic regression (balanced class weights, C = 1.0) fitted leave-one-donor-out on baseline embeddings of all `mac-*` cells, so the model scoring a donor never saw that donor's cells; AUC is computed on that donor's held-out baseline cells (NA if one class is absent). For every edited target cell, dP = P(condition) − P(baseline).

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L120-L122), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L26-L33), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L308-L352)

Donor-level evidence is built in three strict stages. First, a donor is **eligible** only if `CSF1_remove` edits at least `MIN_EDITED = 20` target macrophages. Second, the per-donor effect size d subtracts the *median over the 20 null genes* of the donor mean dP — a null gene with no edited target cell in that donor contributes nothing to the median, and `n_null_used` records how many were used. Third, the two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test of d = 0 runs across eligible donors, repeated within each depth batch. Negative d means the knockout moves cells *away* from the target states beyond what matched null edits do.

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L425-L433), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L435-L473)

Crucially, **no automatic call is made** — the code computes statistics but leaves the judgement to you. The intended logic is comparative, per the repository's rationale: because any input change alters model output, the question is not "does removing CSF1 change the embedding?" but "does its effect exceed that of 20 genes matched for presence and rank in the same neighbour blocks?". A result is strongest when `CSF1_remove` shows both a significantly negative d and `rank_most_negative_of_21 = 1`, while the positive control behaves as expected; a small test-gene effect under a working positive control is then interpretable as a weak effect rather than a method failure.

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L53-L54), [README.md](README.md#L112-L128)

## Controls and Magnitude Readouts

Each control answers a distinct question, and all of them are visible as rows of the `summary` sheet:

| Row / readout | Question it answers | Expected behaviour if the pipeline is sound |
|---|---|---|
| `CSF1_zero` | Does the result depend on how gene loss is encoded (token removed vs value zeroed)? | Should qualitatively agree with `CSF1_remove` |
| `POS_block` (whole fibroblast block emptied) | Can the pipeline detect a real neighbourhood change at all? | Clear, large effect — the sanity floor |
| `NULL_<gene>` × 20 | Is the CSF1 effect larger than edits of comparable size at the same positions? | CSF1_remove should stand apart from their distribution (d, rank) |
| `cell_emb` max abs diff | Negative control: could the edit leak into the cell's own embedding? | < 1e-4 (enforced as a hard check in step 06) |
| `median_heldout_AUC` | Is P(target) meaningful at baseline, before any perturbation? | Well above 0.5; NA if a donor lacks one class |

Sources: [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L12-L27), [README.md](README.md#L85-L97), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L315-L317)

The magnitude readouts — per-cell cosine shift and TERRA's Sinkhorn Wasserstein-2 distance between baseline and perturbed embeddings of the edited cells per donor (p = 2, blur = 0.01, tensorized backend, L2-normalised rows, no subsampling) — are **descriptive only**: W2 cannot tell a shift toward the target states from one away from it, so it is never used as evidence of direction. It is reported raw (`w2_donor`), relative to the null median (`w2_vs_null`), and as the rank of `CSF1_remove`'s cohort median among the 21 genes where 1 = *largest* — note the deliberate contrast with the d-based rank, where 1 = *most negative*. Running step 07 requires the TERRA `perturb` extra (`geomloss`); the script aborts at start-up without it.

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L40-L51), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L114-L118), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L138-L142)

## Reproducibility of Results

The results you read are stamped for reproducibility in two places. Every `07_summary.xlsx`/`07_details.xlsx` embeds a `settings` sheet whose last entry is the MD5 **settings signature** — a hash of the donor list, classifier hyperparameters, condition names and W2 parameters. Step 07 caches per-donor predictions in `WORK_DIR/ko_pool_cache/<P>.npz` keyed by this signature: with `FORCE_REBUILD = False` (default), a cache hit reuses stored predictions, while a changed cohort or classifier setting marks the cache *stale* and refits — so an unchanged signature in a later workbook certifies an unchanged analysis definition. Additionally, step 06's `parameters` sheet records the exact model, GPU, torch version and null-gene list per patient.

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L287-L291), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L355-L367), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L566-L579), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L334-L341)

## Recommended Reading Order for a Result

A disciplined interpretation sequence mirrors the pipeline's dependency order: (1) `06_ko_embed_<P>.xlsx` `checks` — all pass?; (2) `input_qc` in `07_details.xlsx` — no targets outside configured states, embeddings the right dimensionality?; (3) `classifier_auc` — held-out AUC healthy and convergent?; (4) the primary row of `summary` (`spatial` × `CSF1_remove`) — sign of `median_d`, `p_two_sided`, `rank_most_negative_of_21`; (5) controls — `POS_block` detectable, `CSF1_zero` concordant, `cell_emb` flat; (6) only then, the descriptive `w2_rank` and stratified sheets. For a quick first pass, step 07 also prints one console line: `CSF1_remove, spatial embedding: median d = …, p (two-sided) = …, rank … of 21`.

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L552-L554), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L353-L357)

Interpretation must always be read against the framework's documented limits: TERRA is a zero-shot model not trained to predict perturbation responses, a ligand is represented only within a cell's 256 most-expressed genes, and the classifier readout depends on the dataset authors' label-transfer annotations. These caveats, and the planned generalisation of the readouts, are covered on the following pages.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L130-L138)

## Where to Go Next

This page closed the pipeline's arc from raw Xenium export to interpretable workbooks. To understand why these particular statistics — rather than a simple pre/post comparison — were chosen, see [Null-Gene Control Rationale](14-null-gene-control-rationale); for the mechanics of the classifier and the magnitude metrics, see [Leave-One-Donor-Out Classifier](15-leave-one-donor-out-classifier), [Embedding Shift Magnitudes](16-embedding-shift-magnitudes) and [Cohort Summary Statistics](17-cohort-summary-statistics); for how the cached predictions behind these workbooks are managed, see [Reproducibility and Caching](19-reproducibility-and-caching); and before drawing biological conclusions, read [Limitations and Caveats](21-limitations-and-caveats).

# Limitations and Caveats



This page is the honest ledger of the pipeline: a consolidated, code-verified inventory of what `terra-ligand-perturbation` can and cannot tell you. Version 0.1 is a packaged reproduction of a single-cohort analysis (CSF1 knockout around tumour macrophages in the Yan TNBC Xenium data, zero-shot with TERRA-112M), and most of its constraints follow directly from that scope. Each limitation below is traced to the file and lines where it is implemented or documented, so you can distinguish *inherent* method limits (which apply to any in-silico knockout of this kind) from *version-0.1 engineering constraints* (which the planned generalisation roadmap addresses).

## A Map of the Limitation Domains

The limitations are not independent facts — they cascade. A representational limit (what the model can see) shapes the edit semantics (how the knockout is applied), which shapes the control design (what a comparison means), which finally constrains statistical inference (what can be concluded). Reading them as a chain prevents the most common misinterpretation: treating a null result on the primary readout as evidence that the pipeline failed, rather than as one link in a chain of constraints.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph R["Representation limits"]
        VIS["256-token window per block:<br/>ligand visible only if highly expressed"]
        ZS["Zero-shot semantics:<br/>representation shift ≠ predicted response"]
    end
    subgraph E["Edit semantics"]
        LOC["Edits confined to CSF1+ fibroblast<br/>neighbour blocks (blocks 1..10)"]
        NRT["No re-tokenisation:<br/>no renormalisation of edited cells"]
    end
    subgraph C["Control design"]
        NUL["Nulls matched on presence and<br/>token rank only (single draw)"]
        POS["POS_block is an extreme,<br/>non-physiological edit"]
    end
    subgraph I["Statistical limits"]
        DON["Donor-level testing:<br/>n = 38, 12 deep / 26 shallow"]
        ELIG["MIN_EDITED = 20<br/>donor eligibility filter"]
        MAG["W2 and cosine are<br/>magnitude-only, descriptive"]
    end
    VIS --> LOC
    ZS --> MAG
    NRT --> NUL
    LOC --> DON
    NUL --> DON
    DON --> OUT["Interpretation must be<br/>comparative, not mechanistic"]
    ELIG --> OUT
    MAG --> OUT
    POS --> OUT
```

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L130-L138), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L53-L67)

## Representation Limits: What the Model Can See

TERRA-112M represents each cell as 11 blocks of 256 gene tokens — the cell itself plus its 10 nearest neighbours, each block listing genes in order of normalised expression. A ligand therefore exists for the model only if it falls within a block's 256 most highly expressed genes; anything below the cutoff is invisible, regardless of its biological importance. This is the first README-listed limitation ("Low-count transcripts"), and it is structural to the `cell_graph` layout rather than a bug.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L67-L71), [README.md](README.md#L130-L133), [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L26-L29)

Even for the intended target the visibility is partial. The null-selection step measured *CSF1* across the own 256-token blocks of all CSF1+ fibroblasts in the 38 included patients: presence 0.66 and median rank 60. In practice this means roughly a third of CSF1+ fibroblast neighbour blocks do not contain the CSF1 token at all, and a knockout of *CSF1* only changes blocks where the token is present — `n_edit` counts exactly those blocks per target cell. Cells whose edited-neighbour count is zero contribute nothing to any condition's statistics.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L93-L97), [05_null_genes.py](scripts/05_null_genes.py#L110-L114), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L24-L26)

Second, the semantics of the readout are zero-shot. TERRA was not trained to predict responses to perturbation; the pipeline measures how the model's *representation* of a macrophage moves when a ligand token disappears from its neighbourhood. A shift in that representation is not, and cannot be certified as, a predicted biological response. Any causal language about macrophage state change overreaches what this design licenses.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L134-L136)

## Edit Semantics: No Re-Tokenisation by Design

Every patient is tokenised once (step 04), and all 23 conditions are built by editing those frozen token sequences directly (step 06): the CSF1 token and its value are removed from the affected neighbour blocks, the remaining tokens of each block shift up with a stable sort so padding stays at the end, and nothing outside those blocks is touched. Two observed behaviours of `terra-st 0.1.13` motivated this design and are themselves caveats about the tooling:

* Setting *CSF1* counts to zero and **re-tokenising** changes the tokens of non-fibroblast cells beyond those whose CSF1+ fibroblast neighbour blocks contain *CSF1* — re-tokenisation re-normalises and re-ranks the edited fibroblasts and propagates the change to unintended blocks.
* The library's own `perturb_dataset` with `perturbation_target="neighborhood"` edited neighbour blocks belonging to unlisted cells, in addition to the intended edits. The pipeline therefore implements the knockout manually at token level.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L73-L83), [04_tokenise.py](scripts/04_tokenise.py#L8-L11), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L12-L17)

The cost of this choice is that the edit is **not renormalised**: removing CSF1 from a fibroblast's neighbour block does not re-rank the remaining 255 genes the way re-computing expression ranks would. The perturbation is therefore a token-deletion intervention, deliberately local, and its results should not be read as simulating the systemic consequences of ligand loss in a cell. The pipeline enforces and audits this locality: per-patient checks assert that changed cells are exactly the edited cells, that no position outside the edited blocks changes, that padding stays at block ends, and that the `cell_emb` readout (which cannot change under a neighbour-only edit) remains identical within 1e-4 across all conditions.

Sources: [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L12-L26), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L147-L177), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L285-L300), [06_ko_embed.py](scripts/06_ko_embed.py#L315-L317)

> [!TIP]
> The `cell_emb` negative control in each patient's step-06 checks sheet is the certification of edit locality. If a re-run shows a non-zero `max_abs_diff_cell_emb`, the frozen-token premise of the whole design has been violated upstream — stop interpreting downstream results and re-audit step 04.

## Control Design Caveats

The rank-matched null genes are the statistical backbone of the analysis, and their construction carries specific limits. Matching is defined on **presence** (fraction of CSF1+ fibroblast own-blocks containing the gene) and **median token rank** only — within ±0.15 and ±40 positions of CSF1's values. Genes with established direct effects on macrophages are excluded via a hand-curated list of ~50 ligands, so the null is free of *known strong* signal, but matching says nothing about functional similarity beyond visibility. Twenty genes are drawn once from the candidate pool with seed 1234; there is no resampling-based sensitivity analysis, and if fewer than 20 candidates exist the script exits rather than widening the bands — the bands are a pre-specified, non-negotiable design constant.

Sources: [05_null_genes.py](scripts/05_null_genes.py#L12-L24), [05_null_genes.py](scripts/05_null_genes.py#L57-L63), [05_null_genes.py](scripts/05_null_genes.py#L119-L131)

The positive and encoding controls also have asymmetric interpretations. `POS_block` empties an entire CSF1+ fibroblast neighbour block — as if that neighbour had no detected genes — which validates that the pipeline detects *large* neighbourhood changes but is a stronger, non-physiological edit than any gene-level knockout. `CSF1_zero` (value zeroed, token kept) versus `CSF1_remove` (token removed) tests whether results depend on how a loss is encoded in the token sequence. The methodological rationale is that changing *any* input changes a model's output, so magnitude alone cannot establish specificity: the test gene must exceed the effect of comparable edits at the same positions to claim a CSF1-specific signal.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L85-L91), [README.md](README.md#L112-L128)

## Statistical Inference Limits

The unit of inference is the **donor**, not the cell — per-cell dP values are summarised per donor precisely to avoid pseudoreplication, but this caps power at the cohort size. The donor-level test is a two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test of d = 0 (donor mean dP minus the null-gene median of donor mean dP), computed over all eligible donors and repeated within each depth batch. With 38 donors overall but a bimodal depth split of 12 deep and 26 shallow, the per-batch deep stratum has very little power, and the script reports NA rather than inventing a test when a stratum has fewer than one non-zero value.

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L53-L67), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L459-L473), [README.md](README.md#L56-L63)

Three further filters shape what reaches the primary summary. Donor eligibility requires at least `MIN_EDITED = 20` target macrophages edited by CSF1_remove; donors below the threshold are excluded from d, the Wilcoxon test, and the gene ranks (eligibility is recorded per row). A null gene with no edited target cell in a donor contributes nothing to that donor's null median, and `n_null_used` reports how many nulls actually entered each d. And because the classifier readout is trained on the dataset authors' label-transfer annotations of macrophage states, the entire primary readout inherits their label quality — the third README-listed limitation. Held-out AUC is reported per donor, but is NA whenever the held-out mac cells contain only one class.

Sources: [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L99-L106), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L429-L433), [07_ko_pool.py](scripts/07_ko_pool.py#L335-L345), [README.md](README.md#L137-L138)

Finally, the magnitude readouts are descriptive by construction.
